Katalog Berita (Halaman 42/57)

#3063. Vodafone (VOD) Q2 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

Germany restructuring weighed on results despite strong digital services growth.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Vodafone Group Public Limited Company (VOD -1.21%) reported accelerated service revenue growth of 6.4% in the second quarter and upgraded its full-year organic growth guidance for adjusted EBITDAaL and free cash flow. Management reported that the company is entering a new chapter focused on simplification and digital services expansion, supported by a 1 billion euro net cost-saving target by fiscal year 2030. The company completed strategic transactions to gain full ownership of its United Kingdom operations and increased its stake in Safaricom to strengthen its position in African fintech and connectivity markets. While growth accelerated in most segments, the company reported ongoing restructuring in Germany, including significant headcount reductions and an asset impairment driven by rising interest rates.

Margherita Della Valle: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Before moving to Q&A, I'll provide an update on the actions we are taking as we begin our new chapter as a simpler, stronger and growing business. We made a strong start to our new growth chapter with good financial performance, growing customer satisfaction and a fast start with our cost program that we announced in May. This underpins my confidence to upgrade our financial guidance for the year. As I mentioned, simpler, it's worth highlighting that we have continued to simplify our portfolio during the first half of the year, completing two important transactions in the U.K. and with Safaricom in Kenya.

In June, we announced that we increased our stake in Safaricom, strengthening our exposure to one of Africa's leading operators and our world-class financial services platform, M-Pesa. In July, we took full ownership of VodafoneThree in the U.K., giving us greater flexibility to move faster and capture 100% of the value created by the largest mobile operator and the fastest-growing broadband provider in the market. As you heard from us last month at our VodafoneThree investor briefing, we are already seeing the benefits of our 100% ownership reflected in our plans.

We raised our annual cost and CapEx synergy targets and provided a confident midterm outlook with operating cash flow in the U.K. expected to more than triple by FY '32. These transactions are a great example of how we are building a more focused Vodafone with even more exposure to attractive long-term growth opportunities. And that leads me on to talk about our good growth momentum and the strong start we have made in our multiyear growth outlook. I'm very happy with our overall group performance in the first half of FY '27 as we continue to see improvements across all group's key metrics.

Group service revenue growth accelerated to 6.4% in Q2, the highest in 3 years, with both Europe and Africa growing. We also delivered the best ever growth in Vodafone Business at 6.6%. This was supported by a record performance from our digital services portfolio as we continue to enhance our propositions with the smart, secure and sovereign solutions that our B2B and public sector customers need. In our emerging markets, once again, we reported double-digit organic growth in both Africa and Turkiye, which continues to translate into strong growth in euro terms. Growth in adjusted EBITDAaL for the group also accelerated to 6.4% in the first half, supported by strong top line growth and margin expansion.

And most importantly, we are on track to deliver very strong growth in adjusted free cash flow. And this is just the first year of our multiyear double-digit cash flow growth trajectory. Looking at our FY '27 outlook, we said in our Q1 update in July that we were tracking towards the upper end of the group guidance ranges. And this was after only 3 months of our financial year. I'm really pleased that with such a strong first half, I'm confident to upgrade our outlook. To translate what this means in percentage terms, the midpoint of our upgraded guidance range implies organic growth just above 20% in adjusted free cash flow.

Whilst I'm very happy with the group overall performance, I'm under no illusion that we still have much more to do in Germany. But if you look beyond the headlines, you can see that we have turned the corner in important parts of our business with consistent growth in consumer broadband and in B2B. We also see continued improvements in customer satisfaction across all our products. We continue to invest in our scale, mobile and fixed networks and simplify our customer journeys. We are also taking action to further step up our productivity in Germany with the next phase of our headcount reduction program. Yesterday, we announced 2,300 role reductions.

This means that we will have reduced headcount in Germany by 40% since we began our transformation. Looking now to the rest of the group, we have continued to make good progress in improving our customer experience, simplifying our business and driving sustainable growth. Starting with our #1 priority, our customers. We are improving customer experience by removing friction, resolving issues faster, often with the assistance of AI and offering new propositions such as SuperMobile in the U.K. And we can see it in our results. We hold leadership positions now in customer satisfaction in 12 of our markets. Sentiment within our customer base is improving across all our segments. And most importantly, our mobile customer loyalty continues to grow.

From a simplicity perspective, we have started the next phase of our cost transformation journey, building on a long track record of driving change inside Vodafone. As you will remember, in May, we announced that we will deliver over EUR 2 billion annual gross savings by FY '30 across Europe and our shared operations. This will translate into over EUR 1 billion in annual net OpEx savings. This is a comprehensive program. We will remove more than 30% of our addressable costs. We have made a fast start, delivering over EUR 200 million of gross savings in the first 6 months, supported by 3,000 role reductions as well as the first EUR 50 million synergies in the U.K.

We now have clear line of sight on a net reduction in OpEx of over EUR 200 million for the full year. The delivery of this program will have meaningful impact on our results. The net savings target is equivalent to more than 10% of our adjusted EBITDAaL in Europe, driving margin expansion in the years ahead. And that takes me to our third strategic pillar, growth. You heard me talk about Europe. We are taking structural actions in Germany, see unique opportunities in the U.K. and will deliver the next wave of productivity growth and margin expansion. There are two other important growth levers within our portfolio, Africa and B2B.

In Africa, the growth drivers remain attractive, growing customer base underpinned by population growth, increasing data usage, expanding next-generation connectivity and Africa's largest fintech platform with over 100 million users and millions of merchants. And in B2B, we are one of Europe's leading platforms for businesses with 5 million customers. We continue to gain share in growing markets as we expand our range of products and services, bringing the best of connectivity, but also cloud, security, AI and other digital solutions together to help businesses and the public sector accelerate their digital transformation and adoption of AI.

And with our sustained digital services growth, we now have a portfolio with revenue in excess of EUR 2 billion, meaning we have moved firmly beyond core connectivity into nonlinear growth opportunities such as cloud, IoT and security. Taking this all together through the continued execution of our strategic priorities of customer, simplicity and growth, we are well positioned for the future. Our growth will be driven by our strong market positions and the full breadth of opportunities across Europe, Africa and B2B. It is the strong foundations that underpin my confidence in our medium-term ambition to deliver double-digit organic growth in adjusted free cash flow.

This year, we have made a strong start, which enables us to upgrade our FY '27 group guidance. And just to recap, the midpoint of our new group ranges imply that our organic growth will be accelerating to 7% for adjusted EBITDAaL and 21% for adjusted free cash flow. And with that, Pilar and I are looking forward to your questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question today comes from Akhil Dattani at JPMorgan.

Akhil Dattani: I've got a question, Margherita, on the guidance upgrade that you talked us through just now. There's two quick parts to it. The first is that you were previously guiding to the upper end of your former ranges and the upper end of your former range is now the midpoint of your new ranges. So I guess I'd love to understand what the messaging is here. Is it optimism that it's the upper half of this range? And can you sort of talk us through specifically where the greater optimism is in the business as a whole? And the second piece of it is in the mix, you've left the European guidance unchanged. H1 EBITDAaL was down 1%.

The implied H2 is anywhere from minus 2% to plus 6%. So it's quite a big range implied for H2. Maybe you could help us understand what are the key swing factors for H2 that determine where you come out for Europe?

Margherita Della Valle: Thank you, Akhil. And maybe, Pilar, you can build on where is the optimism coming from?

Pilar Lopez: Thank you, Akhil. Thank you for the question. And I mean, as you rightly said, in July, we were already expecting to deliver at the upper end of the previous ranges. And since then, we've really seen a strong momentum in our execution. We've seen it in the U.K., which is performing strongly with top line delivery and the synergy delivery. We are seeing in Germany consistent growth in consumer broadband and in B2B. And this has allowed us to absorb the impact of the European Court of Justice ruling, remember earlier in the quarter, which has had an impact of EUR 100 million on our EBITDA, and that has allowed us to reconfirm the Europe outlook.

Beyond Europe, you've seen the strong performance in Africa and Turkey in the first half, and we are expecting that good growth to continue. And you've also seen the fast start we've made to the efficiency program overall. So with that, we now expect that acceleration in growth that Margherita was referring to. And at the midpoint of the guidance -- of the new guidance range, we are expecting to grow organically adjusted EBITDAal at 7% and adjusted free cash flow over 20%. You mentioned the European guidance. We are very confident at the midpoint of the guidance, where Europe is stable.

And in fact, we were able -- as I mentioned, we were able to stay in the outlook because the U.K. and Germany were performing better, and they allow us to -- again, as I said, to reconfirm and absorb the impact of the ECJ.

Margherita Della Valle: Maybe if I can build on that, Akhil, I think the key word for us is acceleration. In May, as a result of all the changes we have been driving and we are driving in the group, whether it's portfolio or whether it's investment on customer and simplicity, I talked about we are opening a new growth chapter. And by that, that's what we mean. We mean acceleration of growth. And this is where we see very much the 7% and the 20% or 21% that we are announcing today as a good first step, but the optimism is coming really from the midterm.

In May, we said we were expecting to have double-digit growth from now on in our organic cash flow generation. And again, this is the result of the changes. I will reiterate what I just said earlier, right? We have structural actions in Germany with progress quarter after quarter, unique opportunities in the U.K. We now have a cost reduction program that is worth net to the bottom line, 13% of European EBITDA. So a very nice push that makes us confident on Europe. And whether it's in Europe or beyond Europe, I think you will agree that now across our markets, we are in strong position.

I talked earlier around breadth of opportunities because wherever you look, you see reasons to expect growth in Europe, growth in Africa, growth in B2B. So pleased to have done a strong start. Guidance upgrade today, but our focus is all around acceleration for the midterm.

Operator: Our next question today comes from Carl Murdock-Smith from Citigroup.

Carl Murdock-Smith: I'd like to ask about Germany, please. You made the comment this morning that you have much more to do in Germany. You've had to make the noncash impairment to the German business today. You're facing the impact of the recent ECJ ruling that you've mentioned and Deutsche Telekom was making some positive comments last week about its ability to take further share in the MDU market as some access bottlenecks get resolved going forward. Can you expand a bit more on your earlier comments about what you're doing to turn the business around, but also to protect your MDU business in the face of potentially greater pressures going forward?

Margherita Della Valle: Thank you, Carl. Maybe one liner from Pilar on the accounting, and then I'll talk about the business.

Pilar Lopez: Yes. And I mean, you mentioned noncash. And as you know, we regularly review the carrying value of all of our assets. And now in the context of higher interest rates, the mechanics of the impairment, close to 3/4 of the charge have to do with higher government -- German government bond yields, and that impacts the discount rate. You've seen in the release the discount rate we are applying is 8% now versus 7.5% in the last disclosure. So really, the impairment has to do with the higher interest rates and the impact of the ECJ, as you mentioned in the introduction.

Margherita Della Valle: On Germany more broadly, I think beyond the headlines, you will see in all the data points that we are giving that quarter after quarter, we continue to see structural progress. And in the last year, this has been exemplified by the fact that we are now consistently growing in business and we are also consistently growing in consumer on the broadband part of our business. These for us were really important shifts. And as we just mentioned, actually, if it had not been for the ECJ ruling, Germany like the U.K. were both tracking ahead, which is why we have completely reconfirmed our European guidance for the year, absorbing EUR 100 million impact.

So we are taking the right actions for sustainable growth in what we said this previously is the largest market in Europe. We are operating at scale in both fixed and mobile, and we have a strong brand. Now you mentioned -- I said there is more to do, and I'm under no illusion. Our financial performance in the last few years in Germany has been disappointing. But we have not been sitting still. Step by step, we have continued to look resolutely on the midterm sustainable growth objective, which is why we have continued to invest on our long-term health of the business, and we have simplified our operations. The simplification is ongoing.

You know that in March, we completed the first wave of our headcount reductions in Germany and across Europe. In Germany, specifically, that first wave reduced the headcount by 20%. And now we have just announced yesterday another 2,300 headcount reductions. But the important point is that we are simplifying, we are getting leaner as we should. But at the same time, we have two, I would call them growth -- significant growth drivers that we are pushing in Germany. The first one is, as everywhere else, customer experience. You hear us saying and it may be a bit boring at this point, but quarter after quarter, our NPS, which we track obsessively across all our products continues to improve.

And this is because we are simplifying our journeys. We're investing in our network to become better and broader every single day. And the second growth driver is we can now say that we have developed real assets in Germany and more broadly on B2B digital services. You heard me in my introduction, I talked about cloud, I talked about AI, I talked about cybersecurity, all things that our customers are really demanding from us. And it's the investments we have done and we will continue to do in that space that have driven, for example, in Germany, 30% digital services growth in half 1.

So I stand by what I said, we are not yet where we need to be. I think this is clear. But again, as I said, I think we are building a very different Vodafone Germany, which is fit for the future.

Carl Murdock-Smith: And any comments on the point about MDU going forward and the ability to protect that?

Margherita Della Valle: Sure. We actually didn't see any significant movements in MDUs, but perhaps it's because the fiber penetration in MDUs and particularly in what I would call the cable MDUs, which are not all the MDUs of Germany, the fiber penetration is still very low. So we didn't see it. The impact on our net adds that we may want to talk about later is if we have negative net adds, it's gross adds. It's not coming from churn. And also when you look at the numbers we published, you will find that a disproportionately high amount of these negative net adds are in the DSL areas. So nothing to do with the cable MDUs.

Operator: Our next question today comes from Andrew Lee at Goldman Sachs.

Andrew Lee: Question on cost efficiencies for both of you. It seems you're more confident in achieving those cost efficiencies today than you were 6 months ago. So I just wanted to ask, is that simply just the pace of achieving cost efficiencies? Or have you gained in confidence in the scope to maybe even raise those ambitions at a gross and net basis? That's the question. And if you can give any color on what you're seeing that's giving you the confidence here, that would be helpful.

Margherita Della Valle: Sure. I was mulling Andrew, when you were asking me about cost because it reminded me of when we started working together, we at the beginning of the first wave a few years ago of our cost transformation programs. And now we are on wave 3. I would say Pilar can give us an update of what we see in terms of action, but -- we are just at the beginning of the wave 3, and we are effectively executing on what we presented to you in May, which is what we are very simply working on. And from this half year onwards, we will keep updating you on the progress. Pilar?

Pilar Lopez: No, definitely. And just maybe to put in context the targets we set, we committed in May, which Margherita had in her introduction, the over EUR 2 billion annual cost savings, this is effectively a 30% reduction of our addressable cost base across Europe and operations. And this will translate into over EUR 1 billion of net OpEx savings. We like to set net targets that we can track -- you can track on our EBITDA. And effectively, this is 13% of our Europe EBITDA. So that's just to put in context.

And then in terms of the confidence, well, it's the first 6 months, you've seen there is a fast start with EUR 200 million of gross savings delivered in this first half. Where are we delivering those savings? It's a combination of the U.K. synergies, EUR 50 million gross savings this half, simplification. And you've heard about the 3,000 role reduction in the first half after the 11,000 we reduced in the past and the announcement we made in Germany yesterday, another 2,300 over the next couple of years. There are a number of examples of how we are simplifying with our shared operations across the board. And then the third lever is AI.

And there it's great to see how the scaled platform that we have built is already delivering savings. And there are a number of areas where we are being pretty innovative. I mean you have some of the examples in the presentation, and those are already delivering real savings and contributing to the net target that we set. And I think what else to say there? Well, there are headwinds, and we also need to be very aware of those in terms of inflationary pressures on payroll, on energy, on the cost of the tower leases.

But despite the headwinds, we have made a fast start in the first half, and we will continue accelerating in the delivery, and we expect to deliver over EUR 200 million of net cost reduction already this fiscal. And as Margherita said, I mean, there is a long track record of delivering against targets. And as we have more visibility and progress on our delivery, we will update on progress, of course. And also, we will update on further opportunities as we've done in the past.

Margherita Della Valle: But the short summary is EUR 1 billion to the bottom line in Europe and roughly 1/4 of that will be delivered on the first year of the plan. So very sort of logical phasing.

Operator: Our next question today comes from Joshua Mills at BNP Paribas Exane.

Joshua Mills: I'm going to dig into Germany in a bit more detail. So firstly, on the service revenue trends, you talked about strong B2B growth. Could you just give us an update on what percentage of German service revenue is coming from B2B at the moment? And then within the mix, it looks like the digital services business has been a big driver of that. So perhaps you could give maybe a bit of flavor on whether it's much better digital service revenue growth that is driving this, whether the connectivity side of things has really changed as well. That would be the first question.

And then secondly, on competition, with results last week, I think DT were commenting a bit on mobile competition, and we've seen the launch of the new Simsalasim MVNO and also Revolut in the German mobile market. So are you seeing any change on mobile competition going forward?

Margherita Della Valle: Maybe in a nutshell, I start from the second part, which is not really. I would say we have seen a few moves in this quarter, some up, some down. Net-net, I think nothing is materially changing in the pricing environment in Germany. And all the MVNOs, you're talking about MVNOs are not new in any of our markets. And so I would say, generally speaking, very much more of the same. On B2B, turning around B2B was one of our key priorities in Germany. And as I was mentioning earlier, you see now the consistent growth. So maybe I can give you a bit more data points behind this.

In terms of sizing, roughly, roughly, IR can help with the precision, but imagine roughly 25% of the revenues in Germany from B2B and 25% or a little bit more of the B2B revenues coming from digital services. Now this last percentage is moving very fast. So we need to update it. But our strategy in Germany has really been to focus on gaining share on the new growth areas, cloud, AI, security. And we're also improving our connectivity, by the way, to your point, but all the growth, the real growth is coming from digital services. Three things have made a difference to us in the last year.

The first is we have -- you might have remembered me saying it for across the group, we have spent quite a bit of time and investment in expanding our portfolio in digital services. And so if I take the things that maybe are more relevant to Germany in the near term, just to give you a sense, we have launched an AI concierge service to support SME in driving their productivities. We are seeing a great success from our German cybersecurity operations center to serve our B2B customers. And then we have launched the sovereign AI proposition also in the last 6 months. Now this is, I would say, the organic side.

But second driver, we have also been investing inorganically. You might remember, we have acquired, maybe it's a year ago now, Skaylink, a company that is helping customers, particularly in the Mittelstand in Germany moving to the cloud. And again, if I look at, I don't know, the last 2 quarters, we have already signed over 100 contracts with Vodafone customers. So significant synergies. We bring together all our range of services. And last but not least, I would call out our team in Germany. It's fair to say that we have gone through, again, a lot of change, sale processes, effectiveness.

The team has been great at building a strong pipeline, and we see the momentum, and we will see the momentum continuing in the quarters to come. So expect this to be a good growth opportunity for us in Germany, absolutely one of our best growth opportunities ahead of us. By the way, I say Germany, not just in Germany.

Operator: Our next question this morning comes from David Wright at Bank of America Merrill Lynch.

David Wright: Yes, on Germany again, there's obviously been a lot of discussion around bringing the costs down. I wondered to what extent you think about bringing the CapEx down, decapitalizing the business and whether that could be more network sharing agreements, whether it be on the mobile side or even the fixed line side. Deutsche Tel, I think, indicated a potential willingness to share in fiber. Is that a route that you could pursue? And I say that within a sort of a general framework of cable infrastructure operators moving in that direction? And then just a super quick add-on Germany, which is just on the accounting side, maybe to confirm. You mentioned a provision taken against the ECJ ruling.

Is that a cash flow out item this fiscal year? And is that provision included in the cash flow guidance?

Margherita Della Valle: Thank you, David. Maybe, Pilar, you can take the provision.

Pilar Lopez: I mean we've taken a provision, a small provision related to the ongoing class action. We don't expect the class action to conclude at best at late calendar '27. So again, a small provision. And again, from a cash -- potential cash timing perspective, we don't expect the action to conclude again at best. late '27. So I hope that helps.

David Wright: So that's not in this year's cash flow guidance.

Margherita Della Valle: The process will last well into 2027, the court process. But we said it's small. It's worth saying that when you look at the EBITDA trends in half 1 in Germany, it's worth 2 percentage points, yes. So we have done minus 3.2% and minus 2% of that was this provision.

David Wright: Really sorry. So just to confirm, the EBITDA is adjusted for the EUR 100 million or so.

David Wright: But the cash flow guidance is only adjusted for the derecognition, which is more like EUR 60 million, EUR 65 million.

David Wright: And then on to the infra piece, Margherita.

Margherita Della Valle: On to the CapEx, I would say, David, I wouldn't guide to any material reduction of our capital intensity in Germany. And this is because -- if you think about you were going on our fixed line strategy, obviously, we will continue to invest on mobile, digital services and the like. But specifically, as a recap of our strategy in fixed in Germany, we have three pillars, as you know. One is continuing to invest in our cable network. And our cable network performance will continue to grow for years to come. Within our CapEx envelope, we are continuing to fiberize the cable network, and it's getting closer and closer to the buildings in Germany meter by meter.

On top of that, as you know, we reallocate frequencies and all the things that are strengthening the cable performance. We have just increased the uplink speeds, for example, for all our business customers in Germany. The cable road map has its own evolution, positive evolution. In parallel with that, we are building fiber within OXG. And this always happy to do in partnerships, as you have seen. We have now reached 1.1 million households. We expect to be at 1.4 million at the end of the fiscal year. We are probably the second biggest fiber builder in the country now. We are building across more than 75 cities. So this is progressing well.

And then last but not least, our objective in every market in Vodafone is to give to our customers the broadest possible choice in making sure they access gigabit products, which is why in the DSL areas, we are also wholesaling fiber in Germany where it's available. And therefore, that gives us the possibility to essentially sell gigabit speeds to more than 3/4 of German households, and we will continue to do so. Anyway, back to where we started, you should continue to expect the cable network to evolve, and you should continue to expect our portfolio of CapEx initiative in Germany to be broadly similar. We will continue to build fiber through partnerships.

Operator: Our next question today comes from James Ratzer at New Street Research.

James Ratzer: So, Margherita, I think my question really builds a bit more on the question from Andrew earlier around cost reduction. I don't want to kind of underestimate the difficulty in the kind of challenge you have in terms of the cost reduction and the magnitude of what you've announced. But it seems like since you announced it back in May, we've obviously had one very big change, which was that Xavier Niel announced that he is coming on to your shareholder register, and he has obviously a kind of very kind of strong and successful reputation on being very aggressive around cost reduction. So is presumably you've had preliminary discussions with him and his team.

Do you think your kind of EUR 2 billion target is you going absolutely flat out on cost reduction from here? I mean, is there any scope at all given the kind of maybe the fresh eyes his team might have bought your business that there can be any scope for that to be increased? And what can you say at this stage also about what we should expect around Board representation? I think the voting rights now are just a fraction below 20%. I mean if we use the Etisalat framework, that might allow in 1 Board seat. Is that what we should expect? Or do you think he could end up taking two Board seats?

Margherita Della Valle: James, on Vega, I think it's important to say that we never comment on engagement with individual shareholders. But in this particular case, the share transfer is still not approved. So the effects are not completed. There is a number of regulatory processes still open, particularly the NSIA process in the U.K. And this is about national security. I think Vega's expectations were for a conclusion of all these processes by the end of this calendar year, but that's not where we are. And it would really not be appropriate for me to comment or speculate on behalf of a future shareholder.

If I instead answer around our own plans, again, you have been with us for a long time, so you are familiar with all the cost transformation programs that we have also run in the past. I need to say there is one characteristic. You may have heard me say this before that I do care about when we announce cost transformation, which is to be able to commit to net OpEx reduction that effectively can be really directly visible in the P&L. I think you are used to that with us. And that's how -- as we started our new growth chapter in May, we shaped our forecast for the future.

As Pilar was saying earlier, this plan comes from if you want, the various opportunities that we have today as we update every 3 years or so into a new plan, and it's a combination of overall simplification continuing, U.K. synergies and the very significant contribution that AI is making into our operations. As we look at all this, we look at what's possible and we benchmark as much as we possibly can. We have just started. And so in terms of the future, as Pilar was mentioning, we will continue to update you, and we'll see what the opportunities are exactly as we used to do in previous occasions.

Operator: Our next question this morning comes from Robert Grindle from Deutsche Numis.

Robert Grindle: I'm going to follow up on the cost, I'm afraid. It's not about your cost out. It's about the cost of taking those costs out because you've had a fast start and you plan to do more in H2, including the German headcount reduction. But there doesn't seem to be any increase in the restructuring costs that you're talking about, the EUR 700 million or so. So were the German headcount reductions always in the plan for that? Or did you get better value elsewhere? Maybe it's AI, maybe you're just getting good at this. Some color there would be helpful.

Margherita Della Valle: The short answer, Rob, I will give it is that it was already in the plan. We announced these plans back in May. And by definition, the impact were included in our May guidance. So no change, no surprises. It's interesting how many questions on costs we get today, and we didn't get in May. We have probably a lot to say then.

Robert Grindle: Nevertheless, you seem to be going ahead of plan, whereas you're meeting your targets. So good going.

Operator: Our next question today comes from Polo Tang from UBS.

Polo Tang: I just have one question in terms of OXG. So you have a new partner for the fiber JV with SocGen replacing Altice in Germany. However, this means that Vodafone will now have to fund equity injections of up to EUR 1.2 billion. Can you clarify how these equity injections will be accounted for and will it impact adjusted free cash flow?

Margherita Della Valle: I think the situation is a little bit different. But let me tell you where we stand. So First of all, we have been pleased to welcome a new partner in OXG. SocGen knew OXG well because they were involved from the very start. And their presence essentially gives us an enhanced funding position together with full strategic flexibility as we look into the future. The governance of the JV is unchanged. The objectives of the JV are unchanged. Now SocGen comes in with different terms from Altice, and this is because we are at a different stage of the rollout.

They are a financial investor, not a strategic investor, but perhaps the most important point is we should face it. The conditions in the fiber market in Germany today are very different from where they were 4 years ago now. So that's where we are. In terms of funding and equity contribution, the funding of the JV will be a mix of debt and equity. And exactly what proportion, I think that also evolves over time, depending on the rollout, again, overall conditions and the strategy that the JV will want to adopt.

But from a Vodafone perspective, keep in mind that any equity that will come out from the mix of debt and equity will be very much phased over the duration of the build. And I think you have seen this very clearly in the last 2 to 3 years, we have built 1.1 million households and equity contributions from both partners have been very much phased. So they will continue to be phased, and we will see the impact as we go along.

Operator: We have time for one last question this morning, and this question comes from Emmet Kelly at Morgan Stanley.

Emmet Kelly: My question is on Africa, please. So you have been consolidating the extra 15% equity stake in Safaricom since the 1st of July. Obviously, the acquisition takes you to a majority, gives you consolidation of Kenya, Ethiopia and the tech business. However, I think most of us know that in September, Kenya's high court declared the 15% stake sale void. Might be a question maybe more for Vodacom, but I'd be keen to get your opinion on this. Can you give us an update on where we stand today and how this situation might evolve going forward? What's your expectation there?

Margherita Della Valle: Thank you, Emmet. Absolutely. I mean, consistently with our strategy, it was a very natural step for us to add this 15% stake into Safaricom that we have been working with for a very long time. as you know, leading telco, strong positions and strong growth opportunities also between connectivity and financial services. We have had local legal challenges in the Kenyan court, as you say, that process is now going through the appeals court. And the appeal has been fast tracked for urgent resolution. So we look forward to that. In the meantime, as we wait for the conclusion of the appeal, you will have seen the court has indicated that the status quo is maintained.

So we keep going and look forward to the conclusion of the legal process.

Operator: This concludes our Q&A session this morning. I'd now like to hand back to Margherita for any closing remarks.

Margherita Della Valle: Just want to say thank you for your time. Thank you for following us and looking forward to see you again when we have the results of our full year. Thank you.

#3061. The Future Of AI Is Too Important To Leave To Someone Else

Greg Salvato is CEO of TouchPoint One and founder of ApplicantPrime, advancing CX performance and career opportunity.

In October 2025, I wrote about why compassion must be a core leadership principle in the age of AI. As technology transforms how we work and live, our responsibility to one another becomes more important, not less. I’m now more convinced of this than ever. I’m also more concerned.

AI offers extraordinary opportunities to improve productivity, accelerate discovery, expand access to knowledge and solve previously intractable problems. I’m an enthusiastic participant in this transformation, but enthusiasm shouldn’t be confused with naivety, nor should technological advancement automatically be mistaken for human progress.

The greatest risk may not be what we don’t know about AI. It may be what we already know and our willingness to ignore it.

Commercial ambition and competition drove these technologies forward. Meanwhile, public trust, optimism, complacency, fear and a growing sense of powerlessness discouraged scrutiny or resistance. Some technologies even encourage the passive habits that make questioning their influence less likely.

The pattern is familiar. Innovation advances, benefits accumulate unevenly, consequences emerge and society struggles to respond. AI threatens to repeat that pattern at unprecedented speed and scale.

AI can help us learn, investigate complex problems, challenge assumptions and make better-informed decisions. The more capable it becomes, however, the more tempting it is to delegate not only our work but our judgment and, eventually, our sense of responsibility.

We can delegate tasks and execution to machines. We can’t delegate responsibility for the consequences, nor can we assign that responsibility exclusively to developers, executives or policymakers. Their obligations are substantial, but our collective future is too important to leave entirely in anyone else’s hands.

Corporate competition rewards speed, financial markets reward returns and political institutions face competing pressures. Even well-intentioned leaders can make individually rational decisions that produce collectively undesirable outcomes. Compassion alone won’t overcome these forces. It requires courage, independent judgment, discipline and collective action.

Frameworks for AI safety, ethics and governance already exist, but frameworks don’t implement themselves, and we can’t wait for someone else to deliver a perfect solution. I’ve developed a few practical principles to guide my own decisions and hold myself accountable. They require no special expertise, and I believe anyone can apply them.

Before adopting, deploying or endorsing AI, consider what it changes. Who benefits? Who bears the consequences? Who’s accountable? Technical expertise isn’t required to recognize foreseeable human consequences.

Don’t automatically accept assurances from technology providers, employers, governments or AI systems. Question assumptions, investigate incentives, seek competing perspectives and verify claims. AI itself is an extraordinary research and learning tool. Use it to strengthen your judgment, not replace it.

Start where you stand. Your profession, community and circumstances offer opportunities to make a difference. Choose an issue you understand or care about, define meaningful progress and act. Find others who share your concerns. Our individual influence varies, but collectively, it can be extraordinary.

When AI influences decisions affecting employment, healthcare, education, financial security or fundamental rights, identifiable people and institutions must remain responsible. Insist on transparency, meaningful oversight and mechanisms to challenge and correct harmful outcomes.

Good intentions and vigorous activity aren’t measures of success. Establish goals, evaluate outcomes, acknowledge failures and adjust course. Are our choices improving human opportunity, dignity, security and well-being? Apply the standards you demand of others to yourself.

Support credible research, responsible organizations and effective public oversight. Challenge practices that compromise human welfare. Hold institutions accountable and help improve the systems through which they’re governed. Responsible stewardship requires sustained participation, not occasional expressions of concern.

These principles are a foundation for shaping regulations, technical safeguards and institutional reform. Each carries an essential question: What am I prepared to do about it?

Individual acts of compassion matter enormously, but generosity alone can’t address disruption across entire industries. Compassion at scale means multiplying those efforts and ensuring human welfare influences our decisions, incentives and definitions of success. An organization using AI to improve productivity and profitability may accomplish something valuable. Whether it contributes to broader human progress is another question, and it’s one we have a responsibility to address.

I’m an eternal optimist. I believe AI can create extraordinary opportunity, prosperity, discovery and human flourishing. However, optimism is a belief in possibility, not a substitute for disciplined action and accountability. We’ve devoted extraordinary intelligence, capital, talent and rigor to developing AI. We must bring comparable commitment to managing its consequences and ensuring its benefits advance human welfare while respecting fundamental rights.

I previously argued that compassion must guide leadership in the AI age. That responsibility has never belonged exclusively to those with titles or authority. We are all leaders through our choices and influence.

We can’t control every consequence of AI, but neither are we powerless to shape its future. Each of us has a place to begin, a contribution to make and the opportunity to join others in pursuing something better. The responsibility is ours, individually and collectively, as is the extraordinary opportunity.​

#3060. On Holding (ONON) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Record sales and margins, with LightSpray demand outrunning production.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

On Holding AG (ONON -7.54%) reported record quarterly net sales and its highest underlying gross margin to date, attributing results to the execution of its premium strategy across all regions and product categories. Management noted that the company is currently in the initial phase of its largest innovation cycle, highlighted by the rollout of new supercritical foam technologies and the introduction of its LightSpray manufacturing process. The company is actively diversifying into new athletic categories, including football and golf, while expanding its retail footprint and digital engagement with younger consumer segments. Strategic investments in technology and infrastructure are intended to scale operations for long-term growth targets through the end of the decade.

Operator: Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us, and welcome to the On Holding AG Q3 2026 Results. [Operator Instructions] I will now hand the conference over to Liv Radlinger, Head of Investor Relations. Liv, please go ahead.

Liv Radlinger: Good afternoon, and good morning to our investor community. Thank you for joining On's third quarter earnings conference call and webcast. With me today on the call are Caspar Coppetti, Founder and Co-CEO; and Frank Sluis, CFO. David Allemann, Founder and Co-CEO, will join us for the Q&A session. Before we begin, I will briefly remind everyone that today's call will contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the federal securities laws. These forward-looking statements reflect our current expectations and beliefs only and are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

Please refer to our annual report on Form 20-F for the 2025 fiscal year filed with the SEC on 3rd March 2026 for a detailed discussion of such risks and uncertainties. We will further reference certain non-IFRS financial measures such as adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin. These measures are not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information presented in accordance with IFRS accounting standards. Please refer to today's release for a reconciliation to the most comparable IFRS measures. We will begin with Caspar, followed by Frank, leading through today's prepared remarks, after which we are looking forward to opening the call for the Q&A session.

With that, I'm very happy to turn the call over to Caspar.

Caspar Coppetti: Thank you, and a very warm welcome to everyone from Zurich. 7 weeks ago, we were thrilled to host so many of you here with us for our second Investor Day. You walked through our lab, our maker space and our foam competence center. You watched a LightSpray upper come together in minutes, saw the design-led vision that will take our apparel business to the next level and got a first look behind the curtain at our plans for new sports. No slide deck and no earnings call can ever bring On's culture of innovation to life quite like being here, and we are grateful to those of you who made the trip.

On that stage, we made a clear commitment for the next 3 years: to redefine what a sportswear brand can be by running the On Premium Playbook. We aim to grow faster than our industry and grow earnings even faster than sales, with the goal of making On the high-quality earnings compounder in our industry. Today, we report the first quarter of that plan, and we are thrilled with the progress that we are making. Net sales in the quarter grew close to 18% at constant currency to a record CHF 931 million, ahead of the latest expectation we provided you in September. And the first time, we have crossed CHF 900 million in a single quarter.

That is more than 4x the size of the quarter in which we went public 5 years ago. At the same time, our underlying gross margin and adjusted EBITDA margin reached the highest levels in our history. That is the On Premium Playbook doing exactly what it was built to do: growth and margin together, and, not or. We delivered these results in what remains a highly promotional environment by staying true to who we are. That means leading with innovation, design and resonant storytelling, giving our fans a unique offering that they do not find elsewhere. In a high-discount environment, there will always be some consumer choices based on price.

It has never been our strategy to go for these. And in such an environment, we are just as committed to premium as our highest principle. We are incredibly proud of what we have delivered this quarter, with our newest technologies and styles selling strongly at full price. This strategy is what allows us to reach record profitability while investing meaningfully in the 3 years ahead in the technology that will run On at the scale of our 2029 ambitions, and behind football and golf ahead of their launches next year. Much of that investment lands in the second half of this year, and it is exactly what sets us up to deliver 2027 and beyond.

Now let me show you how the On Premium Playbook came to life in Q3 through the 3 strategic growth engines we set out in Zurich: Performance, led by Run; Lifestyle, led by Sneaker; and Apparel, led by Her. In performance, we lead with run. And in this quarter, the biggest innovation cycle in our history got off to a flying start, proving once again that running remains our origin and our core. In Zurich, Scott told you about a day he and I spent in a run specialty store in the U.S., watching runners pick up our shoes and put them down again.

We brought what we saw home, put every function around it and built the shoe in record time, the first masterpiece of our new sensation-based franchise architecture, introducing On's breakthrough, SURREAL superfoam combined with a new CloudTec geometry. That shoe is the Cloudsurfer 3. And in October, it launched with select run specialty partners. The early signals are exceptional. In its first week, the Cloudsurfer 3 sold through at more than 4x the rate the Cloudsurfer 2 did in its launch week. It is already the #1 model with several of our key run specialty partners, and we are pleased to see their teams so invigorated by it, introducing it to their fans with fittings, group runs and in-store events.

This momentum is fully echoed by key run influencers and industry media, who have praised the shoe as a premium leap forward for everyday runners. But this is only the first shoe with our SURREAL superfoam. By the end of 2027, almost all our performance running franchises will run on one of our new supercritical foams. On's pinnacle product, the Cloudboom Strike 2, keeps showing the world what our innovation technology can do. Demand for the LightSpray version was 6x greater than what we could produce, selling out in our U.S. online store on launch day. Our athletes have carried it through the autumn season.

A double victory in the Frankfurt Marathon was followed by a milestone in the New York City Marathon, the first time On athletes reached the podium in both the men's and the women's race at the World Marathon Major. And in the Cloudmonster franchise, the Laced and LightSpray Hyper, the most advanced expressions, keep taking a larger share. Runners can feel the difference the technology makes for them, and they're choosing the very best of it. These successes and the generational updates coming to our core franchises through 2027 give us strong confidence in our ability to win meaningful share in premium running, a market that continues to grow faster than the industry around it.

In lifestyle, we lead with sneaker. This quarter, the Cloudtilt was again one of the fastest-growing sneaker franchises in the whole industry. And every new expression is bringing in new fans. The Cloudtilt Arc launched in September and beat our plan in all 3 regions in its first days. In Asia Pacific, by more than 4x. In Europe, the Cloudtilt is fast becoming a Gen Z staple, taking significant share with this important consumer. But the story is much bigger than one franchise. The Cloud, which also featured in our football edits, continues to show strong momentum, a true evergreen product and icon franchise.

By seamlessly connecting this classic silhouette with our high-profile entry into football, we are driving significant cross-category brand heat and introducing our performance heritage to a whole new generation of lifestyle consumers. In October, 2 new silhouettes joined the lineup: the Cloudnova Moon Mary Jane created with Zendaya, and already trading well above retail on resale platforms, and the sleek lower profile Cloudmuse, which has beaten our forecast since launch. Next year comes the Cloudswift 5, our first sneaker designed from street codes up. The Cloudtilt was just the start. In apparel, we lead with her.

Apparel grew 38% at a constant currency, and we are on track with our goal to triple net sales over the next 3 years while extending our share of wallet with existing customers. Winning with her is a long game, and this quarter showed exactly how we will win it, product designed for her in environments built around her. On the training floor, we launched new Train Tights in FormTec, a fabric developed to sculpt and shape, and backed them with our women's training campaign and women's share of our train collection rose meaningfully. Then in October came our latest collection with Zendaya, a bold design statement in python prints.

And the most visible apparel moment in our history, a reach of 2.5 billion, close to 90% positive sentiment, and top styles selling out across markets within days. Retail continues to be the engine that drives our apparel ambition. In our new generation fleet, apparel share is already at least 50% higher than in our existing stores. And apparel productivity is growing faster than footwear across the whole estate, a strong validator as we look to more than double our store apparel productivity over the 3-year horizon, per product, per moments, per store. It is early, but it is working.

Beyond our 3 strategic growth engines, we showed you in Zurich how we are building for the decades to come with new sports. We're only weeks into that journey, but the early signals from football have been remarkable. Our announcement post became the most seen story in On's history. And in the days that followed, e-commerce sales of our campaign products more than tripled in France and more than doubled in Germany and Spain. That is the halo before we have launched a single boot. Golf follows in the first half of next year, and we will build both sports deliberately. We are thrilled with everything we have seen so far and even more excited about what lies ahead.

The On Premium Playbook everywhere. That conviction ran through every channel and every region this quarter. In the Americas, the work we did with our wholesale partners over the summer, enhanced storytelling, more tech rep education, more shop-in-shops, paid off. Sell-outs strongly improved from the second quarter. Our partners' inventory is healthy, and the Cloudsurfer 3 has landed successfully into exactly the market we wanted. In Asia Pacific, we are building a brand that not only lasts, but is loved. That means expanding deliberately and elevating as we go, upgrading select locations, opening in some of the most in-demand premium mall locations and adding incredible new stores in the region's greatest cities.

It means the same discipline in every channel and every market. And it means engaging our fans even more directly through more than 1,000 street events a year. Japan shows how powerful that combination can be. In one of the world's most premium and culturally influential markets, demand for On continues to outpace supply. When our latest drop with Kith landed in September, it sold out almost immediately. The very next morning, we took it to the streets of Shibuya with a community run that reached well over 1 million people organically. Every decision we make is the On Premium Playbook in action, market-leading growth at remarkably strong margins.

That margin funds investment into the superfoam, the robots, the stores and the athletes that create the next wave of demand, enabling us to keep growing at pace from a bigger base. The margin funds the innovation, the innovation earns the margin, and the loop turns again. As we said at the Investor Day, simple in principle, demanding in practice. Powerful, because it compounds. 7 weeks into the plan, it is already compounding. Frank, please take us through the numbers.

Frank Sluis: Thank you, Caspar, and good afternoon, good morning, everyone. This is the first quarter of the plan we set out at our Investor Day and embodies the On Premium Playbook that we showed you there, growth and margin together. Net sales of CHF 931.4 million, a new record. A gross margin of 66.9%, excluding tariff refunds, the highest in our history. And cash of CHF 1.34 billion, up more than CHF 300 million since the start of the year. I am very pleased to walk you through the results in more detail. Net sales grew 17.8% at constant currency and 17.2% reported, and every region, every channel and every category contributed meaningfully.

Wholesale grew 13.2% at constant currency and 12.2% reported to CHF 538.2 million, and this is where much of the work we did with our partners over the summer showed up. Sell-out stepped up from the second quarter, including a strong back-to-school campaign led by our new exciting launches. In addition, several key accounts in the Americas took holiday deliveries in the final week of September that had been planned for October, business that would otherwise have landed in the fourth quarter. Through all of it, we kept sell-in disciplined exactly as we said we would, and our partners are heading into the holiday season with healthy inventory levels. They can also see what is coming.

The spring '27 order book has built well, and our partners are backing our innovation pipeline with real conviction. Direct-to-consumer grew 24.8% at constant currency and 25.0% reported to CHF 393.3 million, almost twice the rate of wholesale, and another exceptional quarter. Our DTC share reached 42.2%, up 2.6 percentage points year-over-year. You know we always set an extremely high bar for ourselves. And this quarter, we landed slightly below it. Throughout our markets, we held full price discipline despite online traffic being a little softer in a promotional environment. And a few new stores, Munich and Miami among them, now open in the fourth quarter rather than the third.

With this in mind, we are very pleased with how our strategy is driving strong, high-quality growth. The share of our online customers under 24 almost doubled year-on-year, with strong increases among both men and women. In a quarter when the market around us was promotional, the youngest, most culturally influential consumers came to On, while our full price share and resulting gross margin remained market-leading, and that is the next generation of fans arriving on our terms. In retail, we opened some spectacular new stores across the globe, from Copenhagen to San Francisco.

Productivity rose again, strongly led by apparel, and the store initiatives we told you about at the Investor Day drove another increase in customer satisfaction across the fleet. Turning to our regions. The Americas grew 12.4% at constant currency and reported rates to CHF 490.1 million. In North America, growth accelerated from the second quarter. We grew shelf space with our key partners and won younger consumers through back-to-school. We held our position as the brand with the highest ASP and lowest discount rate in the industry, a direct reflection of the strength of our strategy and execution.

Our key accounts grew both in their existing doors and through new ones, and there is a great deal of runway left in both. Further south, Brazil is becoming one of the most exciting stories in the region. The 2 stores we opened in Sao Paulo this quarter traded at more than double our forecast. And when the LOEWE Cloudtilt Cosmic launched in October, Sao Paulo was the second largest city in the world for it. EMEA grew 19.1% at constant currency and 17.9% reported, and passed CHF 0.25 billion in a single quarter for the first time in our history. We still sometimes read EMEA described as a mature region. Look at this quarter.

Every subregion grew, and Southern Europe and the Middle East, in particular, ran well ahead of our expectations. Our Paris, Madrid and Milan stores now trade consistently in our global top 10 alongside our London flagship. This is a region with a lot of potential for growth. And as we set out in September, the runway ahead is long. Asia Pacific grew 31.9% at constant currency and 31.1% reported to CHF 189.9 million. This is the deliberate, controlled pace at which we are building Asia Pacific, expanding and elevating at the same time. This includes being even more selective about how we show up with our partners in the most premium way.

That is why over the coming quarters, we expect growth closer to the mid- to high 20s corridor we set out for the region through 2029 than in the past 2 years. And you can already see the brand we are building. In Japan, our key partners came back to us for significantly more product through the quarter on the back of strong sell-out, with reorders well ahead of what we had planned. And both our Tokyo stores delivered exceptional results. In Korea, every store beat our expectation by at least 30%.

And in Sydney, we opened our first store at Bondi Junction, the epicenter of Australia's activewear movement, in an apparel-first format, and apparel took almost 30% of the sales in its opening weeks. Turning to our categories. Shoes grew 16%; apparel, 38%; and accessories, 40.2%. Apparel and accessories together now make up more than 9% of sales. Caspar told you the run and the sneaker stories. I want to add training, because it is one of the best examples of how authentically this brand can expand. Three years ago, training barely existed for us. This quarter, the Cloud X became our fourth largest footwear franchise, driven by the Cloud X 5 and the Tempo, and the momentum carried into apparel.

Training apparel grew particularly strongly in the U.S., and the share of new apparel customers who found us through training nearly doubled quarter-on-quarter. Training is one of the fastest-growing sports in the world, and we have only just started. Moving down the P&L. Gross margin, excluding the tariff refund, was 66.9%, the highest in our history. Including CHF 52.6 million of U.S. tariff refunds, as we flagged in September, reported gross margin was 72.6%. Last year's third quarter included a onetime adjustment of roughly 200 basis points related to lower anticipated freight and other costs. So on a like-for-like basis, this is an exceptional underlying expansion of 320 basis points.

This is first and foremost the underlying strength of our business model as well as a modest FX tailwind. We would be proud of that margin in any quarter, but especially in such an environment. At the Investor Day, I told you that premium is not the objective in our model. It is the mechanism. This quarter showed what that means. Our margin is the output of the Premium Playbook, innovation that consumers choose at full price, athletes who prove it on the world's biggest stages and experiences in our own channels that On can deliver. Execute each of those steps, and the margin follows.

Full price discipline led by our newest technologies, the sourcing and manufacturing efficiencies that come with strong execution, and a scale and a higher DTC share. And that margin gives us the strength to invest in our future. SG&A, excluding share-based compensation, rose 270 basis points as a percentage of sales, and underlying adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 130 basis points to a record 21.9% when excluding one-off tariff and freight items mentioned earlier. Every part of that investment maps back to our 3-year plan. Selling expenses grew with our store estate, and that is largely a mix effect.

As more of our sales come through our own stores, we earn a higher gross margin and carry higher selling costs at the same time. The net effect is clearly positive. As we showed you in Zurich, retail profitability, including those costs, sits comfortably above the group margin. G&A reflects our investment in technology and expertise, the capabilities to run On at the scale of our 2029 plan. We are building the single customer view and the omnichannel capabilities Alice described at the Investor Day, and we are embedding AI deeply into how we work. That build continues in the fourth quarter. Marketing was 12.1% of sales, a bit below the run rate for this year and reflecting phasing.

Some production costs associated with our football launch, along with a number of grassroots events and partnerships, are landing in the fourth quarter. Put together, 2026 carries the upfront investment in our new sports and our technology foundations, and the material SG&A leverage in our plan builds from 2027. Turning to the balance sheet. I already mentioned our exceptional record cash position. Inventory increased to CHF 495.7 million, up 30.2% year-over-year. Within this, volumes were up just 16%, below our sales growth and a step down from the 20% to 25% growth in recent quarters. The difference is largely currency translation at period end after the U.S. dollar strengthened in September.

We are well positioned for the holiday season and for the Cloudsurfer 3 rollout in January, and weeks of supply in our partners' inventory are healthy. Before I turn to the outlook, one more thank you to all of you who joined us in Zurich and to the On team who made it happen. Two days is a lot to ask of anyone's time, and we are very appreciative. The Investor Day was the result of a massive team effort, and it is the same team with the same spirit of collaboration that will now deliver the plan we set out there. Looking ahead, the fourth quarter has already brought some of our biggest brand moments of the year.

Our latest collaborations with LOEWE and Sky High Farm, our first capsule with Burna Boy, and our athletes on the podium from Frankfurt to New York and Beijing to Kona. The openings of Miami and L.A. stores have drawn huge crowds and stellar demand. We are reiterating our outlook for full year net sales growth in the low 20s at constant currency. We are planning for growth to accelerate in the fourth quarter, with our holiday campaign now live and the biggest innovation cycle in our history gathering pace. And we will run the holiday season the way we have run the whole year. In an expected promotional environment, we will stay true to who we are.

We're excited for the important weeks ahead. The On Premium Playbook is our standard, and we will always choose the long-term health of our brand. On gross margin, we are raising our outlook from at least 65% to around 66%, excluding tariff refunds, reflecting our full price commitment, our higher DTC share and the efficiencies that come with scale. We will keep investing meaningfully into technology, innovation and marketing to support the many opportunities we see ahead of us, and we expect an adjusted EBITDA margin in the range of 19.5% to 20%, again, excluding tariff refunds. Including tariff refunds, we expect a gross margin of around 67.5% and an adjusted EBITDA margin in the range of 21% to 21.5%.

Let me close where I closed at the Investor Day. On is a high-quality earnings compounder. This was a quarter in which much of our industry traded price for volume. We did the opposite and delivered record sales, our highest underlying margins and strong cash generation while doing it. In Zurich, growth and margin, and, not or, was something we said on stage. Today, you can see it in our results. Our biggest product cycle has begun to land. We are investing to scale it, and we are even more excited about this plan today than on the day we presented it. Thank you. Now Caspar, David and I look forward to your questions.

Operator: For the Q&A, David and Frank are joined by Caspar Coppetti, Founder and Co-CEO. [Operator Instructions] Your first question comes from the line of Laurent Vasilescu with BNP Paribas.

Laurent Vasilescu: I wanted to follow up, Frank. Thank you very much for the color on Asia Pacific. I think you called out that Asia Pacific should grow in the mid- to high 20s corridor. I'm curious to know what you're seeing in -- I know you called out Japan as very strong, but curious to know what you're seeing broadly across Asia, China. And then what does that imply -- if you could, what does it imply for the fourth quarter for the other 2 regions as we kind of look for acceleration in the fourth quarter?

Caspar Coppetti: Laurent, this is Caspar. Allow me to take the first part of your question before I hand over to Frank. As you're aware, we're running the On Premium Playbook across all our regions. Now if I had to pick one region where that playbook is almost like a match made in heaven, it is Asia with its aspirational consumer, its brand-savvy consumer. At the same time, Asia Pacific is our youngest region. So there's a lot more demand than we can actually, at the moment, fulfill. And I'll give you a bit of color around that. Take South Korea, for example, and we see a booming economy there. We currently have 3 stores, 3 On stores that we're operating there.

That is well, well beyond the potential that we have. We have a fourth coming online pretty soon, maybe Q4, maybe Q1. But that's just one example. I spoke to this in the prepared remarks. In Japan, we have seen a tremendous demand, especially also for our running products. So in Japan wholesale, say, the Alpen Group, we're now the #1 running brand. When we look into China, and you look at where our own stores and our partner store are, we're still focused on the Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities. So there's also a lot of untapped demand there.

As a matter of fact, a third-party study just showed that we've become now the #2 premium footwear brand in China. And so we are -- the consumers are really looking for what we have. So what you're seeing in the numbers is it's a really paced growth. We could go much faster, but we don't see a need for it. And of course, we're not willing to lean in, say, in a period like now, Double 11, when it's highly promotional, we're not necessarily want to waste our marketing dollars to spend against basically more promotions when we want to sell full price. And with that, I hand over to Frank for the bridge on the numbers.

Frank Sluis: Thanks, Laurent, for the question. Yes, as Caspar explained, we are, of course, really happy with the quarter 3 growth in APAC with 32%. It's been strong, right, on an ever-growing base. The mid- to high 20s refer to the Investor Day, the plan period '27 to '29. And in that sense, of course, we're not giving an outlook for quarter 4 per region. But I think it will gradually move as the base is growing in APAC, of course, like in any other region, we'll steadily get to that growth rate across the plan period, as we described in the Investor Day.

Laurent Vasilescu: Very helpful. And as my second follow-up question, I'd say it was very helpful, the Investor Day. I think you called out that you're currently at 60% of DICK'S Sporting Goods doors and 50% of Foot Locker and JD, with the ambition to get to 75% for 2029. I think you called out additional doors for this quarter. Curious to know, how do we think about this 75% target? Is it a steady progression over the next 3 years? Or is there a material step in next year as you continue to have strong orders from these key accounts?

Caspar Coppetti: Yes. Thanks. That's an excellent question. I mean, first off, I also want to share the good news that the strong progress in wholesale sell-out in the U.S. that we've seen and we've reported on in Investor Day, that has continued for the whole quarter. I think the numbers we outlined and that you just repeated reflect also the investments that especially DICK'S are making in upgrading their fleet. They're opening quite a large number of House of Sport stores. They're elevating some of their existing doors. And this means that we have a wider field to play with our On Premium Playbook, right?

So I don't look at this number as a fixed number, but more of a kind of like a well-aligned number with our key partners of what is the premium environment that they can provide to them.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Adrienne Yih with Barclays.

Adrienne Yih-Tennant: My first question is going to be on the LightSpray, obviously, technology. What have you learned from the early reads on it? And in the Analyst Day or the Investor Day, you had talked about a 10% penetration target, but it was unclear about when we would get to that, and how that changes the supply chain, the investments that you need to make over that horizon and how you might accelerate that to get to a higher number on a shorter time period?

Caspar Coppetti: Thank you so much for your question. We love talking about the innovation. Hey look, LightSpray is well on track. We just saw quite a big uplift in demand for LightSpray after the football announcement because, obviously, the technology that the football boot is based on is LightSpray. And so that actually translated over to LightSpray sales of our existing models, mostly the LightSpray Cloudmonster Hyper. Now unfortunately, production is still quite below demand, and we're ramping up production very quickly. So we have the 2 facilities, the one in Switzerland and the scaled factory in Korea. We're just about to bring online a factory in Vietnam.

And some of the football boots and most of the football boots will be made in Portugal. So by midyear next year, we'll have 4 LightSpray locations in production. What's very encouraging is to see as we scale this technology, that our margins are becoming very attractive. We -- one of the things that we have to manage, and as every manufacturer has to manage, is the defect rate, and we've made fantastic progress towards like a 5% defect rate, which is in line now with other technologies. And so I also want to give a shout out to the technical team on our end that has managed this in a very short period of time.

Now if you look a bit ahead, and that's to your 10% question, that is directional, whether we hit that by '29 or 2030 or '28, wouldn't go too deep. What you can expect though is that we're going to roll out LightSpray, not just to our performance franchise, but it will also start to show up in our lifestyle or sneaker franchises. And we have quite a deep pipeline of how the technology becomes more vivid, has more optionality, has more color options, and more texture and so on. And I would say, expect some of that to land in '28 where we will, for the first time, see the full potential of the technology.

Adrienne Yih-Tennant: Okay. Great. And my follow-up question is on AI and the investments that you're making there. There's some discussion about kind of a future world where Muse somewhat disintermediates some of the brands. And I'm just thinking about how are you kind of philosophically thinking about kind of maintaining that customer connection, the brand and the experience in order to kind of mitigate that risk?

David Allemann: Thank you for the question. When it comes to AI and changing consumer surface, you, of course, know that we have seen the whole transition from desktop to mobile to social. And so that's just the latest change of the surface. And we're very proactive about it. So a high percentage of our customer service conversations are already fully done with AI, that gives us a rich color on customers, and it's really a conversation.

And if you can imagine that this happens at scale, not just in customer service, but then also on the overall services that we give consumers through the website, through retail, through our app, that, of course, is an incredible potential to engage with customers at scale through AI. So we're definitely working on that. And you've probably seen that we've -- in a more tech-focused area of migrating completely from AWS to Google Cloud, that we used agentic to fully do that migration. Originally, the plan was to do that in 1.5 years. That whole process compressed down to 3 months just through agentic move from AWS to Google.

That's been one of the case studies at the recent Google at Work conference of a complex process that is made much more efficient through agents. And so if it can happen there, you can imagine what that means then for the consumer-facing technology.

Aneesha Sherman: I'm curious about the environment in the Americas. It's nice to see the stronger growth in that region. Caspar Coppetti: Thank you. I'm happy to take the first part of the question. I would say, especially in U.S. wholesale, it's pretty much the same story as in Q2 and Q3 in terms of promotional environment. We, of course, are a bit less affected by that. So we're leading with innovation and our stories, and we stay the course. So we're very much basically unaffected by that. We focus on what we can control, and that is trying to keep inventory levels and our supply in the right balance. Now in Q2, we spoke about that. We took measures to prepare for the upcoming generational shift in our running technologies. Some of that is now already in market.

What we're very encouraged by is that these signals are, of course, right now, Cloudsurfer is only available in run specialty. The strong sell-through signal has been noticed by our wholesale partners. So the bigger boxes, and they've actually increased their spring '27 orders on the back of that. So we remain very, very confident that we will gain share in performance running in '27. Frank Sluis: Thanks, Caspar. Yes, I think Aneesha, to give a bit more sort of color on the numbers. The meaningful step-up has been there in quarter 3, and including a tight control of the sell-in.

So we're positive on the inventory levels. If we look further to quarter 4, we will not, of course, guide specifically on the channels. But what we have said in the press release is that we expect an acceleration of quarter 4 growth versus quarter 3, and that will be predominantly DTC led. And that -- and the other point is on the wholesale, what we saw in quarter 3 was that -- what's something that we can't really control is that we had a bit of extra pickups from retailers, meaning that our growth, we said in the Investor Day, we would land at about 17%.

We were slightly ahead, which came predominantly from that, and that will have obviously a corresponding impact on quarter 4. But again, that's why I think when we look at quarter 4, we expect an acceleration, DTC-led. Yes.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Kelly Crago with BMO Capital Markets.

Kelly Crago: Great quarter. I just want to dig into the U.S. wholesale channel a bit more. First, on the run specialty channel, you had some good call-outs there around the Cloudsurfer 3. So just curious how that channel has been trending for you, how it's trending now and how you expect that to trend as we look ahead? And then I have one follow-up.

Caspar Coppetti: Thank you. Yes, the run specialty channel for us is something that's very close to our heart because that's where we started, and we still believe that's where our technology is validated. So what we've done now with Cloudsurfer 3, this shoe was heavily -- basically was developed with a lot of input from our run specialty partners, a lot of insights. We also have a panel of run specialty owners that test the product. So we said to honor that commitment that the channel has to On, the channel has access to it for the first 3 months exclusively, right? That is obviously something that not a lot of brands have done or ever done.

And so we're getting a lot of love back. So we're definitely seeing that in the pull rates, how often On gets pulled, how other silhouettes or franchises are being sold, and we're seeing it in the order rates going into '27. If you look back maybe 5 years back, and you look at pure market share in the channel, On's market share was maybe a bit higher than it was today, but it was a very different product mix. And so comfort is no longer part of run specialty.

In fact, we're not doing comfort at all. And so if you compare the numbers, that explains part of the difference. Right now, we're definitely seeing a very quick acceleration and a strong belief of the channel in us.
