You still had a follow-up?

Kelly Crago: Yes. Are you seeing shelf space gains based on sort of the market dynamics here? And how has that impacted your order books as we look to '27?

Caspar Coppetti: Yes, yes, absolutely. So again, the overall, the lifestyle market is down. We're very significantly up and so as a result, we've gained a lot of market share. And of course, that is reflected in the shelf space that we're getting. Our goal as On is to basically stand on several legs in that channel. Obviously, the Cloudtilt is an absolute blockbuster. In Europe, it's the #1 selling sneaker. In the U.S. and in Asia, it's in the top 3. What we're very encouraged by now in this Q3 is that we're starting other styles to be picked up heavily. First of all, the youth is discovering the Cloud, one of our original staples that's now 12 years old.

And they're almost like rediscovering it and giving it new meaning. So we've seen a lot of demand for that, especially in lighter colors. We also see, in addition to the high stack trend that we've seen for quite a long time now in the market, we're seeing a sleeker silhouette emerge, especially for the female customer. And we have just launched 2 styles that cater to that. The Cloudnova Moon Mary Jane that we launched with Zendaya and the Cloudmuse that we just launched, both are getting really, really good pickup rates. So this continues to be a good story for us.

And of course, as some of our competitors have not so strong innovation pipelines, also our key partners, so Foot Locker, JD, SNIPES over here in Europe, they are willing to trial things with us. And you can imagine if a consumer comes back into, say, a Foot Locker store, and they see a new style from On, it's a discovery process. And so that's how we're hoping to broaden our appeal with that consumer.

Are you seeing acceleration already quarter-to-date? And how should we think about that across the geographies? And just as a follow-up, you mentioned the factory in Vietnam for LightSpray coming online shortly, which is super interesting. And you talked about '26 capacity increase by, I think, a 30-fold. David Allemann: So Anna, thank you very much for your question. This is David. You're right. I mean, DTC grew 25%, almost twice as fast as wholesale, and gained 2.6 points of share year-over-year. And I feel very few brands in our industry are growing their own channels at that rate. And we did that, and I think that's important. We did that at full price, which is why our gross margin hit the record 66.9%. And we also achieved this despite high productivity flagship openings shifting into Q4, for example, Munich and Miami Aventura. So we had to offset that. The more interesting question I think that's where you're pointing to, is what is driving the growth?

We are putting even more energy into our DTC engine, younger customers, bigger baskets that mix footwear and apparel, and a stronger presence and preference for the brand through our retail stores, which, of course, is part of our long-term strategy. It follows our Premium Playbook, preference is earned and definitely is not bought, and that's also what you saw from us in the last quarters. If I can give you a few examples. So younger customers. Our online customers under 24, almost doubled year-over-year, and that's both men and women. There's bigger baskets, people who come to us through apparel come back sooner and buy more. So we're really kind of growing share of wallet as well.

And then just the sheer presence through retail, 10 new stores in Q3 from Copenhagen to San Francisco, Sao Paulo. So we spoke about that in the call. And then if you think about how this goes into the next year, we basically told you that in the Investor Day, that we're going to scale over the next 3 years to 180 doors roughly. So it's really an incredible energy and that also shows in our latest brand tracker that shows that nearly 1 in 3 heavy sneaker buyers says that they now prefer On.

The goal with LightSpray, of course, is to be closer to consumers with our manufacturing. So the things we have learned in Korea are now going to Vietnam, and these things can then go to other locations that are still to come.

Frank Sluis: Thanks, Alex. But I would not necessarily read it really as a trend, but a bit more as just probably fluctuations that you always see in a business, more than any of that.

Yes.

#3059. Prediction Markets Are Arriving in Your Investing App, and That Makes Us Nervous

NerdWallet, Inc. is an independent publisher and comparison service, not an investment advisor. Its articles, interactive tools and other content are provided to you for free, as self-help tools and for informational purposes only. They are not intended to provide investment advice. NerdWallet does not and cannot guarantee the accuracy or applicability of any information in regard to your individual circumstances. Examples are hypothetical, and we encourage you to seek personalized advice from qualified professionals regarding specific investment issues. Our estimates are based on past market performance, and past performance is not a guarantee of future performance.

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. And while our site doesn’t feature every company or financial product available on the market, we’re proud that the guidance we offer, the information we provide and the tools we create are objective, independent, straightforward — and free.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us. This may influence which products we review and write about (and where those products appear on the site), but it in no way affects our recommendations or advice, which are grounded in thousands of hours of research. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews of their products or services. Here is a list of our partners.

Prediction markets are booming, but that doesn’t make them a sound investment strategy.

The investing information provided on this page is for educational purposes only. NerdWallet, Inc. does not offer advisory or brokerage services, nor does it recommend or advise investors to buy or sell particular stocks, securities or other investments.

Around this time every year, we conduct NerdWallet’s annual broker review process. We assess what’s changed in the industry, discuss which brokerage features matter most (and which ones now matter less), and finally, we do the work by opening accounts to test them.

Prediction markets, which have made their way into some of the most popular investing apps, came up more than we expected in testing this year.

At first, we decided to simply collect information on who does and doesn’t offer access to them, without intending to reward or penalize a broker either way. It would be a neutral presentation of facts, not something that would factor into how we scored a broker.

But one afternoon, all together in the office, we confronted an uncomfortable question: “Do prediction markets, and such easy access to them within an investment app, go against NerdWallet’s editorial house views?”

After careful consideration, we all agreed: they do.

So we started to configure our 2027 rubric with a firmer stance against this trendy feature, penalizing brokers that actively market sports and entertainment event contracts, and whose prediction markets come with few, if any, guardrails.

We’ve distilled our discussion down to three main points:

These products are being marketed alongside investments.

We fear they could be discouraging long-term investing.

Let’s start here: Many aspects of trading could be seen as gambling-adjacent. Options, futures, highly leveraged single-day equity bets and even crypto can all easily fall into the “highly speculative” category. So why are we picking on prediction markets in particular?

In our view, a key differentiator is a much lower barrier to entry with few in-app guardrails in place.

Most of the products we mentioned above require some level of fluency — and at times even permission from the broker — to dabble in. To trade options, for example, you need to answer questions about your investing proficiency, your finances and more. And even after approval, the terminology required to trade can be so intimidating that the language itself can become an indirect deterrent.

Event contracts, which form the backbone of prediction markets, are largely presented in the vernacular, and our testing showed approval to trade them is completed with a few taps from the home screen. Moreover, their content is often unrelated to finance — according to a May 2026 report by the Pew Research Center, around 80% of volume on the prediction market platform Kalshi was for sports events[1]Pew Research Center. Trading Volume on Prediction Markets Has Soared in Recent Months. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Answering a binary question (yes/no; this/that), posed in everyday language about a familiar topic — something like, “Will the Knicks beat the Spurs on Sunday?” — can be far less daunting than figuring out what an options chain is or understanding forex pairs.

In other words, what makes prediction markets accessible to a wider audience is also what makes them problematic, especially when housed within an investing account. Which brings us to our next point.

On the platforms that feature them, we found that prediction markets almost always appear alongside stock and ETF trading. We think this is a mistake. What has made these mobile-first investing apps so good for so long (making it easy to move, manage and invest money through a beautiful interface) is what’s now making us nervous.

For example, most investing platforms let users do any number of smart things with idle cash. They could open an Individual Retirement Account (IRA), a custodial account or a robo-managed portfolio all through a single app. But now, they can dip into that same pot of money to bet on whether Beyoncé or Alicia Keys will play the Super Bowl halftime show.

But is anyone actually trading these event contracts? Let’s use data from publicly traded brokers that offer prediction markets to explore this.

In Q3 2026, Robinhood’s revenue from event contracts rose more than 600% year over year to $173 million, while the number of event contracts traded grew more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion[2]Robinhood. Robinhood Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . This was the second-highest source of transaction revenue behind options trading. In a forecast reported on by Cointelegraph, Bernstein analysts projected Robinhood’s prediction markets could drive $1.7 billion in annual revenue by 2028[3]Yahoo Finance. Bernstein Sees Robinhood Prediction Markets Reaching $1.7 Billion in Revenue by 2028, Topping Crypto. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Coinbase's Q1 2026 quarterly report called prediction markets “one of its fastest-scaling products ever, driven by strong retail interest[4]Coinbase. Coinbase Q1 Financial Results Show Resilient Financial Performance Driven by New All-Time High Crypto Trading Volume Market Share. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources ."

In a call discussing Webull’s Q2 results, U.S. CEO Anthony Denier noted trading volume in Webull’s nascent prediction market product grew about 70% quarter over quarter[5]Gloom. Webull (BULL) Q2 2026 earnings call transcript. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

Gemini’s Q2 report shows prediction market volume rose 93% quarter over quarter[6]Gemini. Shareholder Update Q2 2026. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

So, now that we’ve established that these markets are growing in popularity — and investing platforms appear to have a large incentive to lean into them — how are all those event contract traders faring? That brings us to our final point.

Is all this even worth it? Several studies show how hard it is to actually turn a profit in prediction markets. Here are a few:

One study, conducted by researchers at ESSEC Business School, HEC Montréal and the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management, covered 2.4 million Polymarket accounts across $67 billion in trading volume between November 2022 and March 2026, and found that 69% of users lost money[7]SSRN. Who Wins and Who Loses In Prediction Markets? Evidence from Polymarket. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . Moreover, the top 1% of users who made a profit accounted for about 76% of all gains. Translation: Even if you did turn a profit, there’s a good chance you didn’t make much.

A Bloomberg analysis supports this: From January 2025 to April 2026, more than 100,000 Polymarket accounts lost at least $1,000[8]Bloomberg. Most Prediction Market Traders Are Losing Money While Bots Rack Up Gains. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources . Of the 2 million active wallets studied, almost half made or lost less than $10 during the period, while far fewer accounts collected larger profits.

A separate Wall Street Journal analysis echoed the same trend: 67% of Polymarket profits go to 0.1% of accounts, and more than 70% of Polymarket users lost money[9]The Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

While there is far less data available on Kalshi trades (Polymarket runs on a public blockchain, making it easy to extract and analyze data), a Kalshi spokesperson confirmed in the Wall Street Journal analysis above that one month of data in 2026 showed there were 2.9 unprofitable users to each profitable user[10]Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 10, 2026. View all sources .

The first study above discusses how event contract trading is binary and zero-sum: If one trader wins, another loses. This means traders allocating money to these instruments could be missing out on aspects of equity markets that have helped create long-term wealth for previous generations.

“Unlike equity markets, there is no equity premium, no dividends, and no passive investment options. Their short maturities naturally encourage short-horizon trading, which is precisely what the behavioral finance literature has suggested is most destructive to wealth accumulation. Given the rapid growth of these platforms and their role as a potential entry point for young investors, understanding who bears the losses has direct implications for investor welfare and market regulation.”

As a reminder, the vast majority of Polymarket users bore the losses.

At NerdWallet, our mission has always been to help people make smarter financial decisions, so we’re sticking by that. Starting with our 2027 ratings, brokers that offer easy access to sports and entertainment event contracts will lose points in our scoring system because we believe this new product has the potential to harm long-term wealth building and doesn’t belong in investing platforms.

So, what’s a better way forward? Bring back the friction and make prediction markets a separate app. Financial institutions, businesses and individuals can still explore legitimate use cases for prediction markets, such as forecasting and hedging. And we’re not here to stop anyone from trading event contracts for entertainment with extra money. We just don’t want these markets so easily conflated with the legitimate investing vehicles these apps already offer. And our reviews will reflect that.

#3056. Stock Market Today, Nov. 10: Nvidia Stock Plunges 5.5% as CEO Scandal Overshadows Its Upcoming Earnings Report

Nvidia shares extended their sell-off as an investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang raised fresh concerns about corporate governance, leadership uncertainty, and the AI chipmaker's future.

Nvidia (NVDA -5.47%), the leading manufacturer of artificial intelligence (AI) chips, plunged 5.52% on Tuesday, closing at $168.80 as mounting controversy surrounding CEO Jensen Huang rattled investors. Reports of a potential foreign intelligence operation involving Huang have prompted an independent board investigation and raised concerns about corporate governance and regulatory scrutiny. This comes at an inopportune time as Nvidia's earnings report is scheduled for November 17.

Trading volume surged to 420.8 million shares, more than three times its three-month daily average of 127.2 million, highlighting the intensity of the sell-off. Shares have now declined for two consecutive sessions as investors weigh the unfolding investigation against Nvidia's long-term AI growth prospects.

Broader equity markets also retreated on Tuesday, although Nvidia's losses significantly outpaced the major indexes. The S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.38%) declined 0.38% to 7,521, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -0.74%) fell 0.74% to 25,066 as hotter-than-expected inflation data weighed on investor sentiment.

However, Nvidia's semiconductor peers fared considerably better. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD +1.30%) gained 1.30% to $515.21, while Broadcom (AVGO +3.91%) climbed 3.91% to $331.98. The divergence suggests Nvidia's steep sell-off was driven more by company-specific concerns than a broader reassessment of AI chip demand.

Nvidia's upcoming November 17 earnings report will be an important test of whether its underlying business can overcome the recent controversy. Investors will be watching data center revenue, profit margins, and management's guidance for signs that hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure remains robust heading into 2027. Strong results could help restore confidence in the company's long-term growth prospects.

However, investors shouldn't underestimate the importance of Jensen Huang's leadership. As Nvidia's co-founder and CEO for more than three decades, Huang has been instrumental in shaping its technology roadmap, cultivating strategic partnerships, and positioning the company at the center of the AI revolution. Any uncertainty surrounding his future introduces risks that extend well beyond the immediate investigation.

For now, Nvidia's competitive position in AI computing remains formidable, but the unfolding situation adds a new dimension to its investment outlook. Even a strong earnings report may not fully alleviate investor concerns until there is greater clarity surrounding Huang's leadership and the potential regulatory implications.

#3055. The Last Generation That Speaks Networking

Douglas Murray is the chief executive officer at Auvik.

I’ll say it: I’m old (or so my wife tells me). When I entered the workforce, data communications revolved around technologies like ATM and Frame Relay. With the introduction of the Cisco Catalyst 6500 series and the growing adoption of IP networking, the way the world connected began to change.​

I witnessed those changes firsthand over the course of my career in tech. When I earned my Cisco Certified Internetwork Expert (CCIE) certification, knowing a network also meant knowing its architecture at a physical level, port by port. Today, the deep, specialized networking expertise that defined my generation is becoming increasingly rare.

To put this in perspective, think about how many students coming out of university today go on to pursue networking certifications like the CCIE or JNCIE.​

As veteran specialists with decades of networking experience leave the workforce, fewer professionals with the same depth of networking expertise are stepping in to replace them. At the same time, the role of the IT professional has become much broader. Talent shortages, tool sprawl and rapidly changing technology have helped solidify the rise of the IT generalist, someone who must possess knowledge across a wide range of IT functions rather than specializing in a single silo.​

This shift toward IT generalists has reshaped what an IT career looks like. Organizations now hire for roles like cloud engineer, platform engineer and site reliability engineer, positions that often span multiple areas of infrastructure, including networking, security and operations. In many cases, the specialized knowledge that once sat with individuals deeply focused on the network now has to be shared across broader IT teams managing many other responsibilities at the same time.​

With AI, cloud adoption, SaaS and automation, day-to-day work has been steadily pulled away from racks, consoles and physical infrastructure. The network itself, however, hasn’t become simpler, even though the way we manage it has advanced considerably. A typical environment today spans multiple vendors, each with its own operating systems, commands and conventions. ​

One persistent challenge within that complexity is visibility. Despite advances in tooling and growing IT budgets, my company’s 2026 report found that 27% of IT professionals still cite network visibility as a top challenge. At the same time, modern networks must support an increasingly diverse mix of infrastructure, devices and applications, creating more dependencies to manage and secure. All of this is happening amid evolving cybersecurity threats and IT staffing shortages.​

These ongoing hurdles explain why many businesses are turning to AI. Across the market, vendors are using AI to help IT teams navigate the complexity of network management and resolve issues faster through automation. But being able to manage something through an AI tool does not automatically translate to understanding it. That distinction matters all the more for teams without a dedicated network specialist.​

Historically, much of network knowledge lived with specialists who could recognize what a healthy network looked like, distinguish urgent issues from background noise, diagnose root causes and determine the best course of action for a specific environment. That level of fluency typically takes years of practice to build, and it’s growing scarcer.​

As many network specialists approach retirement age, their deep network knowledge and the judgment it enables still need to exist somewhere within the organization. This has already become an urgent issue for many IT leaders: Earlier this year, Enterprise Management Associates reported that 52% of organizations are struggling to hire and retain network engineers in 2026, up from 26% in 2022.​

An organization might not be able to control the structural changes reshaping the IT workforce, but it can decide where its institutional knowledge goes. With the right​ ​​technology, role design and skill development, ​​organizations can extend network fluency across their IT teams. AI has an important role to play in carrying the expertise forward, although not as a black box that simply tells teams what to do or autonomously executes actions without transparency into how those decisions are made.​

Instead, AI can offer organizations a way to preserve and extend at least some of that expertise by taking knowledge that once required years of specialized experience and putting it in front of the broader IT team at the moment it’s needed. By bringing together network context, correlating signals to surface likely root causes and explaining not just what to do next but why, AI can help IT generalists approach problems from a specialist perspective.​

Over time, that guidance can deepen their understanding of network issues and sharpen their troubleshooting instincts. The goal is to make network-speak accessible to IT professionals at every level, giving them the knowledge and insights they need to make informed decisions, even without years of specialization in the field.​

My generation learned to “speak network” through years of hands-on experience. The task before us now is to ensure that expertise outlives us and continues to grow in the next generation.​

Today, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 6.9% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is eight basis points lower than yesterday and 17 basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

This morning the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) dropped the October Consumer Price Index, which shows that inflation rose another 0.4% last month. This outpaced expectations: Economists had forecasted an increase of 0.3%. CPI is one of two key measures of inflation, which the Federal Reserve aims to keep in check relative to the strength of the labor market. (The Fed looks more closely at a different inflation measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures Index, which comes out Nov. 25.)

Raising the federal funds rate is the Fed’s main tool for bringing inflation down, and futures traders are banking on a rate hike when the committee meets Dec. 8-9. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates directly, but an anticipated rate hike can put upward pressure on mortgage rates, which respond to investors’ expectations for the economy and Fed policy.

Central bankers raised the federal funds rate in September, but it hasn’t been enough to pull inflation closer to the Fed’s target of 2%. Investors aren’t sure that one more hike in December will do the trick, either. According to CME FedWatch, further rate hikes may be in store for January.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

#3048. Here's How Much a $5,000 Investment in SpaceX Stock Could Be Worth by November 2027

Space Exploration Technologies' stock price could be noticeably higher by this time next year, but successful investing requires thinking about the long term.

Analysts' 12-month price targets aren't guarantees of where a stock could trade down the road. But with a company like Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +0.72%), price targets can help retail investors establish a risk-to-reward framework to inform their investment considerations.

After all, with SpaceX not only involved in the space sector but also viewing its biggest opportunities in artificial intelligence (AI), it helps to get a ballpark sense of what an investment today could be worth a year from now.

Today, we'll look at how analysts are valuing the company to get an idea of how much a $5,000 investment made now could be worth by November 2027.

According to data tracked by CNN, analysts generally have a favorable outlook on SpaceX. Out of the 47 who cover the stock, 77% rate it a buy, 19% a hold, and 4% a sell.

Among that group, the median one-year price target is $245, which would be an 82.4% gain from the Nov. 6 closing price of $134.27. We'll ignore the highest target of $800, as SpaceX is unlikely to reach that in just a year. We will, however, focus on the lowest target, $118, which would amount to a 12.1% loss.

If someone bought $5,000 worth of SpaceX at the Nov. 6 closing price of $134.27, that would yield approximately 37 shares. With 37 shares, if SpaceX reached the median one-year price target of $245 per share, that $5,000 investment would be worth $9,065. If the stock price sank to the lowest target, $118, that $5,000 investment would be worth $4,336.

SpaceX is showing accelerated revenue growth, as evidenced by its third-quarter results, with sales growing 161% to $14.5 billion. The company also reported net income of $4.4 billion, a nice change of pace from the $1 billion net loss it reported in the prior-year period.

The company is enjoying a noticeable sales growth trajectory. It's forecasting first-quarter 2027 revenue of between $33 billion and $37 billion, which is impressive given that it reported $18.6 billion in revenue for all of 2025.

If SpaceX can keep growing its sales and trimming its net losses, investor enthusiasm could provide some fuel to help the stock price reach that $245 target.

There are a few reasons why SpaceX's stock price could fall to $118, and it could always slide even further. One of the factors putting pressure on it now is the recent broad sell-off in AI stocks. While SpaceX's AI segment went from generating $813 million in the third quarter of 2025 to $7.5 billion in the third quarter of 2026, it's still spending heavily to build its data center infrastructure. Its capital expenditures totaled $19.6 billion in the third quarter, with $16.4 billion of that spent on its AI division alone.

The share price could also fall amid a broad market sell-off or due to a few underwhelming quarterly performances.

The risk-to-reward framework looks favorable over the next year, but doesn't make SpaceX an automatic investment just based on one-year price targets. Ultimately, meaningful wealth isn't typically created after just one year of owning a stock, and it will take years for SpaceX to execute on its ambitions.

Even in this stock's short trading history, there have been many wild price swings. Those are only likely to continue. To hold onto this stock through the rockiest moments requires shareholders to have strong conviction in the company. While it's common to hear people talk in retrospect about how much money retail investors could have made by investing in one of CEO Elon Musk's other companies, Tesla, in its early days, what is less often shared are the tales of investors who sold their stock along the way because they couldn't handle the volatility.

With SpaceX, capturing the biggest gains will require patience and a strong enough belief in the company that a shareholder won't react with a knee-jerk sell if they see the stock price head significantly lower.

Legacy margins climbed as Chaparral and Robalo integration advanced.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

MasterCraft Boat Holdings, Inc. (MCFT -3.17%) reported financial results for the first quarter of its six-month transition period, highlighting the strategic integration of the Marine Products acquisition. Management reported that the addition of the Chaparral and Robalo brands has diversified the portfolio across price points and categories, reducing dependence on any single boating segment. The company reported significant margin expansion in its legacy business, driven by a premium product mix and operational cost discipline. Management indicated that dealer health remains a priority, with inventory levels currently below prior-year levels. The company raised its guidance for the transition period based on first quarter performance and continued synergy execution.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for standing by, and welcome to the MasterCraft Boat Holdings, Inc. First Quarter 2026 Transition Period Earnings Conference Call. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded. [Operator Instructions] I would now like to hand the conference over to your speaker today, Alec Harmon, Senior Director, Strategy and Investor Relations. Please go ahead, sir.

Alec Harmon: Thank you, operator, and welcome, everyone. Thank you for joining us today as we discuss the first quarter transition period performance of MasterCraft Boat Holdings. As a reminder, today's call is being webcast live and will also be archived on our website for 1 year for future listening. With me on this morning's call is Brad Nelson, Chief Executive Officer; and Scott Kent, Chief Financial Officer. Brad will begin with an overview of our operational performance. After that, Scott will discuss our financial performance. Brad will then offer some closing remarks before we open the call for questions.

Before we begin, we would like to remind participants that the information contained in this call is current only as of today, November 10, 2026. The company assumes no obligation to update any statements, including forward-looking statements. Statements that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and subject to the safe harbor disclaimer in today's press release. Additionally, on this call, we will discuss non-GAAP measures that include or exclude items not indicative of our ongoing operations. For each non-GAAP measure, we will also provide the most directly comparable GAAP measure in today's press release, which includes a reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to our GAAP results.

Beginning this quarter, certain corporate costs that were previously reported within our Performance and Wake segment are now being reported separately. This change better reflects how we manage the combined company, affecting segment presentation only and has no impact on our consolidated results. Prior period segment results have also been recast for comparability. Also as a reminder, in connection with our change to a December 31 fiscal year-end, today's results cover the first 3 months of our 6-month transition period, which runs from July 1 through December 31, 2026. We will compare these results to the prior year period, which includes the 3 months ended September 28, 2025.

Because this quarter includes a full quarter of contribution from Chaparral and Robalo and the prior year period includes no contribution from these brands, we will speak to our results on both a total company basis and a Legacy basis, with Legacy representing our Performance and Wake segment, including corporate costs, and our Leisure segment. Unless otherwise noted, the following commentary is made on a continuing operations basis, and all references to specific quarters and periods will be on a fiscal basis. With that, I will turn the call over to Brad.

Bradley Nelson: Thank you, Alec, and good morning, everyone. We delivered results above our expectations in the first quarter of the transition period. In our first full quarter operating as a combined company following the acquisition of Marine Products, we exceeded expectations for both net sales and adjusted EBITDA with strong Legacy execution complemented by the first full quarter contribution from Chaparral and Robalo. Total company net sales grew more than 120% year-over-year. Importantly, our Legacy business net sales grew 37% and delivered adjusted EBITDA growth of nearly 140%. We are pleased with our performance this quarter. These results reflect deliberate product, commercial and operational actions we have taken across our business to drive premium mix, clean channels and reduce costs.

These efforts are foundational and continue to build on the momentum we have delivered over the past several quarters. Dealer health remains strong and continues to be a priority for MCBH. Dealer inventories across our established brands are healthy and below prior year levels with inventory turns better than last year and near pre-COVID levels as we exit the quarter. Because of this, we believe our dealers have more flexibility to respond to market demand while we remain disciplined in aligning wholesale shipments with retail demand. Now turning to retail. On a calendar year-to-date basis, total company retail continues to outperform the broader market. Consumer sentiment remains cautious, and we are monitoring retail trends closely as we plan production.

Against that backdrop, with the recent addition of the Chaparral and Robalo brands, the benefit from diversification of our portfolio is proving to be helpful, providing exposure across a broader range of consumers, product categories and price points. Chaparral and Robalo performed particularly well at retail during the quarter. That broader coverage gives us more ways to serve customers and reduces our dependence on any single boating category or market. Looking ahead, we believe the breadth of our portfolio, combined with our continued focus on product innovation, positions us well to continue our momentum.

We have an exciting pipeline of new products in development across our brands that we believe will further strengthen our competitive advantages and provide additional opportunities for growth. Our approach and priorities remain steady. We will continue aligning wholesale with retail demand to preserve dealer health, leveraging our flexible operating model to control costs and investing in innovation and synergies throughout the cycle. Now turning to our segments. In Performance and Wake, MasterCraft continues to lead in the premium ski/wake category. Our model year 2027 lineup builds on the momentum of the next-generation X Series with enhancements designed around the driver and rider experience.

The success of the next-generation X Series is a clear example of the strength of our products and portfolio strategy and our ability to translate a deep understanding of our consumers into products that resonate in the market. Combined with our ongoing cost, productivity and quality initiatives, those actions are driving stronger earnings and margin performance. Together, these factors contributed to a strong Q1 performance with MasterCraft delivering a 26.7% adjusted EBITDA margin, generating $21.8 million of adjusted EBITDA. The strength of these results are evidence of the earnings progress created by innovation, simplification and sustained operational execution.

During the quarter, MasterCraft also made its first appearance at the Monaco Yacht Show, where we showcased the X24 as a superyacht tender featuring custom factory-installed lifting points, expanding MasterCraft's presence within the ultra-premium boating market and continuing to expand the brand globally with luxury customers. In Leisure, adjusted EBITDA margin improved nearly 500 basis points year-over-year, driven by higher volumes, lower discounts and cost initiatives. For model year 2027, Crest expanded its Conquest SE lineup at an accessible price point and refreshed the Caribbean Series, including the new 22-foot model, while both Crest and Balise now offer twin-engine configurations on 24- and 26-foot models.

Balise also broadened its addressable market with a 22-foot model across all layouts and an all-new entertainer layout featuring a wet bar, refrigerator and grill. We are also building real momentum in distribution. Crest and Balise added a meaningful number of new dealers during the quarter, including several existing partners from across the broader MCBH network. This reflects the value of our broader brand portfolio and the opportunity to deepen relationships with high-quality dealers across categories. Expanded sales coverage, a focused dealer acquisition strategy and an enhanced product lineup, all position our Leisure brands well for growth as conditions improve. Turning to Recreation and Sport Fishing segment.

We are pleased with our integration progress as we continue to advance operations as a combined company. Our focus on synergies has shifted from planning to execution with initiatives underway and dedicated teams in place across product and portfolio strategy, distribution expansion, operating disciplines and sourcing. On sourcing, our corporate sourcing team is beginning to realize the benefits from the increased scale of the combined company while continuing to identify additional opportunities across our supplier base. Operationally, we are also taking steps to optimize our manufacturing footprint, improve capacity utilization and reduce costs. These are foundational steps in building a more efficient and profitable combined company.

And while we remain early in the process, we are encouraged by the progress to date and the opportunities we see ahead. Turning to capital allocation. Our priorities remain unchanged, maintaining a strong balance sheet, investing in innovation and growth, which includes synergies, returning capital to shareholders through share repurchases and maintaining a disciplined approach to M&A. Overall, we executed well in a dynamic market, exceeded our expectations and advanced the integration of our combined portfolio. With that, I'll turn the call over to Scott.

Scott Kent: Thanks, Brad, and good morning, everyone. I'll start by reviewing our results for the first quarter, then cover our balance sheet and capital allocation and finish with our outlook for the remainder of the transition period. Net sales for the quarter were $154.1 million, an increase of 123.4% compared to the prior year period, including $59.3 million from our Recreation and Sport Fishing segment. On a Legacy basis, net sales were $94.8 million, an increase of 37.4% compared to $69 million in the prior year period, driven by higher volumes of our next-generation X Series models, which drove favorable mix, along with disciplined pricing and lower discounts.

Consolidated gross margin was 21.1% compared to 22.3% in the prior year period, reflecting the blended margin profile following the Marine Products acquisition. Legacy gross margins expanded 600 basis points to 28.3% from 22.3% in the prior year period, driven by improved fixed cost absorption, favorable mix, lower discounts and operating improvements across both our Performance and Wake, and Leisure segments. Operating expenses were $20.5 million compared to $11.6 million in the prior year period. The increase primarily reflects a full quarter of Recreation and Sport Fishing as well as additional acquisition and integration costs related to the Marine Products transaction.

Adjusted net income was $12.2 million or $0.50 per diluted share compared to $4.7 million or $0.29 per diluted share in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA was $20.1 million with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 13% compared to $7 million and 10.1% in the prior year period. On a Legacy basis, adjusted EBITDA was $16.7 million, with margin expanding 750 basis points to 17.6%. As a reminder on the purchase accounting, our adjusted results this quarter exclude $1.9 million of integration and transaction-related expenses, $0.6 million of amortization of acquired intangibles and the remaining $0.3 million of inventory step-up related to the Marine Products combination, which is now fully recognized.

Consistent with what we outlined last quarter, intangible amortization and depreciation for the acquired company are now running at normalized levels of approximately $0.6 million and $2.6 million per quarter, respectively. Turning to the balance sheet. We generated $2.9 million of free cash flow in the quarter and ended the period with $41.9 million in cash, no debt and full availability under our $75 million revolving credit facility for total liquidity of $116.9 million. After pausing share repurchases while completing the Marine Products acquisition, we resumed buybacks in the quarter, consistent with our long-standing approach to capital allocation. We repurchased approximately $4.8 million of our shares with approximately $18.7 million remaining under our current authorization.

With a strong balance sheet and cash generation, share repurchases remain an important part of our capital allocation strategy. Now turning to our outlook. Based on our first quarter out-performance and current expectation, we are raising our guidance for the 6-month transition period. We now expect net sales of between $293 million and $297 million, adjusted EBITDA of between $32 million and $34 million and adjusted earnings per share of between $0.75 and $0.80. We continue to expect capital expenditures of approximately $9 million for the period. Our priorities for the remainder of the period remain unchanged, aligning wholesale with retail demand, protecting dealer health, maintaining cost discipline and executing our synergy plan.

We believe this disciplined approach positions us well to navigate the current environment while continuing to strengthen the business for the long term. As we look to the December quarter, we expect our underlying build rates and AUSPs to remain consistent with Q1. However, normal holiday seasonality will likely result in modestly lower sequential shipments due to fewer production days. Overall, we remain confident in the strength of our portfolio, our balance sheet and the long-term earnings power of the combined company. This quarter's performance demonstrates another step forward with strong execution, disciplined cost management and commercial optimization. Our financial flexibility will allow us to continue investing in innovation while also aggressively pursuing our synergy plan.

As we continue executing our focused plan and leveraging the scale of the combined company, we believe we have a meaningful opportunity for ongoing value creation. With that, I'll turn it back to Brad for closing remarks.

Bradley Nelson: Thanks, Scott. This quarter reinforces three important drivers of our long-term earnings potential. First, commercial and operational execution across our business is translating into higher earnings. Second, our expanded brand portfolio and growing dealer network are creating new opportunities for growth across categories and end markets. And third, the investments we are making to capture synergies and leverage the scale and capabilities of the combined company provide meaningful opportunities that we believe will drive further value creation. Looking ahead, our priorities remain clear. We will continue to align wholesale with retail demand, drive operational improvements and invest in product innovation that supports the long-term competitive strength of our brands. We are moving decisively from synergy planning to execution.

Our focus is on preserving what makes each of our brands unique and successful while unlocking opportunities created by the scale and capabilities of the combined company. With a strong balance sheet, a flexible operating model and five leading brands, we are confident in our ability to execute through the current environment while building an even stronger company for the long term. I want to thank our team members, dealer partners, suppliers and shareholders for their continued support and another strong quarter. Operator, you may now open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your first question comes from Joe Altobello with Raymond James.

Joseph Altobello: First question on the guidance. You obviously raised the transition period guidance, but it seems like the September quarter was better than you originally thought and the December quarter, maybe a tad lighter than you originally thought. Were there any timing issues in the quarter? Are you seeing any margin pressures cropping up here in the December quarter?

Scott Kent: Yes, Joe, I think our -- we really outperformed a little bit in the first quarter, and some of that was timing. So we did shift a bit of our production from Q2 into Q1 or just shipped a few of it a little early. So that's a lot of it. Remember, December -- the December quarter does have some less production days in it because of the normal holiday seasonality. So it is a little lower from a quarter sequential basis. But the underlying build rates and really the ASPs and all that are consistent with Q1. So it's just a matter of some timing fluctuations between costs as well as build rates between the quarters.

Joseph Altobello: Okay. Perfect. And you sort of addressed this a little bit in your prepared remarks, but how would you assess the promotional environment in the ski/wake category at this point?

Scott Kent: Generally, I think we're -- it's still a competitive environment out there. We're still having to do discounts. We think they're pretty much more normalized to some degree. There is a cleaner channels out there from our perspective, and that does help us to keep our discounts low. Our new products that we've been introducing, especially around the XStar and the X Series product line have also helped us not have to do a lot of discounting. So a lot of the actions we've been taking really over the last 2 years are really helping us keep those discounts a little lower than what we might have to do if our channels are a little more unhealthy.

Joseph Altobello: Are you being forced at all to sort of counter other manufacturers' discounts?

Scott Kent: Again, discounts are probably a little higher, but not anything beyond what we'd call normal. We're generally doing our discounts in the normal times we do discounts. So again, we think our position with our dealer health as well as our channel and product are really helping us keep our discounts a little lower.

Operator: Your next question comes from Anna Glaessgen with B. Riley Securities.

Anna Glaessgen: I'd like to start with that gross margin number you gave us on the Legacy business, 28.3%, pretty impressive considering the historical performance, a number we haven't seen in quite some years. Maybe give us some perspective on how this was achieved despite still at a lower production rate than historical norms and to what extent there was maybe anything onetime in there?

Scott Kent: Again, the Legacy gross margin did expand about 600 basis points to the 28.3% that you mentioned. It does reflect some improved absorption year-over-year on that increased volumes. It does have favorable mix. Again, our X Series product that is driving a bit extra sales in the quarter from what X Series would typically do because of the success of that product. We do have some lower discounts on a year-over-year basis. And we do continue to have continued operating improvements, not just in our MasterCraft division, but also in our Leisure segment and our Pontoon brands as well.

So again, all of our strong pipeline management, the new products and operating execution has really been transferring into profitability and showing just the kind of power that we can have when we actually are able to grow sales.

Anna Glaessgen: Got it. And then coming back to retail, are we still expecting for the overall transition period for units to decline in the 5% to 10% range?

Bradley Nelson: Yes, Anna, this is Brad. It's clearly a selective market out there. Consumers remain cautious. But yes, consistent with our prior view, our guidance assumes market down for this calendar year period to be roughly down between the 5% to 10% that we mentioned prior. And then going forward, we're planning for a continued cautious market, but there are buyers out there. It's just the market is not broken. It's just more selective. And in recent periods of time, we continue to be rewarded just with good execution on product as well as a clean channel, and we'll continue to align production of retail to -- of wholesale to retail.

Operator: Your next question comes from Gregory Miller with Truist Securities.

Gregory Miller: For my first question, I'd like to get your perspective on how initial boat shows have proceeded, including the FLIBS recently. I appreciate there's weather in Fort Lauderdale. But outside of that, I'd be curious to get your impressions on your brand's performance there.

Bradley Nelson: Greg, yes, the read on FLIBS and just some of the early sentiment out there across the industry and the sectors within the industry and our categories have been pretty much flattish year-over-year. There's a couple of exceptions to that rule, maybe some strengths and weaknesses. But in general, we've seen -- our performance at both shows has been consistent with that with the broader marine category, which is flattish. In a couple of categories, we've seen better performance. But it seems like attendance at the show was down a little bit, but at the same time, there were still active buyers engaged. So the quality of the buyers seemed slightly improved.

Scott Kent: I remember that the FLIBS show -- you might remember that the FLIBS show is really a saltwater show as well as a bigger boat show. So our brands are not quite as fully represented at the FLIBS show. Really, it's our Robalo brand mostly that is at that show and has the more significant presence. So being flattish on Robalo was actually pretty positive for us.

Gregory Miller: Great. For my follow-up, you mentioned on the call and then you had the press release before earnings on the dealer network expansion, which is a pretty significant number of dealer additions coming from your Legacy brands. So I was just hoping to get a little more context in terms of how that all came to pass in the last couple of months. And then in particular, any thoughts on further growth internationally?

Bradley Nelson: Yes. Distribution in general and a strong dealer network, that's a growth lever for us long stated. It's part of our core strategy. So we always work on that, and we'll continue. Now with the addition of Chaparral and Robalo, we have a boat for everybody. We've got a wide range of price points. We have a diversity of categories. We're not as reliant on a category or two within Marine. So that certainly helps us. So we were able to add dealers in the past quarter in all of our brands. And some of those were international, but most of those were in North America. And some of them were cross-brand polymerization within our MCBH family.

There are active discussions happening. We already signed some of those and already seeing some boats move accordingly. But there are ongoing discussions, numerous, in fact, between our newly expanded dealer network going forward, and we see strong potential as that unfolds. Ultimately, our broader portfolio gives our dealers much more flexibility through this dynamic market environment, and it just gives us a lot more ways to win, and we're starting to see that.

Operator: Your next question comes from Noah Zatzkin with KeyBanc Capital Markets.

Noah Zatzkin: I guess maybe if you could expand a bit on kind of like what were you're tracking in regards to the synergy opportunities around Chaparral and Robalo. Just some context about kind of where you're tracking a plan and the opportunity that remains ahead.

Bradley Nelson: Yes. We've got -- we've already captured approximately $6 million of annual public company and overhead savings from the transaction. We are now moving from a broader synergy and integration perspective, we're pleased with our progress. It's on pace. We're moving now from planning into execution. We do have dedicated teams working initiatives around sourcing, operating initiatives, footprint, portfolio as well as distribution initiatives. And we're seeing some early sourcing benefits starting to emerge. So that will continue to mature with time. Some of these things will take a little bit more time, and we look forward to giving updates as visibility improves in the future.

Scott Kent: And I'd generally say we're on track, if not ahead, in some of our synergy plans versus what we laid out. So I think we're really pleased with the progress so far.

Noah Zatzkin: And hoping you could maybe just comment on what you're seeing or hearing in terms of kind of health of the broader industry dealer base now out of selling season.

Scott Kent: As we talk to our financing partners, generally speaking, I'd say industry inventories are down across the board. Dealer health is generally healthy across. That doesn't mean you don't have the occasional problem with a dealer here and there, but certainly nothing broad-based that's certainly causing any overall concerns at the moment.

Bradley Nelson: Well, I would add, in general, with the inventory side of that, Noah, managing pipeline inventory, as you probably know, is central to how we manage this business. So managing that pipeline, we feel good about the number of units that are out there as well, we feel generally good about the aging profile of those units. And that's going to help us. Dealers right now seem fine. It's one of the stronger parts of our story actually as we lean forward as they now have flexibility to deal with a dynamic consumer.

Operator: Your next question comes from Gerrick Johnson with Seaport Research Partners.

Gerrick Johnson: I'm interested in Crest and the expansion of distribution there. Pontoons are obviously very competitive and you have a few new competitors coming into the space. So it looks like you added 13 dealers. How much of that came from the MPX relationship? And if it was organic, what is it about Crest that's enticing dealers to take on the brand?

Bradley Nelson: Yes, Gerrick. Overall, let me make a broader statement around Leisure. Team is really engaged, a strong team, making progress, moving in the right direction. That business, just from a broader perspective, margins up nearly 500 bps. It's now 6 consecutive quarters of profit growth due to cost initiatives and efficiency initiatives. So we're pleased with the progress. It's not fully where it needs to be, but key to that effort is distribution expansion that you've mentioned. Finding dealers that are truly aligned with our product innovation and with the market right now is core. So among those that we signed, yes, some of those are due to MCBH relationships across, including Chaparral and Robalo and we're early.

So we're pleased with the early progress there. It has strong potential. As you know, some of those things take time to unfold to get a dealer on board, to get them signed, to get them engaged on the product, trained, develop to where they can take a healthy stocking position and then start retailing boats. We're making progress on all those fronts, but it's still early. And that's really what we're seeing with dealers is interest in the product refreshes that we've done. So we've expanded our Conquest lineup, our SE lineup, which adds a variety of new affordable price points.

The team has refreshed the Caribbean series, added twin configuration -- twin engine configurations on all of our 24- and 26-foot models for both Crest and Balise and a brand-new Balise 22-footer across layouts. So we're seeing dealers engaged on products, on our innovation stance, some of the structural changes we made in the business and then the quality of the products remains high. We're pleased with the data that we're seeing there, too.

Gerrick Johnson: Okay. Great. Sounds good. And then on Robalo and Chaparral, you're kind of more of a midrange kind of boat brands there. That's kind of the cohort of consumers that are feeling the most pressure. So what's going on there to drive the outperformance versus the industry for both Robalo and Chaparral?

Bradley Nelson: Well, you've got two proud brands that have been -- Chaparral obviously being a market leader in the Gen-Rec and runabout space continues to be that. Tremendous dealer network, tried and true proven products, proven execution, high-quality boats. And with Robalo on the saltfish and sportfish side of the house, is surging. We're pleased with market share gains there and a very engaged dealer network. And we're seeing some continued vibrancy in that sport fish market. It's one of the more resilient categories within Marine. And our price point diversity now across those boats, it's not all midrange. We've got price points from low to premium, and that diversification across all of our brands is helping us right now.

We've been pleased with the early progress.

Scott Kent: I think some of the product that we've introduced with especially the Robalo has also been really strong. They've got a really strong dual console lineup with a couple of new entrants in the dual console lines. They've also added some additional center consoles. They also have a Bay Boat series. And frankly, we've been winning share in all 3 of the segments that we compete in with some of the product introductions that we've been introducing with that lineup as well. So Robalo has really been a shining star for us from a market share perspective.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. This concludes today's call. Thank you for attending. You may now disconnect.

#3043. Car Insurance Soars for Drivers With Poor Credit; Here’s What to Do

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

While building your credit, shop around for auto insurance quotes. Some insurers are more lenient than others.

Lead Writer & Licensed Insurance Specialist

Your driving record may be spotless, but if you have poor credit, car insurance companies view you as a risk — and they’re significantly raising your rates.

Over the past three years, drivers with poor credit have seen auto insurance premiums surge 37.7%, according to NerdWallet’s 2026 Auto Insurance Rates Report. These price hikes were even steeper than those faced by drivers with good credit who caused a crash or got a DUI.

In January 2023, someone with poor credit and a clean driving record would pay a median of $2,864 per year for full-coverage car insurance, NerdWallet’s analysis found. By January 2026, premiums for this driver had risen to $3,944 — an increase of $1,081 per year. By comparison, the same driver with good credit saw an increase of only $576.

“Credit scores are one of the most harmful things that results in you paying higher auto insurance premiums,” says Michael DeLong, a research and advocacy associate with the Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit Consumer Federation of America. “The penalties are extremely severe.”

While higher premiums after a wreck or DUI may not be a surprise, DeLong says many drivers aren’t aware their credit scores will affect their car insurance rates. To further complicate things, building credit can take months.

But there are ways to get relief more quickly. DeLong suggests comparing car insurance quotes from multiple companies, because some insurers penalize poor credit less than others. Raising your deductible, evaluating your coverage and avoiding small claims can also help.

NerdWallet’s analysis found that insurers raised rates more sharply from 2023 to 2026 for drivers with poor credit than for those with good credit — even if the poor-credit driver had a flawless record while the good-credit driver had a DUI, speeding ticket or at-fault crash.

When our sample driver with poor credit also had a recent DUI or speeding ticket, rate increases were even greater. Prices for a full-coverage policy went up by more than 40% for drivers with poor credit and a recent DUI, the biggest increase of any profile we analyzed.

Drivers often think it’s unfair for credit to affect car insurance prices, DeLong says, since it isn’t directly linked to driving behavior. Some states agree; California, Hawaii and Massachusetts don’t allow credit as a factor in setting auto insurance rates.

However, insurers say credit scores can indicate the likelihood that a driver will file a claim.[1]National Association of Insurance Commissioners. Credit-Based Insurance Scores. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources They use what’s called a credit-based insurance score — similar to the typical credit scores used by lenders but weighted differently.

“It helps in predicting expected claims activity and loss costs more accurately,” said Norman Niami, a member of the American Academy of Actuaries' Automobile Insurance Committee, in an email.

The practice has been controversial, with critics arguing it disproportionately hurts low-income and minority drivers. But a Federal Trade Commission report to Congress in July 2007 concluded that credit-based insurance scores were strong predictors of risk even when controlled for income, race and ethnicity.[2]A Report to Congress by the Federal Trade Commission. Credit-Based Insurance Scores: Impacts on Consumers of Automobile Insurance. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources

The explanation may be that some people simply tend to take risks, according to a statistical analysis published in the North American Actuarial Journal in 2016.[3]North American Actuarial Journal. Empirical Evidence on the Use of Credit Scoring for Predicting Insurance Losses with Psycho-social and Biochemical Explanations. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources Researchers concluded that risk-taking behavior can affect credit scores as well as insurance claims. Their analysis found that average losses per policy were 64.6% higher for drivers with the lowest credit scores than for those with the best credit.

Working to build your credit over time may help lower your car insurance premiums, but it’s not a sure thing. A credit-based insurance score is just one of many factors (along with things like location, age and driving history) that insurers use to rate a person’s risk.

Building credit “can produce a noticeable premium decrease in some cases, while producing little or no change in others,” Niami said, depending on whether the new score causes an insurer to move you into a better rating tier. Each insurer sets its own score thresholds, so a score viewed as “poor” by one insurer might be considered “fair” by another.

At the same time, consumer advocates argue it’s difficult for many people to take the steps needed to strengthen their credit scores.

“Most people probably have some idea that you can improve your credit score by trying to pay your bills regularly and reliably, and using different kinds of financial resources and credit cards,” DeLong says.

“But again, that’s easier said than done," he says. "If you’re struggling at a low-wage job and trying to juggle bills, or if you don’t easily have access to a credit card, that advice may not be especially helpful."

Drivers with poor credit or no credit may be able to take other steps to lower their premiums.

Comparing car insurance quotes from different companies is one of the best ways to ensure you have the cheapest rate possible. Insurers set their own pricing formulas, and some are more forgiving of poor credit than others. A NerdWallet analysis of October 2026 rates found that in about half (49.3%) of U.S. ZIP codes in states that allow credit scoring, the cheapest insurer for a driver with poor credit was a different company than the cheapest for a driver with good credit.

Although you can’t improve your risk profile overnight, “there’s a bunch of small things you can do that over a two- to three-year span make you look a lot better” to insurers, says Bradley Flowers, founder of Portal Insurance agency in Mobile, Alabama.

Consider a higher deductible. Raising your car insurance deductible — the amount of a future claim that you agree to cover yourself — lowers your premium and signals to insurers that you’re less likely to file a claim. But be sure you can afford to pay the higher deductible if you have to make a claim.

Adjust how you’re billed by insurers. By signing up for automatic payments and ensuring you don’t miss insurance payments each month, you’ll get a small discount while improving your risk profile for insurers.

Avoid minor claims if you can. Flowers recommends thinking twice about filing minor claims, such as windshield cracks. “When you’re in one of these situations, let’s save our insurance for the really bad stuff,” he suggests.

Lastly, be sure your coverage fits your vehicle. If you could afford to replace your car on your own, consider dropping collision and comprehensive coverage to bring your premiums down. Your trimmed-down policy would still provide you with liability coverage after a crash, while leaving you to cover damage to your vehicle.

NerdWallet's 2026 Auto Insurance Rates Report is based on an analysis of more than 1.4 billion rate estimates provided by Quadrant Information Services for all 50 states and Washington, D.C., from January 2023 to January 2026.

Quadrant derives its rate data from modeled estimates based on carrier rating algorithms; figures do not reflect every available carrier or every consumer's individual rate. Liberty Mutual does not participate in Quadrant's rate data and is not represented in this analysis.

Quadrant’s figures are modeled rate estimates produced by running a fixed driver profile through carrier rating algorithms. They represent both new business and renewal rate estimates, and they are not a record of what actual drivers paid.

NerdWallet anchored its analysis to a 3-year old Toyota Camry LE, ensuring each analysis period reflected rates for the same-aged car.

The primary rate analysis is based on a 35-year-old single driver with good credit, no recent at-fault accidents or driving violations, and a full-coverage policy with $1,000 deductibles for collision and comprehensive coverage. Rates are pooled across male and female drivers.

In states where drivers must carry other types of insurance not included in our full coverage profile specifications, we added the minimum amount of coverage required by those states. Some policies include additional coverage at the insurer’s discretion.

In addition to our base profile driver with good credit and a spotless driving history, we analyzed rates for the following driver profiles:

Drivers with an at-fault crash. We added a single at-fault crash causing $10,000 in property damage.

Drivers with a speeding ticket. We added a single speeding ticket for driving 16 mph over the speed limit.

Drivers with a DUI. We added a single drunken-driving violation.

Drivers with poor credit. This is the same as our regular base profile, except the driver has poor credit instead of good credit. We also analyzed rates for drivers with poor credit and each of the three incidents above.

NerdWallet applied a strict comparability filter before calculating year-over-year figures. Only coverage variants and carrier/state combinations present in all four years of data were included in median calculations. This ensures reported changes reflect genuine pricing shifts among stable carriers, rather than differences caused by insurers entering markets, exiting, or going insolvent during the analysis period.

#3041. Grupo Cibest (CIB) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Nequi's spinoff is complete and its loan book is expanding fast.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Grupo Cibest S.A. (CIB -3.96%) reported third quarter results that included loan growth acceleration and the completion of the Nequi spinoff. Management stated that commercial lending served as the primary driver of portfolio expansion as demand for new projects in Colombia increased. The company revised its full-year loan growth guidance upward to reflect this stronger demand. The transition of Nequi into an independent commercial financing company was completed on Sept. 1, and the entity now serves 29 million customers. Management indicated that capital allocation strategies, including the divestment of Banistmo and new capital instrument issuances, are intended to optimize the group's structure for long-term returns.

Operator: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Grupo Cibest Bancolombia Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. My name is Carrie, and I will be your operator for today's call. [Operator Instructions] Please note that this conference is being recorded. I will now turn the call over to our Chief Economist, Laura Clavijo for an overview of the macroeconomic landscape. Laura?

Laura Clavijo: Thank you, Juan Carlos. If you could please proceed to Slide 4. Turning to Colombia, the economy enters 2027 with a mixed but gradually improving outlook. Our central view is that the year will be characterized by two competing forces, an improving investment cycle and post-earthquake reconstruction on the one hand and the necessary adjustment in fiscal and monetary conditions on the other. We expect GDP growth to moderate from 2.6% in 2026 to 2.4% in 2027. Household consumption should remain an important source of growth, but lose momentum as high interest rates, persistent inflation and softer labor market conditions constrained disposable income. At the same time, fiscal consolidation will reduce the contribution from government spending.

Encouragingly, the composition of growth should become more investment-oriented. This investment is projected to rise above 17% of GDP, supported by construction, mining and energy projects as well as reconstruction following the August earthquake. Inflation remains one of the key challenges, following a projected 6.7% year-end reading in 2026, headline inflation could peak at 7.3% during the first half of 2027, largely reflecting the impact of El Niño on food and regulated prices, together with indexation and the minimum wage adjustments. We expect these supply side pressures to fade during the second half, bringing inflation down to 5.5% by December. Nevertheless, still well above the Central Bank's target range. This inflation backdrop will keep monetary conditions tight.

We suspect the policy rate could rise further to 12.5% and remain at this level well into 2027 with the Central Bank waiting for clear evidence of disinflation before restarting the easing cycle. We, therefore, anticipate only modest cuts in the fourth quarter while fiscal risks and elevated global rates further constrained the scope for monetary easing. The fiscal position remains the main macroeconomic vulnerability. An ambitious economic rescue bill worth 2.4% of GDP, containing a significant budget cut and additional taxes are being discussed in Congress before year-end. The signals of fiscal responsibility but be weighed against significant expenditure rigidities and historically high financing requirements.

Our baseline scenario speaks of a Central Government deficit of 7.9% of GDP in 2027, compared with 7.2% in 2026 and assumes a fiscal adjustment of at least 1.5% of GDP to maintain investor confidence and set the path towards fiscal sustainability. Finally, external accounts remain manageable, although the current account deficit is expected to widen from 2.5% of GDP in 2026 to 3.2% in 2027. Importantly, remittances of around 3.4% of GDP should remain an important buffer, keeping the external deficit below its historical average of approximately 4%. Overall, 2027 should be viewed less of a year of acceleration and more of a year of transition.

Growth remains resilient, and its composition improves but Colombia will need to navigate sticky inflation, restrictive financial conditions and above all, a demanding fiscal adjustment before a more balanced and sustainable expansion can take hold. If you could please proceed to Slide 5. Turning to Central America. The outlook for El Salvador and Guatemala remains constructive, although inflationary pressures warrant attention. In El Salvador, growth accelerated to 5.1% year-over-year in the second quarter of 2026, increasingly supported by investment and double-digit construction growth. While resilient consumption, tourism revenues and renewed progress under the IMF program provide additional buffers despite lower remittances and higher import costs. In Guatemala, growth remained robust at 4.3%, supported by domestic demand, remittances, manufacturing and exports.

However, inflation has risen to 4.7%, while the medium-term outlook increasingly hinges on translating fiscal expansion and the strengthened public-private partnership framework into infrastructure investment. Alongside institutional improvements that could support the country's path toward investment grade. From a credit loss perspective, provision expense amounted to COP 145 billion, an increase explained by higher loan origination in a one-off related to the transition between former credit model under local GAAP and the current IFRS accounting.

Commercial loans were the main growth driver, expanding 5.5% during the quarter as per a more constructive business environment in Colombia. Consumer loans also grew at a faster pace, increasing 2% in the quarter, mainly driven by unsecured personal loans and credit cards.

Meanwhile, mortgages maintaining their positive trend, expanding 2.1% over the quarter. Please proceed to Slide 15. When broken down by entity, Bancolombia continued to drive growth supported by commercial loans. The decline in savings accounts reflect seasonality related to payroll and employee benefit payments. At Bancoagricola and BAM, deposit growth was mainly driven by sight deposits. Please proceed to Slide 17.

Our funding mix remained resilient, supported by the strength of our sight deposit base, which represents 57% of total funding and provides a structural advantage in containing funding costs in the current interest rate environment. Bancoagricola and BAM also reported NIM compression, mainly reflecting higher funding costs and lower lending and investment income, respectively. On an annual basis, however, while loans are growing at 9.7%, net interest income is increasing almost 16% and underscoring our robust intermediation capacity. Please proceed to Slide 19.
