Net provision charges reached COP 1.2 trillion, up 17% over the quarter, mainly reflecting an increase in a specific client segment in Bancolombia as well as the consumer segment, driven by higher originations. BAM recorded higher provisions following updates to its expected loss models, incorporating new information for the year while Bancoagricola's provision expenses remained elevated with higher returns adjusted by risk.

Overall, quarterly cost of risk stood at 1.8% and bringing the 9-month accumulated cost of risk to 1.7%. We continue to closely monitor recent events that could affect asset quality. While proactively managing exposures and addressing potentially affected clients. Starting with the earthquake in Colombia, asset quality in the affected areas remains in line with the overall local loan book, supported by relief measures and proactive client management. We may see some deterioration going forward as collections normalize, and we are building provisions accordingly with no expected impact on our cost of risk guidance range for either this year or next year. Regarding El Nino, our main exposure is concentrated in agribusiness, particularly agro exporters.

Provision expenses related to these exposures have already been recognized in line with expected credit losses. Given our limited exposure to potentially affected clients, we do not expect any material additional impact. Please proceed to Slide 21. Delinquency ratios remained well contained across portfolios during the quarter and reflect a meaningful reduction on a yearly basis. Moreover, from an expected losses perspective, Stage 1 has increased significantly its share, driven by growth on originations while Stage 2 and Stage 3 exposures declined over the year. Coverage remained solid at 131% and for 30-day past due loans in 195% for 90-day past due loans.

Overall, these trends indicate that the asset quality remains in line with our guidance considering the pace of growth. Please proceed to Slide 22. Operating expenses remained broadly stable, increasing only 0.3% quarter-over-quarter, driven by higher financial transaction taxes related to the ordinary and extraordinary dividend payments. On a year-to-date basis, expenses grew 8.7%, mainly reflecting the wealth tax recognized earlier this year. Excluding this effect, annual expense growth would have been approximately 5.2%, that is close to 1 percentage point below inflation. Overall, the consolidated cost-to-income ratio stood at 46.6%. We remain focused on structural efficiency and have launched different initiatives addressing our most significant operating and fee related expenses.

In parallel, our AI program is accelerating its adoption across the organization to enhance productivity, supporting a more scalable operating model. Please turn to Slide 23. Shareholders' equity reached COP 39 trillion, up 1.7% over the quarter. Mainly driven by earnings generation, while the year-over-year decline mainly reflects the Banistmo divestment. In July, Bancolombia issued COP 1 billion intra-group capital instrument contributing 44 basis points as additional Tier 1. Combined with the other intragroup transactions, this enhances the group's capital efficiency while providing additional flexibility to support growth in strategic priorities. Bancolombia's stand-alone solvency ratio remained relatively stable at 13.7% as earnings generation and the AT1 issuance helped offset the extraordinary dividend and growth in risk-weighted assets.

Finally, Cibest stand-alone double leverage increased to 98%, reflecting dividend distributions, yet preserving flexibility for corporate initiatives. Please turn to Slide 24. Net income reached COP 2 trillion, which represents an ROE of 22%. The accumulated net income increased 10.5% over the year despite the absence of Banistmo's earnings contribution. And consistently, ROE has jumped from 18% to 22% in the same period underscoring the rationale behind the divestment and the merits of the capital reallocation strategy. So your net fees are running at about, I think it's COP 1.4 trillion per quarter. And at the margin, you're growing, I think, 15% year-over-year, right? So what do you see as sustainable growth for maybe 2027, 2028, since you're getting good traction on the commercial business? And maybe a second question related to fee income ratio. So you reached 21% this quarter.

You got, again, good traction in commercial business in Nequi and you get some efficiency gains to capture going forward. So what's the level of fee income ratio that makes sense for us to model for your long term?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: In terms of fee guidance, what we have seen in 2026 is a very positive result on fee expenses we have been able to contain the fee expense growth. And that way, we have reached the 15% net fee growth. Now for 2027, that is probably not going to be sustainable. So we're going to see revenue on fees growing more in line with the expenses. Both of them should be growing between 10% to 12%. That way, the guidance for net fees for next year should be around 12%. But we will keep on investing on how to transfer the operational processes that demand the fee expenses in order to defend and sustain the margin for fees.

Now regarding your second question, the fee income ratio for us is not a goal itself. It's more a result because it depends a lot on the margins that depends a lot on the interest rates from the Central Bank. So in a more like longer-term picture in which margins come down, fee income ratio should reach figures closer to 25%, but somewhere between 20% and 25% and is reasonable to project and it will all depend on margins, as I explained before.

Operator: Moving on to Andres Soto with Santander Mexico.

Andres Soto: I have a couple of questions. The first one on your double leverage ratio. You have mentioned the 98% level on this third quarter. What is your expectation by year-end? And what is your assumption both for the 2027 guidance and for your medium-term guidance in this metric?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: Andres, yes, our double leverage ratio is around 98%. As you know, after the divestment of Banistmo, it decreased significantly. We do not believe that's going to be above 105, 110 tops, that's basically because of the way we plan to manage leverage. We have a lot of room for leverage. As we have mentioned before, the 120% is the ratio that the risk rating agencies expected us to have, but thinking about between 100 and 105 for double leverage in 2027 should be -- should work.

Andres Soto: Mauricio, how do you guys think about the combination of cash dividends and buybacks?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: So we think about it in a very different way. Both of them are very important tools to manage the leverage structure and the value creation for shareholders. But the buyback program is executed only on market conditions. So it's a tool. We have it. We look at the market every day, but we are not going to execute unless we believe it's an attractive price to not only execute but also to signal the market.

Whereas ordinary dividend is more a result of the leverage structure we have leaving the operational banks having the solvency ratios that they need to absorb growth and the excess capital flowing into the holding that way being able to distribute between 50% and 60% of our net income. So if you think about ordinary dividends going forward, it should be with a growth of inflation plus 2 or 3 points, growing in real terms. Now extraordinary dividends are only coming with extraordinary milestones as it was the creation of Cibest and the divestment of Banistmo.

Andres Soto: That's very clear. And I have a different question, and this is regarding your loan growth expectations for 2027. You mentioned this is going to be driven by commercial lending, when you see the competitive environment, how do you see the risk-adjusted returns that these new commercial loan production is going to produce versus the one that you currently have in your book?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: Andres, the competitive environment is tough. There is a lot of competition, but we are very well positioned, not only in terms of capital, that we have plenty to absorb big tickets and be able to work with our corporate clients, but also with funding. As you know, we have a competitive advantage in funding, and we are activating that to be able to work with those customers. But also and most important of all, is our customer-centric strategy in which we are not focused on competing on pricing. We're competing more in value proposition.

We're competing more in terms of being the principal relationship of our customers in order to be able to serve them with not only lending needs, but everything related to structuring, advisory in all their financial needs.

Operator: Moving on to Santiago Villanueva with Davivienda Corredores.

Santiago Villanueva Lizcano: I just have two, the first one is, what opportunities do you see for the group in terms of RUGE, the new program through which the government aims to incentive the private investment? And my second question is that I would like to better understand the differences between the year-to-date net income for Nequi as reported during the call and the year-to-date net income through August as reported to the Superintendencia Financiera. While a loss of COP 21 billion is reported to the Superintendencia Financiera the figure mentioned during the call, shows a profit of COP 111 billion. So how should I read those differences?

Juan Uribe: Thank you, Santiago. Regarding the incentives that the government is proposing on its fiscal project that they presented or presented to the Congress, I think it's a good opportunity for Colombia and for investors I think one of the main challenges that Colombia has today, it's the lower rate of investment to GDP. Colombia used to have levels around 24%. Now it's 16%. So the proposed measures, I think, are going to incentivize the investment and the idea, the goal is that, that investment returned to levels of more than 24% of GDP, as I mentioned.

For us, we will need to wait and see how the -- what is the final result and what ends being the decision of Congress regarding those incentives for investment. We think there is going to be an opportunity, but we will make, as I mentioned, wait and see.

Laura Clavijo: I would just add that our growth forecast of 2.4% for 2027 does, in fact, include the positive signals in terms of investments that are already in place. And that would be furthermore boosted by the program such as RUGE. We estimate investments to grow 3.5% in 2026 and 4.7% in 2027. And as Juan Carlos was mentioning that will gradually bring investment as a percentage of GDP, at least for next year, around 17%, 18%. Still a long way to go from our golden years in investment, but definitely signals in the right direction.

Mauricio Botero Wolff: Now in terms of your question about Nequi. So Nequi is very particular and we need to understand the difference between the accounting figures, formal accounting figures and the managerial accounting figures. So it was born in September 1. So it only has in the third quarter, it only has a P&L of 1 month of operation. We have the balance sheet of that was built throughout the history. So the way we presented Nequi assuming it existed from January 1, 2026, and that way managerial net income should be between COP 160 billion or COP 180 billion.

Now for next year, that should grow and be above COP 250 billion, but -- it's important to expect that 2027 figures should converge. So the managerial accounting and the formal accounting is going to look much more similar as we build the history of Nequi going forward.

Operator: We'll hear next from [ Alonso Aramburu ] with BTIG.

Unknown Analyst: There's been discussions about the potential increase in the interest rate cap [Foreign Language]. I'm just wondering if this materializes and let's assume the [Foreign Language] increases by 4 or 5 percentage points. What kind of impact would that have on your NIM in 2027?

Juan Uribe: There have been a lot of discussions, as you mentioned, regarding the cap rate in Colombia. And our view is that in Colombia, there is not just one cap rate. Actually, there are like six for different types of loans. The most common, it's the consumer loans cap that applies for credit cards and consumer loans. But there are other cap rates for different type of loans. As a matter of fact, in Nequi, around 6% of our loans have a cap rate that is different than the consumer cap rates. So there are opportunities today.

Our view is that there will be some conversations on how that rate is calculated but we see difficult to have the discussion in Congress and remove completely the cap rate. So that will give an additional room that conversations about how that cap rate is calculated. And to your question, for us, that's an opportunity. What happened with the cap rate and at the level that is today in Colombia, at least the consumer cap rate which is around 28.4%. It's that generates exclusion to some people that due to their level of risk that cap rate don't allow formal financial institutions to lend them.

If that ceiling increases, probably that will include more people that -- as a matter of fact, are already customers of either Bancolombia or Nequi. So that will allow us to lend them money that today, it's difficult due to the level of risk and the cap rate. So what we see is we can keep operating in the way we're operating today with the current cap rate. But if the calculation of the cap rate changes and allow more room, that will also -- will be a big opportunity for us, Alonso.

Unknown Analyst: Okay. But on a net basis, I would assume your margins should be able to increase marginally, in addition to potentially faster loan growth, right?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: Yes, you are correct.

Operator: This now concludes our question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the floor back over to our CEO, Juan Carlos, for closing comments.

Juan Uribe: Thank you, everybody, for participating in this third quarter conference call results. We are positive about how the Grupo Cibest results are developing. The third quarter showed that we are in the trend of having the results that we were expecting. And what we have seen so far for the fourth quarter, it's positive. So we will think that we will end 2026 in line of what we are expecting. 2027 will have some challenges. But I think we are well prepared to face those challenges and take an opportunity -- advantage of the opportunities that we will have in next year.

With this, we conclude this conference call, and we hope you participate in the fourth quarter conference call results. Thank you very much. Have a good day.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for your participation. This does conclude today's teleconference. You may disconnect your lines, and have a wonderful day.

#3038. Apollo to buy nearly 10% stake in Abu Dhabi-backed alternative asset manager Mubadala Capital

Investing giant Apollo Global Management is finalizing a deal to buy nearly a 10% stake in Mubadala Capital, the alternative asset manager subsidiary of Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund, Mubadala Investment Co., according to people familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity.

The deal is expected to be announced later Monday morning, they said. Financial terms were not immediately known.

The transaction is significant on multiple fronts. It further advances Apollo's ambitions in Abu Dhabi often called the "capital of capital." The firm has spent the past 15 years building key strategic relationships there, with both the country's investment arm and its core leadership.

Apollo already has a multibillion-dollar partnership with Mubadala Investment Co., first established in 2022 and extended two years ago. At the time of that extension, Apollo said the agreement would strengthen the firm's Capital Solutions platform by enabling the firms to jointly source and provide customized debt and equity financing to companies worldwide.

In 2023, the institutions formed a $2.5 billion joint venture designed specifically to co-invest in global private credit opportunities over a five-year horizon.

For Mubadala Capital specifically — the region's only large-scale asset manager, advising and administering more than $755 billion in assets — the deal further advances its growth strategy under the direction of CEO Hani Barhoush, and its relevance on the global investing stage. It also marks an inflection point for the company's core alternatives business, which has grown to more than $60 billion.

John Zito, co-president of Apollo's Asset Management arm, and Barhoush have worked closely together over the past several years and, according to sources, their close-knit relationship and the success of prior partnerships led to talks of deepening ties. So did the belief that scale in the asset management business matters more than ever.

"Capital as a moat is a big thing," said one person familiar with the deal.

Importantly, the deal also continues a notable shift in the relationship between American investment firms and the Middle East. While the region, and Abu Dhabi specifically, has long been a sought-after source of capital, this deal further reverses that dynamic, with Apollo making a significant direct investment in the country and its investment vision.

Mubadala Capital's international offices include London, New York, Rio de Janeiro and San Francisco.

Apollo's investment in Mubadala Capital is similar to deals the firm has done with other asset management platforms, including Diameter Capital, Thoreau, Motive Partners and others.

Spokespersons for both firms declined to comment.

#3035. Stock Market Today, Nov. 10: Wall Street's Rally Hits a Roadblock as Hot Inflation Raises the Stakes for the Fed

Yesterday's rebound lost momentum as rising Treasury yields and renewed inflation concerns weighed on stocks

Wall Street's rebound stalled on Tuesday, November 10, as hotter-than-expected inflation data reignited concerns about Federal Reserve interest rate policy and sent Treasury yields higher. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -0.74%) dropped 0.74% to 25,066, retreating from Monday's gains, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.38%) slipped 0.38% to 7,521 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -0.30%) fell 0.30% to 52,232.

Selling pressure extended beyond equities as gold fell 1.84% to $4,038.70, while the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.88%, approaching the psychologically important 5% threshold. Market performance was mixed across sectors, with consumer cyclical stocks leading gains and industrials advancing, while healthcare lagged. The divergence highlighted an increasingly selective market as investors reassessed the outlook for interest rates and economic growth.

Despite the broader market decline, several prominent stocks posted strong gains on Tuesday. Meta Platforms (META +0.00%) surged more than 5% after JPMorgan (JPM +0.00%) added the social media giant to its Focus List, while Sea Limited (SE -1.49%) jumped 8.1% following stronger-than-expected quarterly revenue.

On the downside, Nvidia (NVDA -5.47%) plunged 5.52% amid an ongoing investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang, adding to uncertainty ahead of the chipmaker's upcoming earnings report.

Tuesday's sell-off underscores a growing challenge for equity investors heading into year-end. With inflation proving more persistent than expected, markets are increasingly pricing in another Federal Reserve rate hike in December. Higher borrowing costs could weigh on corporate profitability and put additional pressure on stock valuations, particularly among growth companies whose valuations depend heavily on future earnings.

However, the divergence in individual stock performance suggests investors are becoming more selective rather than abandoning equities altogether. Strong corporate earnings and favorable company-specific developments continue to attract capital, even as broader market conditions deteriorate. This could favor businesses with healthy balance sheets, strong cash flow, and the ability to sustain growth without relying heavily on external financing.

Looking ahead, investors should watch upcoming inflation data, Federal Reserve commentary, and Treasury yields for signs of whether monetary conditions will tighten further. With the 10-year yield approaching 5%, the sustainability of Wall Street's recent rebound may depend increasingly on corporate earnings delivering enough growth to justify elevated valuations.

#3031. Jensen Huang’s 700,000% Return Magnifies Nvidia Succession Risks

The office of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang has an unusual setup: The chief executive officer sits at an enormous oval desk facing his lieutenants, with room for more employees in stadium seating behind them. The arrangement — created as part of Nvidia’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California — is purpose-built to suit how Huang runs the company. Though it’s not uncommon to see cultlike tech CEOs who obsess over details, Huang is in a class of his own. He has led the business since its very beginning 33 years ago, the longest such run in Silicon Valley. And even as Nvidia grew into one of the world’s most powerful companies — with a stock return of more than 700,000% — there’s still no one designated to potentially replace him. #3030. Why Lincoln Educational Services Stock Soared Again Today

Yet another peer just posted an estimates-beating quarter.

For the second trading session in a row, Lincoln Educational Services (LINC +4.54%) stock posted a solid gain on Tuesday. The company's shares continued to benefit from bullish momentum sparked by its impressive third-quarter earnings report and similarly encouraging results from a peer. Its shares closed Tuesday more than 4.5% higher.

That peer is American Public Education (APEI +2.84%). It published its third-quarter results after market close on Monday, and its stock rose the following day. That was mainly thanks to enrollment increases in both of its core operating divisions and to management's top- and bottom-line guidance revisions.

This will sound familiar to Lincoln Educational shareholders, as these dynamics were at play in their company's third quarter. What also helped Lincoln was its double-digit increases in student starts, population, and overall revenue -- and, yes, a guidance raise.

This, along with the recent quarterlies of other education stocks, suggests that demand is rising for the vocational and specialty learning services these companies provide.

To me, two key factors are contributing to that demand. The first is the shortage of skilled trade and technical workers in the U.S. This has been caused, in large part, by several generations that have placed a premium on "traditional" college and university degree programs over vocational learning. The second is the ever-rising cost of such programs, which has made them harder to afford for many Americans, particularly amid rising consumer prices.

These feel like durable mid- to long-term trends, as I don't see the causes behind them melting away anytime soon. I think the education sector will continue to post encouraging growth, and I'd consider its better stocks to be buy candidates -- Lincoln Educational included.

#3026. NH Investors (NHI) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Senior housing now drives 18% of income, but summer occupancy fell short of plans.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

National Health Investors, Inc. (NHI -4.83%) reported a third quarter defined by the completion of its $541.6 million skilled nursing portfolio sale and the subsequent rotation of capital into the senior housing operating segment. Management indicated that the Senior Housing Operating Portfolio now contributes 18% of total net operating income, doubling its share since the beginning of the year. While the same-store portfolio met growth objectives, recently acquired properties experienced operational delays and occupancy growth that trailed management's initial expectations. The company maintained a leverage ratio below its target range while executing $396.2 million in year-to-date investments, positioning the firm for its second largest investment year in company history.

Operator: Good day, everyone, and welcome to the National Health Investors Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Webcast and Conference Call. [Operator Instructions]. It is now my pleasure to hand the floor over to your host, Dana Hambly, Senior Vice President of Finance. Sir, the floor is yours.

Dana Hambly: Thank you, and welcome to the National Health Investors Third Quarter 2026 Conference Call. On the call today are Eric Mendelsohn, President and CEO; Kevin Pascoe, Chief Investment Officer; Todd Siefert, Chief Financial Officer; Chris Maingot, Chief Operating Officer; and David Travis, Chief Accounting Officer. Yesterday, NHI released its third quarter results and conference call information for a press release after market close. Today's remarks may include forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks or uncertainties and are not guarantees of future performance.

Investors are urged to carefully review NHI's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including its Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, and Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, for a discussion of these risks. Copies of these filings are available on the SEC's website at sec.gov or on NHI's website at nhireit.com. In addition, today's call may include certain non-GAAP financial measures, reconciliations of which are provided in NHI's earnings release, which has been furnished to the SEC on Form 8-K. Listeners are encouraged to review those reconciliations provided in the earnings release together with all other information provided in that release. I'll now turn the call over to our CEO, Eric Mendelsohn.

D. Mendelsohn: Good morning, and thank you for joining us. This has been a year of significant transition for NHI. We completed the sale of the NHC portfolio on July 1, substantially reduced our skilled nursing exposure and accelerated our investment in private pay senior housing. Our conviction and SHOP remains strong. We continue to see the most attractive risk-adjusted opportunities for our capital in private pay senior housing, where we believe that the industry backdrop provides powerful and sustained tailwinds for our company. Capturing that opportunity requires both disciplined underwriting and consistent execution. While NHI is focused on the long-term opportunity, we understand the importance of delivering consistent quarterly results.

And in that regard, our third quarter SHOP performance fell short of our expectations. Our 15 same-store properties delivered approximately 19.5% year-over-year NOI growth, consistent with our outlook, but recent performance in the non-same-store communities reduced the contribution we expected from the total portfolio in the quarter. We're not satisfied with those results and are addressing the operating performance with our partners. Our longer-term growth outlook for those properties is unchanged. Chris Maingot, our new COO, will discuss the drivers and our response in more detail. The NHC sale provided $555 million in net proceeds to support NHI's repositioning. We expect to recycle more than 95% of those proceeds before year-end, primarily into SHOP and expected SHOP transition investments.

We've already completed more than $395 million in investments year-to-date and expect significant additional closings during the fourth quarter. Based on that activity, we expect 2026 to be our second largest investment year in the company's history. This portfolio repositioning enhances our growth profile and the portfolio's valuation potential as we redeploy capital from skilled nursing assets into senior housing. By increasing our exposure to SHOP, we participate directly in operating upside and strengthen NHI's long-term growth profile. Including our October acquisition, SHOP now contributes approximately 18% of total NOI compared with 9% entering the year, and we expect that share to grow rapidly as our investment focus is primarily towards SHOP opportunities.

We are executing this strategy from a strong financial position. Our leverage is less than 3x, which is comfortably below the low end of our target range, and we have ample capital available to fund our current pipeline. That flexibility allows us to remain selective to pursue investments that meet our return standards, including low to mid-teens unlevered IRRs. Kevin will provide more details on our investment activity, and Todd will review our financial position and full year guidance. We have also strengthened our executive management team and clarified responsibilities to support a larger operating portfolio.

Chris is leading our asset management team and the build-out of our operating platform, while Kevin is focused entirely on business development and expanding our investment relationship. Together with Todd's financial leadership, this structure gives us greater capacity to grow the portfolio and manage it effectively. We're encouraged by the direction of these changes and our objective remains high single-digit to low double-digit organic SHOP NOI growth. Our priorities are clear: improve the operating performance, deploy capital thoughtfully and build the capabilities to support sustainable growth. We believe the strategy and team are in place, and we recognize that operating results will be the measure of our success.

We are focused on delivering to meet the expectations that we establish and earning your confidence through consistent execution. We have made considerable progress during this transitional year, and I have confidence in the company's strategic direction. I believe NHI is exceptionally well positioned to capitalize on the most attractive senior housing environment that I have experienced in my career. I'm excited about the opportunities ahead. With that, I'll turn the call over to Kevin. Kevin?

Kevin Pascoe: Thank you, Eric, and good morning. I'll begin with our recent investment activity and pipeline, then discuss our business development priorities and the broader investment environment. Year-to-date, we have completed $396.2 million in investments at an average yield of 7.5%. That includes $320 million of SHOP investments at an average year 1 yield of 7.3% after routine CapEx. Our SHOP acquisitions have averaged approximately $223,000 per unit, well below estimated replacement costs, providing an attractive basis for operating growth. We recently completed $51.4 million in investments on 2 properties we previously held $42.3 million in construction loans. Our incremental capital investment was a modest $9 million net of the proceeds of these loan payoffs.

These transactions demonstrate our loan-to-own strategy, allowing us to not only establish strategic relationships during development, but ultimately acquire the completed and stabilized properties. Turning to the pipeline. We currently have $285 million under signed letters of intent, including approximately $190 million that we expect to close during the fourth quarter. Those anticipated closings would bring our total 2026 investment to approximately $590 million. The properties we expect to acquire before year-end will initially be structured under net leases with anticipated conversions to SHOP in 2027. This structure allows us to complete the acquisitions in 2026 within the time frame to our planned Section 1031 exchanges with a clear path for future participation in the operating performance going forward.

Beyond the signed LOIs, we are evaluating approximately $400 million comprised primarily in SHOP. We continue to see active flow of investments and enter 2027 with a substantial pipeline. Our focus is on communities in primary and secondary markets with identifiable opportunities to increase NOI through incremental occupancy gains, pricing growth, expense management and targeted capital investment. We continue to expect high single-digit to low double-digit organic NOI growth, supported by specific operating goals with our operating partners at each property. Existing relationships remain an important source of investment activity. All investments completed year-to-date have been relationship-driven. As our SHOP portfolio expands, we intend to build meaningful scale with select group of operators.

Adding communities to established relationships allows us to leverage prior diligence, supports more efficient asset management and deepens alignment with our operators. Recent interest rate movements have prompted additional discussion and negotiations, although we have not yet seen meaningful change in pricing. If higher financing costs persist, this could moderate competition for acquisitions and make new development more difficult to justify. We believe our access to capital, ability to execute and strong operator relationships position us well as a reliable partner in that environment. We continue to make progress on resolving lingering issues for a subset of the same-store SHOP portfolio where we believe capital could be more productively redeployed. We will provide further details as our plans are finalized.

We are pleased with this year's investment activity and the opportunities ahead. Our priority remains disciplined growth, acquiring communities at an attractive basis, expanding strategic operator relationships and investing where we see the strongest potential for long-term returns. With that, I'll turn the call over to Chris to discuss portfolio performance and our operating initiatives.

Christian Maingot: Thank you, Kevin. It's a privilege to join you today as NHI's Chief Operating Officer. I joined NHI because I believe the company is well positioned to be the capital partner of choice for senior housing operators. Its track record of building long-term relationships, seasoned team, access to capital and growing commitment to SHOP were key factors that attracted me to the company. Over the past 3 months, I've spent considerable time with our team and operating partners getting to know the portfolio. That work has only reinforced my confidence in the opportunity ahead. It has also helped us identify some near-term priorities and opportunities for improvement, which I'll touch on in a moment.

Let me start with our third quarter results. Total SHOP NOI increased 134% through significant contributions from acquisitions over the past 12 months, and the Same-Store portfolio grew NOI 19.5% year-over-year. While the growth was substantial, the quarterly result was below our expectations. Occupancy growth during the summer selling season was slower than we anticipated. It reflected transition-related operating disruptions and slower growth at certain legacy holiday communities. Unusually high onetime expenses at select operators also impacted the quarter. Our immediate priority is improving revenue growth with particular attention to communities where filling vacant units offers the greatest RevPAR opportunity.

We've been working with our operating partners to ensure they have in place fully staffed sales positions, rent-ready inventory, pricing and incentives that align with local market conditions. We also introduced targeted short-term incentives for community teams at select properties to support sales activity. The sequential increase in recurring capital expenditures largely reflected spending to prepare vacant units for occupancy. Having that inventory available is essential to converting tours to move-ins. As we execute on these properties, we see some encouraging signs in occupancy over the past 3 months. Consistent with typical seasonal patterns in senior housing, we expect occupancy to taper as we move through the holiday season.

Move-in incentives and variability in holiday-related expenses may also temper the near-term financial benefit of that progress. At the recently acquired communities, we view these transition-related disruptions as temporary. We continue to believe these investments can perform in line with our underwriting and are working to get performance on the right track. We are currently partnering with our operators to develop the 2027 operating budget and business plans. We entered that process with a clear view of the growth opportunities across the portfolio, the communities that warrant the greatest attention and the actions needed to improve performance. Our approach is tailored to each community and includes identifying revenue-enhancing capital projects and directing resources where we see the greatest potential return.

To support this work, we've also made some changes to our internal organization. We have realigned our asset management team by investment type and functional expertise, establishing separate teams dedicated to SHOP and to triple net and loans with clear responsibilities and expectations for each. Data-driven decision-making will be central to our approach. To support that commitment, we have bolstered our data and analytics team. This team will strengthen our portfolio insights while improving our tools, processes and technologies. By combining community operating data with broader market and customer information, we aim to identify opportunities earlier, work more efficiently and help our team and operating partners improve performance. We are recruiting for several positions to support these efforts.

Over time, I believe this approach can support organic SHOP NOI growth in the high single-digit to low double-digit range. Our priority is improving execution and establishing a more consistent operating trajectory. Turning to triple-net portfolio. The portfolio continues to provide a solid foundation with healthy EBITDARM coverage across the major asset classes. Bickford paid more than $1 million in percentage rent during the quarter, modestly ahead of our guidance assumptions. My first 3 months have only strengthened my confidence in NHI's opportunity. Our focus is on translating that opportunity into consistent operating performance as we grow, and I look forward to doing so alongside our team and operating partners.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Todd to discuss our financial results.

Todd Siefert: Thank you, Chris, and hello, everyone. Interest expense for the third quarter decreased 9% year-over-year due to lower average debt outstanding. Turning to our balance sheet and liquidity. These items are partially offset by stronger performance and expectations elsewhere in the organization compared to our prior guidance. That concludes our prepared remarks. Thank you again for joining us today. Operator, please open the line for questions.

#3024. Kemper (KMPR) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Rate actions lifted margins as management traded policy volume for profitability.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Kemper Corporation (KMPR +3.74%) reported improved sequential underwriting results as rate increases in California and other key markets began earning into the portfolio. Management stated the company is prioritizing profitability and margin restoration over policy growth, leading to an expected decline in policies in force. The company consolidated its distribution and marketing capabilities under a unified leadership team to coordinate lead generation and digital sales across product lines. Management reported that geographic diversification is a priority, with Florida and Texas representing a growing share of the personal auto book to reduce concentration in California.

Operator: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Kemper's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. My name is Jen, and I will be your coordinator today. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded for replay purposes. I would now like to introduce your host for today's conference call, Michael Marinaccio, Kemper's Vice President of Corporate Development and Investor Relations. Mr. Marinaccio, you may begin.

Michael Marinaccio: Thank you. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Kemper's discussion of our third quarter 2026 results. This morning, you'll hear from Steve McAnena, Kemper's President and CEO; and Brad Camden, Kemper's Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. We'll make a few opening remarks to provide context around our third quarter results, followed by a Q&A session. During the interactive portion of the call, our presenters will be joined by John Boschelli, Kemper's Executive Vice President and Chief Investment Officer; Chris Flint, Kemper's Executive Vice President and Chief Distribution and Marketing Officer; Eric Kappler, Kemper's Executive Vice President and Head of P&C; and Jennifer Kopps-Wagner, Kemper's Executive Vice President and Head of Life.

After the markets closed yesterday, we issued our earnings release, filed our Form 10-Q with the SEC and published our earnings presentation and financial supplement.
