#3008. Embraer (EMBJ) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Eve's transition flights advance as Embraer's record backlog keeps growing.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Embraer S.A. (EMBJ +7.05%) reported record revenue for the third quarter and reached an all-time high backlog of $35.7 billion. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue and free cash flow based on performance across all four business segments. The company is currently executing production leveling initiatives to balance delivery volumes throughout the year and is investing in new technologies, including the Eve electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft.

Guilherme Paiva: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and thanks for standing by. My name is Gui Paiva, and I'm the Head of Investor Relations, M&A and Venture Capital for Embraer. Welcome to Embraer's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. Participants on today's conference call are Francisco Gomes Neto, President and CEO of Embraer; Felipe Santana, Chief Financial Officer; Thais Moraes, Corporate Communications Director; and me. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. This conference call will be conducted in English, but please let me say a short announcement for Portuguese speakers. [Foreign Language]. The agenda includes the presentation of third quarter 2026 results, followed by an investor only Q&A session and subsequently, a session exclusively for the press.

Participation instructions will be provided later. We remind participants Eve's results were discussed at the company's conference call last week. Before we begin, a legal notice. This presentation may contain forward-looking statements, which involve risks and uncertainties as detailed in the disclaimer available in the slides and in the documents filed with the Brazilian Securities Commission, CVM and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, SEC. It is a great pleasure to hand the floor to our President and CEO, Francisco Gomes Neto, who will begin the presentation of the company's results. Please, Francisco, go ahead.

Francisco Neto: Thank you, Gui. Good morning and good afternoon, everyone. It is a pleasure to be with you today to discuss Embraer's third quarter '26 results. We delivered record third quarter revenue of $2.3 billion, with revenue and margin expansion across all our businesses. Our backlog reached a new all-time high of $35.7 billion for the eighth consecutive quarter. Based on these results, we are revising up our 2026 revenue and free cash flow guidance. Let me now turn to the key highlights of the quarter. In Commercial Aviation, Farnborough drove 28 firm E2 orders and ANA ordered 8 additional aircraft. In Executive Aviation, we reached a record backlog of $8.2 billion and launched the new Phenom 300EV.

In Defense, Colombia ordered 2 KC-390s while we advanced our partnership with Mahindra, including plans for local assembly line in India. And in Service and Support, we continued expanding our customer agreements. During the quarter, we delivered 22 commercial jets and 41 Executive jets. Total company deliveries increased 6% year-over-year with Commercial Aviation growing 10% and Executive Aviation stable. In Commercial Aviation, we delivered 52 aircraft year-to-date, representing 63% of the midpoint of our full year guidance, 5% points above the 5-year average. In Executive Aviation, we delivered 115 aircraft year-to-date, representing 70% of the midpoint of our full year guidance and a material 10% points above the 5-year average.

These numbers are evidence of our progress in our production leveling initiatives, although we still have room for additional improvement. Our company-wide backlog reached $35.7 billion, up 14% year-over-year and another all-time record for Embraer. All 4 business units increased their backlog year-over-year, led by Defense & Security, up 56% with a strong 2.9 book-to-bill ratio. Executive Aviation backlog grew 12% year-over-year, supported by a 1.4x book-to-bill ratio. Commercial Aviation backlog grew 4% year-over-year, while Services & Support increased 14% with both maintaining book-to-bill ratios above 1x. In addition, we hold approximately $23 billion in options, which could expand our backlog to almost $60 billion if exercised.

With that, I will now hand the call over to Felipe, who will walk you through our financial results. Felipe, the floor is yours.

Felipe Santana de Lima: Thank you, Francisco. Good morning and good afternoon, everyone. I will now talk you through our results by business unit. All comparisons are year-over-year unless otherwise noted. Starting with Commercial Aviation, revenues increased 13% to $696 million, driven by higher volumes and prices. Adjusted EBIT totaled $17 million with a positive 2.4% of margin. The year-over-year improvement was supported by suppliers' compensation. For the fourth quarter, we expect a better customer mix, with full year margins broadly in line with the last year's average. Looking ahead, our ambition is to continue improving Commercial Aviation and profitability to the mid-single-digit level over the next few years.

In Executive Aviation, revenues increased 12% to $655 million, supported by higher prices and product mix. Adjusted EBIT reached $105 million with a positive 16% of margin, circa 130 bps up year-on-year versus a comparison, excluding U.S. tariffs. In Defense & Security, revenues increased 22% to $341 million. Adjusted EBIT was $54 million with a positive 15.7% of margin, driven by higher KC-390 volumes, customer mix and product stage. For the fourth quarter, we do not expect Defense EBIT margins to remain at the strong level seen in the second and third quarters. Still, the division remains on track for another record year, now with profitability around double-digit levels.

Services & Support revenues increased at 30% to $638 million, driven by higher volumes. Adjusted EBIT totaled $108 million with a positive 17% of margin, supported by operating leverage circa 330 bps above year-over-year. At a consolidated level, net revenues increased 17% to $2.35 billion in the third quarter. Revenues were well balanced across our business with Commercial Aviation representing 30%, Executive Aviation, Services more than 25% each and Defense 15%. In the first 9 months, revenues reached $6 billion, representing more than 70% of the midpoint of our full year guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $370 million in the quarter with a positive 13.5% of margin.

Adjusted EBIT reached $255 million with a positive 10.9% of margin compared to 8.6% a year ago or 9.4% if we exclude U.S. import tariffs. The year-over-year improvement was driven by strong operating performance across all the business. In the first 9 months, adjusted EBIT margin reached 10.7% or 4.2 points above the 5-year historical average. Adjusted free cash flow, excluding Eve, was $628 million in the quarter, reflecting sales-related predelivery payments and stronger operating results. Investment totaled $150 million during the quarter as we continue to invest in new technology and support our current projects and future programs. Adjusted net income was $74 million in the quarter, with a 3.1% of margin compared to 4.2% a year ago.

The year-over-year decrease mainly reflects higher financial expenses from the mark-to-market of our long-term incentive plan and higher taxes. Earnings per ADS now stands at $2.2 on a last 12-month basis. We ended the third quarter with a net cash position. Net cash to adjusted EBITDA, excluding Eve improved to a positive 0.4x from a negative 0.5x a year ago. Our average debt maturity ended the quarter at 8.7 years, while the average cost remained at 5.1%. During the quarter, we declared BRL 154 million in interest on equity. This corresponds to BRL 0.22 per share or circa of $0.17 per ADS.

In 2026, we declared BRL 354 million in interest on equity, representing a dividend yield of around 0.52% based on the share price at the quarter end. Also, for our shareholders, in November, we will change our ADS ratio from 4 common shares per ADS to 1 common share per ADS. This change has no impact on our underlying equity value. Last but not least, a quick word about our guidance. From an operational standpoint, we stand by our commitment to deliver 80 to 85 aircraft in Commercial Aviation and 160 to 170 aircraft in Executive Aviation.

From the financial side, we are happy to increase our revenue guidance to between $8.4 billion to $8.6 billion because of the strong performance of our business. The adjusted EBIT margin remains unchanged at between 10% and 10.6%. However, we raised our adjusted free cash flow guidance once again, now to $700 million or higher, supported by better operational performance and cash generation. With that, I will hand it back to Francisco for his closing remarks. Thank you.

Francisco Neto: Thank you, Felipe. I would like to provide a brief update on Eve's continued progress. The flight test campaign continues to advance with 73 flights completed in more than 3 hours of flight time. Following the completion of hover flights, Eve is now advancing through transition flights with full transition expected before year-end. In summary, we continue to see strong demand across our businesses and positive momentum in our global markets. We would like to welcome Japan Airlines to our E2 family, the second operator of our small narrow-body jet in the country and the Hellenic Air Force to our KC-390 family, the seventh operator of our next-generation military aircraft in Europe.

We remain focused on sales, efficiency and execution while continuing to invest in new technologies for the future. Our progress is driven by the trust of our clients, the support of our suppliers and the commitment, discipline and energy of our people. And we are proud to be certified once again as a great place to work. Together, we remain guided by the pillars of our culture and our motto: Safety first, quality always. With that, we are now ready to take your questions.

Operator: We will now start the question-and-answer session. We remind you again that this conference is being recorded. Its broadcast is intended exclusively for the participants of this event and may not be reproduced or retransmitted without the expressed authorization of Embraer. We also highlight that this conference call is being conducted in English with translation to Portuguese. Please let me say a short announcement for Portuguese speakers [Foreign Language]. [Operator Instructions] The first part of the Q&A session will be exclusively for equity research analysts and investors. The second part of the Q&A will be only for the press. The first question comes from Marcelo Motta with JPMorgan.

Marcelo Motta: It's regarding the guidance, if you could comment a little bit about the EBIT margin expected for the fourth quarter. If our math is correct, here, we are talking about maybe a 10.3% margin, which would be a decline of 60 basis compared to the third quarter. And usually, in the fourth quarter, we see higher operational leverage. Felipe commented that the margins on the defense might not remain at the level that we are seeing like the 16% EBIT. So maybe if you can comment about this and why we will not see an expansion of EBIT margin in the fourth quarter given the high operational leverage that quarter?

Felipe Santana de Lima: Marcelo, Felipe here. Thank you for your question. It's important to highlight, right, the production leveling, especially in Executive Aviation, where it's much more balanced throughout the year, right? So when you compare last year with this year, we already see fourth quarter not so -- have so much concentration on deliveries on Executive Aviation. Also important to mention that we're still behind on the production level on Commercial Aviation, given that we'll have a concentration of deliveries on the fourth quarter Commercial Aviation, where the EBIT margin is below the average of the company.

And also on defense, as I mentioned on the slides, we do have this year on the fourth quarter, some annual contract adjustments related to costs, inflation and FX on Brazilian real-denominated contracts. So given that, that's the reason why we reiterate the guidance of 10 to 10.6% of EBIT margin for the full year of 2026.

Operator: The next question comes from Kristine Liwag with Morgan Stanley.

Kristine Liwag: So just a quick follow-up on the services business. You're now at 17% margin, which is a very record margin for the service business. Going forward, is this a new level we should expect for services going forward? And how should we think about the contribution of the Dallas facility once you...

Felipe Santana de Lima: Felipe here. Thank you for your question. Services & Support continues to benefit, right, from higher volumes, operating leverage and the growth of Embraer's installed base. Margins can vary between quarters depending on the mix, but we remain confident in the fundamentals of the business. And it's important to highlight that we still have OGMA for the next year on the ramp-up of the GTF engines. And also, we're going to have the start of Dallas, as you mentioned. So we believe that margins on Services & Support can be better until the end of the decade, close to 17 to 18%.

Operator: The next question comes from Myles Walton from -- with Wolfe Research.

Louis Raffetto: Louis Raffetto on for Myles. Maybe you can just touch on the supplier compensation. It was mentioned within Commercial Aviation, just kind of ballpark how large that was? And then maybe more broadly on the supply chain? Just what are you guys seeing? Any better or worse? Any commentary you could provide?

Guilherme Paiva: Thanks for the question. This is Gui here. The suppliers compensation for the quarter in Commercial was in single-digit levels. As we -- and we didn't disclose the value because we think when we suffer from the supply chain, we absorb the cost. When it benefits from the compensation, it's part of the business. So we think it is a recurring event that we deal with on a daily basis and should be accompanying the results of the division. In terms of the supply chain, we have made material progress in our Executive Aviation leveling of production, moving close to 10 points of production out of Q4. In Commercial Aviation, we have done some progress but still plenty to do.

I think one of the recurring themes has been engine supplies that have impacted us and the industry. But we continue to work with our suppliers to improve the situation, and we do expect Commercial Aviation and Executive Aviation and defense volumes to increase -- continue increasing before the end of the decade.

Operator: The next question comes from Ronald Epstein with Bank of America.

Andrew Steinhardt: This is Andrew Steinhardt on for Ron. I just wanted to ask one on Phenom 300EV triple certification. Congrats on obtaining that during the quarter. Can you talk about the demand environment for that aircraft and its level of contribution to the Executive Aviation's record backlog in the quarter?

Francisco Neto: Sure. So Ron, thanks for the question. Well, the Phenom 300 continues to be our best seller, and we see this going forward. We are now investing to increase production of the Phenoms and the Praetors as well. But we see the production increase in the next years as you know, to cope with sales demand that continues to be strong, even now -- even stronger now with the launch of the EV version.

Andrew Steinhardt: Got you. I appreciate the color there. And if I could just ask a follow-up. What's driving your higher confidence in the free cash flow forecast for the year, just given that much of the other guidance metrics are largely remaining the same?

Felipe Santana de Lima: Felipe here. Thank you for your question. It's important to mention that on the third quarter, we had, especially with the prepayments on -- with the increase of the backlog, especially on defense and also Executive. So given that, we saw more PDPs coming inside the cash of the company. Of course, when we look to the fourth quarter, we are preparing the company on the inventory side for the deliveries next year. So that's the reason why we feel comfortable with the $700 million or higher on the free cash flow for the full year of 2026.

Operator: The next question comes from Andre Ferreira with Bradesco BBI.

Andre Ferreira: Congrats on the results. I wanted to go back to the guidance topic. So the midpoint would imply -- in revenues would imply a 7% year-over-year decline in revenues for the fourth quarter. Of course, there's production leveling, which kind of lowers the amount of deliveries for the fourth quarter. But I wanted to know if this reflects concerns about supply chain at the margining -- worsening compared to the third quarter? Or does it reflect, I don't know, like mix, defense POC timing or maybe some conservatism?

And just a follow-up here on the free cash flow kind of on the opposite end of the last question, if the $700 million floor, if it also looks conservative because the 9 months was almost $600 million already. Any color on that?

Felipe Santana de Lima: Andre, Felipe here. Thank you for your question. So regarding the guidance, right? It's important to mention that you're right regarding the POC of defense. But it's important to highlight that for defense, it will be one of the highest levels of margins on the double digit for the year on defense. Of course, that we -- as I mentioned earlier, we do have the impact on Commercial Aviation, where the EBIT is lower, right, when you compare and we do have a concentration of deliveries there and also with defense. So given that, that's the reason why we see and very comfortable with the guidance that we gave of 10% to 10.6% of margin.

On the free cash flow, as I mentioned also earlier, we are also preparing the company right for 2027, and we're already working on inventory for the deliveries that we're going to have and also connect with the production level, we want to see more deliveries in the first quarter, right, on Executive and also Commercial. So this gives pressure on the cash in the fourth quarter. So that's the reason why we maintain the $700 million of floor for the free cash guidance.

Andre Ferreira: All right. Perfect. Just one point about the revenues, if that also reflects mix of maybe more E1s and more light Executive jets because it also implies a 7% drop at the midpoint.

Felipe Santana de Lima: No. On revenues, the mix is probably in line from what we planned. So nothing different on the mix of the deliveries on Commercial and Executives.

Operator: The next question comes from André Mazini with Citi.

André Mazini: Two quick ones. The first one on the Embraer and Northrop Grumman collaboration for the KC-390 that you guys are developing for the aerial refueling tanker for the U.S. Air Force with the Boom technology and all that. Now with the Democrats controlling both houses, Congress and Senate, can we expect the chance of that going forward may be increasing? So your thoughts on that and that program, in particular, of course, the Boom refueling is developed, which is great. So that's the first one. And the second one, of course, results are pretty strong, congrats. But it was a miss to our net income, mostly on the financial results, right?

And particularly inside the financial results, the stock compensation line item was a little bit greater than what we had. So if you could talk a little bit about that line item and how investors should model that going forward?

Francisco Neto: So thanks, André for the question. So I'll take the first one. We don't see any changes in our plans because of this result of the midterm elections in the U.S. So we really believe we have a great solution for the U.S. Air Force with the KC-390. And we continue to work very closely with Northrop to develop the boom project with them to make the KC-390 a good option for the U.S. Air Force. So no change for us because of the elections.

Guilherme Paiva: André, Gui here. On the second part of your question, as you noticed, our financial expenses were a little bit higher than normal. That was because of the mark-to-market of our long-term incentive program in the company. That is obviously a noncash expense. And from an economic perspective, it is very important to highlight that we do own 28.6 million shares in treasury to hedge our position. So at the end of the day, that's just how accounting works. But from an economic perspective, the company is fully protected from any variation share price up or down.

Operator: The next question comes from Alberto Valerio with UBS.

Alberto Valerio: I have 2 here. The first one, a follow-up on the cash flow generation. You used to see 50% of EBITDA free cash flow. And this year, even excluding the tax refund around $8 million (sic) [ $68 million ], we should see above that. Could you see that for the future? Could this cash flow keep with a ratio higher than 50% of EBITDA? And another one that would be what to do with this cash that the company is very strong at this moment. We know that Eve project is derisked next year, and we should have some announcement of a new program for Embraer in 2027 or something for 2028?

Felipe Santana de Lima: Alberto, Felipe here. Thank you for your question, right? So regarding to the ratio, right, of the free cash flow to EBITDA on the last 5 years, on average, right, we are on 50%. This year, we had, especially with the deals that we had on defense, had some money coming that was expected next year. So probably next year, we're going to see a bit less this ratio. And going forward, we expect to maintain this level of 50%. So the next year, probably below that, but 2028 onwards, around this average, mainly because of defense and the down payments from the customers. And also regarding the cash, right?

So we continue to strengthen the balance sheet of the company. The company was historically net cash. So we're just getting back where we were pre-pandemic and also pre the investments that we had also on E2 and the KCs. And regarding new program, we don't have anything planned. We continue to study something on Executive, Commercial or even defense. So we don't have anything planned of announcement for next year.

Operator: The next question comes from Lucas Laghi with XP.

Lucas Laghi: I have a follow-up on the Executive Aviation division. I mean profitability was a highlight, but we're still seeing a very strong momentum for net new orders. I mean we estimate slightly above the $1 billion of net new order this quarter for the division. So I mean, we understand that there is a lag, right, until the moment that you place the orders until it becomes revenue and EBITDA. But I mean, considering the tightness on the market, I mean profitability is already at high levels, but net new orders continue strong level. So how should we think of the profitability of the division going forward? I mean can it get better than that?

I mean it's already at very strong levels. But considering the strong momentum on orders, I mean, could we still see some room for profitability to further improve considering the list prices that you're selling the aircraft nowadays? And just a follow-up on that, but considering your plans to reach 200 units per year over the upcoming years and considering this very strong demand as we speak, should we expect it anytime sooner? I mean, could you anticipate this expansion of deliveries on the Executive division in the short term?

Guilherme Paiva: Lucas, thanks for the question. It's Gui here. I think not only from Executive Aviation, but if you look across the Board for the company. I think we are in a very special position because when you look at the products that we've manufactured and the engineer has helped us produce, we believe we have a very strong product portfolio across all divisions and that it's generating the value that for our customers and ultimately for our shareholders. So in terms of profitability, the company always continues to strive for being more efficient. That's part of the DNA that we have that we're always going to try to improve our margins and our results.

In terms of volume, we continue to work with a target of reaching 200 units in Executive Aviation in 2028. And part of that effort, we're investing in our facilities. We do expect our CapEx in 2027, '28 to temporarily increase towards $500 million, $550 million before coming back to the regular level of $400 million that we have had in previous years.

Francisco Neto: So Gui, if you allow me to complement or to summarize this, I mean, yes, we do see opportunity to improve profitability of Executive Aviation going forward, combining the launch of new versions that will help us to sustain or even increase the sales price with higher production levels that, as Gui said, we are investing to increase the production, and we continue to invest in improving -- increasing efficiency. So we have been able to reduce the lead time production of our Executive jets year after year. So the combination of all these 3 fronts, we believe will help us to see improvements in the profitability of our Executive Aviation unit, right?

Operator: The next question comes from Daniel Gasparete with Itaú BBA.

Daniel Gasparete: Most of my questions were already answered. So I would like to explore more about the strategy side, if I may. The company has been doing great and looks like it's going to continue doing so over the next few years. So I'd just like to get the ideas from Francisco. What is his planning, what he's thinking about for the company for the next few years in terms of strategy? How he's spending his time thinking about bringing the company to the next level? How he thinks about the strategic position of the company? What the company needs to do?

And also, if I may also ask to Felipe, it has been a few months already as his post of the CFO. Congrats on that. And the company has been doing fantastically well. So just to get his view on what he sees as opportunities here to collect in terms of improving working capital dynamics, perhaps SG&A, how you're seeing efficiencies that could be captured for the company?

Francisco Neto: Daniel, thanks for the question. I'll take the first part. I mean, we see the continuity of our medium-term sustainable growth based on the current backlog of $35.4 billion -- $35.7 billion now. Thank you, Gui. $35.7 billion. And the market is still supporting us. This fuel prices is helping us with the Commercial Aviation as we have the most efficient E-Jets in the market. Executive jets, we see the demand continue to be, I mean, robust with our new launches of the Phenom and the Praetor. And the KC also, we are selling very well.

So we see the company continue to grow sustainably in the next 4 or 5 years as we are investing in increasing production as well for the 3 lines, right? I mean we want to increase the production of E-Jets, Executive jets and the KC-390 and Super Tucano. So in parallel, we are working in 2 big programs that can help us boosting this growth in India, I mean with 2 fronts, Civil Aviation and KC-390 as well. And we have this big opportunity in the U.S. if we succeed to introduce the KC-390 as an agile tanker in the U.S. Air Force.

So -- and in parallel, we are investing in new technologies in preparing the company for a new cycle of products that can be either a new Commercial jet family or Executive jet family or even defense aircraft that will support a more ambition growth in long term for Embraer.

Felipe Santana de Lima: And Gasparete, Felipe here. So thank you for your question. Yes, I see a lot of opportunities on the working capital, right? When we look to the inventory turn where we can reach 3x, right? We are below that. We're around 2.1x this year. So on the working capital and also look to efficiency, right, as a whole for the company, where we have been more efficient on costs and the way that also we're allocating capital as well.

So we see a lot of opportunities really to improve, right, the margins of the company in the coming years and also the financials have been supporting the execution of this backlog, as Francisco mentioned, and also on the strategic initiatives, as we already mentioned as well.

Francisco Neto: And another point that I forgot to mention, Daniel, is that if our eVTOL, right, we're continuing investing in the development, the certification process of our eVTOL, that will be also an important contributor to Embraer revenues and profitability after 2029.

Operator: The next question comes from Ronald Epstein with Bank of America.

Ronald Epstein: Maybe a quick financial question. Year-over-year, it looks like the contract liabilities went up by $450 million. What is that?

Felipe Santana de Lima: It's basically PDPs, Ron. Felipe here. Thank you for your questions. It's basically PDPs, right? You see this increase on the backlog that we are seeing, right? And it's a reflection also on this account on the balance sheet with the PDPs that we're receiving on the customers.

Ronald Epstein: Okay. So that's just all predelivery payments. Okay. Good.

Ronald Epstein: And then what is the quarterly spend on Eve?

Guilherme Paiva: So Ron, their guidance is about $225 million, if I remember correctly. So the run rate that you are doing something close to $50 million, $55 million.

Ronald Epstein: Got you. Got you. Got you. Got you.

Guilherme Paiva: And the -- just as some milestones, right, the company expects to achieve full transition for the prototype before year-end. We're going to be building 6 prototypes through the first half of '27. And we intend to start the flight campaign for the certification in the mid of '27 and finishing in '28.

Ronald Epstein: Got it. Got it. Got it. And then has there been any more discussion internally? You're thinking about what the next move is for you all in Commercial Aviation?

Francisco Neto: Actually, we don't have any news, important news on that front, Ron. We continue making studies, which way we should go. I mean, as a next cycle of products, we have an engineering team, the marketing team is making a lot of studies and combining with the funding strategy and the customers' conversations, we don't have any decision yet, which way we will go. But we keep investing in new technologies to be prepared for a new cycle of products.

Operator: Next question comes from Kristine Liwag Morgan Stanley.

Kristine Liwag: So with Ron's question about the potential new aircraft and the studies that you're doing, I mean, it sounds like with the full transition for Eve happening by year-end this year, you're really derisking that program. And so the opportunity for the next big project could come pretty soon. It seems like you've got capacity opening up maybe for engineers second half of '27, maybe into '28. So that seems to be more on the horizon. So I wanted to ask Francisco, when you think about the opportunities, either in a potentially larger narrow-body or a larger business jet or something in military or all the other investments that you have, what are the key priorities that you're looking at?

What are the variables that you're weighing? And when you think about some of these endeavors, what's your appetite to go do it alone in terms of a project that has a high ROI, but it is not too expensive versus going for challenging a duopoly, which might take more company resources? How do you balance those opportunities?

Francisco Neto: Kristine, thank you very much. This is really a great question. But just for you to know, our engineering has been very busy, and will be very busy with not only with EV. EV is one of the projects we are working on, but they have been busy, I mean, in doing updates on the existing products. Like, for example, we are now in the certification process of the E2TS for the E2 that is a unique feature that we offer to the market, this autonomous takeoff of a commercial jet. Also, we have hundreds of engineers, I mean, busy with update on the specification of the KC-390 that we are selling. Now each deal requires a different specification.

Also, we are now working to update our Super Tucano. So we have a lot of engineers working in this update of the cockpit of the Super Tucano with this new feature as a Drone...

Francisco Neto: Exactly. So thank you, Gui. So again, we -- our engineering is very busy. But we have -- I mean, some of them working, making studies, as I said, about new opportunities for Embraer either in Commercial Aviation or Executive. But Kristine, yes, we are taking into consideration all the aspects. One thing we won't -- we will not do is to put in risk the financial health of our company.

So the next movement will be based on a very robust decision in terms of customer acceptance, in terms of funding, in terms of product and especially, I mean, the chances we will have to succeed with the new product without putting risk what we have built in terms of financial health in the company.

Guilherme Paiva: Kristine, and just to complement what Francisco said, we don't think it will be prudent to have 2 big CapEx fronts happening at the same time. So we have to materially derisk Eve as a project before we take the next step. And part of that derisking process, I would highlight, first the full transition flight at year-end; and second, the first manned flights for the prototype that we expect to happen in the second half of '27.

Kristine Liwag: Great. Great. Super helpful. And then also back to Services & Support, I think this is one of your sleeper segments because I think investors don't realize how large of an aftermarket business you now have as a proportion for total EBITDA. In terms of that Services & Support business, you give us an understanding regarding backwards looking. What did you change in your strategy to be able to grow this business more? Was it really more of a function of the larger installed base? Or did you do something different to increase your capture rate? I mean you're clearly making investments there as we've seen with OGMA and Dallas.

How do we think about your overall strategy in this business? And did this continue to be a faster grower for EBIT for the company. I mean, the margin upside here in the quarter was just a significant standout, right? So just wanted to understand the sustainability of that.

Francisco Neto: Thank you, Kristine. It's another great question. Yes, I mean, you were totally right. I mean we are growing a lot in commercial executive and defense. But we see our Services & Support area as one of the most important growth avenues for Embraer. So we are investing to grow the -- to expand our capabilities to do more service for commercial jets as the commercial jet fleet is growing. Same in the executive jets. We are now, I mean, reviewing the structure to be even more focused on sales and customer support. We are now implementing a lot of AI tools to help us to be more efficient and more customer friendly.

So we are doing a lot of investments in that area because we do believe that they are going to contribute a lot with the profitable growth of Embraer within the following years.

Felipe Santana de Lima: If I can add here also, Francisco, also investment in simulators and training, right? That is also good margins. And with this increase, especially the increase of sales of E2s, we're investing now installed bases of simulators around the world to support our customers as well.

Operator: Next question comes from Marcelo Motta with JPMorgan.

Marcelo Motta: Just if you can comment on commercial campaigns. No one has asked about it, but there are news about KLM, Brussels, India Go (sic) [ IndiGo ]. I know that you don't comment about specific campaigns, but if you can just remind us how positive you are about the future of the E2, let's say, for the next 6 months, what you expect on new orders or book-to-bill? That would be great.

Francisco Neto: Thank you, Marcelo. Yes. We are very happy now with the development of our Commercial Aviation, in terms of sales and also EBITDA recovery plan as we expect to be at a 5% EBIT until 2028. So -- and since 2024, we have seen the sales of E2 getting traction with a great year in '25, another great year in '26. We are now very pleased with KLM plans to expand the E2 fleet operated by KLM Cityhopper. So I mean -- as I mean, we see the customers, airlines recognizing more and more. I mean the benefits of having the -- our small narrow-body complemented the operation of the larger narrow-bodies.

So we see this in Europe, we see this in South America, in North America, Asia-Pacific. So I mean -- and we are still working on other campaigns. So we -- yes, we are very optimistic now with the development of our Commercial Aviation, not only in revenues, but also in EBITDA recovery.

Operator: Next question comes from André Mazini with Citi.

André Mazini: So my additional question is around Executive Aviation pricing. Of course, great margins on that business. And you also comment on improved pricing, right? I mean the jets delivered currently are having very good prices. That's why margins are so good, of course, on top of the production leveling and whatnot. However, if you look at some industry data sets, it seems that on the margin, prices are not as high as they were probably 12 or 18 months ago. So I think the question is, is the pricing of what's being delivered today, which is making these margins be so high?

Is it kind of older prices, if you will, and at the very margin, jets that are sold today are not having the buoyant prices we saw 12, 18 months ago, or at the margin, it's still growing, right? So what's the picture of the margin of these jets that are being sold right now?

Guilherme Paiva: Thanks for the question, Gui here. So at the end of the day, we do believe that we have one of the best products in Executive Aviation in the segments that we that we play in, and that's the value that we drive to our customers and eventually to our shareholders. We're very pleased with the results the division has had in this decade. There is a lag in pricing, as you mentioned, of roughly 2 to 3 years given the success of our products and the demand that we have seen from our products.

And we don't know exactly what data set you are referring to, but we are optimistic about the profitability and the growth that we have in the division for the next couple of years.

Operator: The next question comes from the chat with Lucas Barbosa with Santander. Congratulations on the results. My question is regarding the risk of high oil prices and higher rate environment and globally. Is the company seeing any request from customers to postpone deliveries because of these factors? And does management expect any impact from them in upcoming years?

Francisco Neto: Well, Lucas, thanks for the question. Well, first, we have not seen any impact, I mean, in our -- either in terms of delay of deliveries or delay of sales campaigns because of the fuel price. What we have seen is that the market has been resilient. And actually, it opens an opportunity for the E2s as E2s are very efficient, fuel efficient compared to older aircraft. And it's a great alternative for the airlines, I mean, to add more flights, frequency of flights or open new routes and improving their performance, I mean adding so more efficient aircraft to their fleets.

So again, we have not seen any impact in our business either in terms of deliveries or new campaigns.

Operator: Thank you very much, sir. This concludes the question-and-answer session for equity research analysts and investors. Now we will start the Q&A session dedicated to the press. [Operator Instructions]. The first question comes from Ioannis Rekkas with flight.com.gr. What are your plans for cooperation with Greece regarding the decision for 3 KC-390 with an additional option for 3 more and the fact that the Hellenic Ministry wants 25% domestic production for every new procurement.

Francisco Neto: Well, thanks for the question. So we are very happy, and we welcome Greece to the KC-390 family with this order for 3 with options for additional 3. So we will work with Greece as we do with the other customers. I mean, with a collaboration in terms of training, in terms of Services & Support to make sure that the operation of the KC-390 in Greece will be very successful. So that's what we are planning to do with that customer.

Operator: [Operator Instructions]. The next question is also from the chat with Jonathan Hemmerdinger. Embraer had previously hoped to have the E2TS system certificate by the end of 2025. Why has that process taken longer than expected? When do you expect certification will happen?

Francisco Neto: So thank you, Jonathan, for your question. Yes, we continue working with the authorities, the local authorities to certify the E2TS and we expect the certification to happen soon as we have already some customers, I mean, very interested in that function in their aircraft.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] The next question comes also from the chat with Jack Richardson as a freelance. Could you provide an update on what, if any, progress you have made on the Eve for military applications?

Francisco Neto: Thank you for the question. At this point of time, we are focusing on the original objective, original purpose for Eve, that is urban air mobility. So we are really advancing the certification process. And in parallel, we are making some studies, but we don't have any definition to launch a variant of Eve at this point of time.

Operator: [Operator Instructions]. The next question comes also from the chat, and it is from Molly McMillin from Aviation Week. You mentioned that you had not seen delays or cancellations because of higher fuel prices and mentioned Commercial Aviation specifically. What have you seen in Executive Aviation? Also, what are you planning for timing in new product upgrades and products in Executive Aviation?

Francisco Neto: Thank you, Molly, for the question. Well, I mean, honestly, in Executive Aviation, I think this -- the demand depends more on the wealth creation than on the fuel price. So that's why we have not seen any impact in the demand of our executive jets because of the fuel price increase. And the other question was?

Francisco Neto: New product. Well, we have launched this year the new version of the Praetors, the Praetor 500E and 600E and more recently of the Phenom 300EV. So both with the new features that have been very well accepted and received by the market.

Operator: The next question comes from also the chat, and it's from Caroline Bruno. Can you give -- can you please give us an update on your supply chain? Boeing and Airbus have problems with theirs, but yours seem more robust. Can you elaborate on this?

Francisco Neto: Yes, Caroline, absolutely. Well, we also have a problem with supply chain. But well, in general, we have been able to manage to reduce the shortages of parts by approximately 25% when we compare, I mean, 2026 versus 2025 despite the growth in the company's delivery volume. But we also have -- we still have some, I would say, we call pacers. We have -- we are still having issues with specific components as engines, as fuselage parts, as windshields and some other components. But I mean, a few components that, yes, they have impacted our production process.

But at the end, we have been able to manage and may be in line and delivering the production according to our guidance.

Operator: This concludes the question-and-answer session in English for the press. [Operator Instructions] [Foreign Language]. The first question comes from Nelson Düring from DefesaNet. Francisco, could you talk about competition for KC-390 in India, please?

Francisco Neto: Nelson, competition in India will be fierce because it's based on price, ultimately. We really believe that KC-390 are the best option for the India Air Force (sic) [ Indian Air Force ] because of its characteristics, because it's a more modern product. It has new technologies and their operating costs are highly optimized compared to those of the competition. But as I said, it is ultimately a competition based on price. So it's going to be hard. It's going to be tough, and we are getting ready for that bidding process.

Operator: The next question is also from the chat from Xandu Alves from Jornal do Vale. Francisco, you mentioned Embraer is getting ready for a new product cycle. Could you explain what that means, please? Is it a new family of commercial jets, maybe bigger aircraft? What about in executive and defense? Could you elaborate please?

Francisco Neto: Well, thank you for the question, Xandu. We haven't yet defined what the new product cycle will look like for Embraer. Right now, we are conducting studies. We're assessing the market, talking to clients, talking to suppliers, conducting studies, talking to funding sources, strategic partners so that we can make a decision on how we're going to move forward in the long term, whether we're going to have a new family of executive jets or commercial aircraft, we haven't yet decided on what kind of aircraft or what size yet or if we're going to have a new defense product. That's where Embraer is at the moment.

Operator: The next question is from Bruno Andrade from Veja.

Bruno Andrade: I have a couple of questions. I sent my questions through the chat, but I'll ask them here. What will be the military aircraft front for the next 2 years, '27, '28? Do you see new countries coming into your portfolio? Also, what do you expect in terms of growth for services and support? You mentioned that you wanted to be a relevant line. How can it grow over the next few years? So those are my 2 questions.

Francisco Neto: Thank you for the questions, Bruno. In defense, the KC aircraft line, yes, there is plenty of opportunity and new potential clients for KC-390s. It's a relatively new product, KC-390s went into service in 2019. And since then, we've sold more than 70 aircraft, most of which have been to other countries. Greece has been the latest and the seventh European country to adopt KC-390. We sold it to Asia, to South Korea, to Central Asia, Uzbekistan and South America, we recently announced Colombia. So there are plenty of opportunities for this aircraft globally, including these 2 major projects, India, between 60 and 90 aircraft and the U.S.

Air Force, which is one of the largest clients for that kind of aircraft in the world. So there are plenty of future opportunities for the aircraft in Services & Support, as I mentioned during the presentation. That is one of the major avenues for growth for Embraer because fleets are growing. So the services -- the demand for services and parts also grows. And we also have a new agnostic front, which is engine revisions being conducted by our company in Portugal, OGMA. We have a multibillionaire agreement for GTF engine revisions and the subsidiary is growing a lot.

It was worth USD 230 million, USD 240 million in revenue, and we expect it to get up to $600 million by 2030. So those 2 fronts will be leveraging services, which is a very profitable area for Embraer. Not only in terms of finance but also because it ensures client satisfaction, and it opens the door to new sales for clients.

Bruno Andrade: So you mentioned $600 million by when?

Operator: The next question is from Marcelo Rocha from Radio Station CBN. Mr. Rocha's question is in the chat box. So I'm going to read it. So CEO, Francisco Gomes Neto, Boeing has opened positions for engineers in Brazil, including São José dos Campos, which is where the headquarters for Embraer are. There are new opportunities for November. In 2022, the same situation caused some discomfort between the companies. Now that Embraer is projecting market growth and an increase in the backlog. How worrying is it to lose experienced engineers -- the potential to lose engineers to the competition? Does the company have enough professionals for that growth? And how long does it take to train a qualified engineer?

Francisco Neto: Thank you for the question, Marcelo. Actually, the whole industry is growing. Embraer is growing and so is the competition. So it's only natural that there is an increased demand for qualified professionals. I would say that we have enough engineers for the time being. We have a lot of work for them. That's what engineers love, new projects and opportunities to take part in developing new processes, new systems, new aircraft. So we're doing very well, and we are totally prepared for the company's future growth supported by qualified engineers, which are renowned worldwide.

Operator: Next question is also from the chat from João Sorima from O Globo. How are the talks with the U.S. government in terms of KC-390 acquisitions? Any progress?

Francisco Neto: Yes. We are working with the authorities and the whole U.S. defense ecosystem to show them the benefits of introducing a modern aircraft like KC-390s. But we all know this is a project for the mid- to the long run. We won't be seeing any results in the short term. But we are very optimistic because it's a great opportunity. There are 49 KC-390 suppliers in America. So more than 50% of the content of the aircraft is produced in the U.S. It's a fantastic aircraft for the U.S. Air Force. The first project includes 1 tank (sic) [ tanker ] supplier for jet -- fighter jets.

It's an agile tank (sic) [ tanker ], and it can open the door to KC-390s and it's a great option for the U.S. Air Force for other missions. So yes, we are making progress. But as of yet, nothing has been defined in the short term to buy the aircraft.

Operator: Thank you, Mr. Gomes. Ladies and gentlemen, we now conclude the Q&A session and the earnings release conference call for Embraer. Thank you for joining us, and have a great day.

#3006. What to expect from the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers

NBA fans have been waiting for November 10 since the NBA schedule was released in August. From the moment Brad Stevens opted to trade Jaylen Brown away from the Boston Celtics to a conference rival, the Philadelphia 76ers, you knew the two sides were on a collision course. Now, Brown is set to face off against his old team on his new home court for the first time since that trade went down.

On paper, the Sixers have the stronger roster. Nick Nurse is coaching a starting five comprised of multiple future Hall of Famers, including two former MVPs, LeBron James and Joel Embiid. On the opposite side of the floor, Joe Mazzulla is working with a retooling roster comprised of veteran talent and young, high-upside developmental pieces such as Hugo Gonzalez and Jordan Walsh.

There are a lot of differences between where each team is in terms of its development and timeline. However, once the game gets underway, all of that will go out of the window, and all eyes will be on the matchup between Jayson Tatum and Brown. The former teammates will undoubtedly take turns guarding each other at points during the game, and will likely feel they need to prove something, both to the fans in the arena and those watching from home.

In a recent discussion that has been posted to the "NBA on the NBC" YouTube channel, Ahmed Fareed, Brian Scalabrine, and Frank Isola discussed the upcoming matchup between Boston and Philadelphia and what we can expect to see on the court. Tatum and Brown were undoubtedly at the forefront of that discussion, but they weren't the only factors the trio pinpointed, with both teams having things to focus on and areas to try to avoid.

#2997. Investors are doing just as well this year by shunning AI. How to invest if the tech trade keeps fizzling

A version of the S&P 500 without AI briefly pulled ahead of the traditional index this year and is now neck-and-neck as investors rotate into other areas of the market.

A proprietary Goldman Sachs index tracking the S&P 500 without stocks classified as "AI enablers" was up 12.4% through Oct. 22, edging ahead of the standard S&P 500's 12% gain. The Goldman index is now neck-and-neck with the S&P 500 as tech rallied in Monday trading.

Tech and AI-related companies make up about 45% of the S&P 500. That heavy weighting has helped power the index for years, but it's turned into a liability lately; the S&P 500 tech sector is down about 7% this month while other sectors have held up.

Investors have soured on debt and equity issued by companies like CoreWeave and Oracle. Shares of Meta Platforms sank almost 7% Thursday after it outlined more plans to spend heavily on capex and issue additional shares.

Companies supplying power and equipment for the buildout have been hit hard — names like GE Vernova, Bloom Energy, Vistra and Quanta Services all suffered steep declines during the recent selloff.

Goldman, which launched the measure earlier this year with S&P, uses the S&P 500 as its starting universe and excludes companies perceived to be enablers of AI before applying S&P 500 Index weighting methodology to the remaining universe of companies.

The ex-AI index lagged the S&P 500 for most of the year as investors continued to favor chipmakers, cloud-computing companies and other firms benefiting from heavy AI spending. However, that advantage has been narrowing and it disappeared last week.

Meanwhile, investors are rotating into defensive areas. ETFs like State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF, State Street Health Select SPDR ETF and State Street Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF are up 7% to 10% this month. Energy is ahead 10% too, though that's more related to the war in Iran.

Some analysts recommend sticking with non-AI companies for diversification and protection against more pain in tech. The "AI pendulum has swung back in favor of non-AI exposure over the last two weeks," Oppenheimer technical analyst Ari Wald said in a note on Oct. 24.

Two industries that Oppenheimer favors now are commercial services and insurance. The firm upgraded those industries to overweight last week, recommending Republic Services, Cintas, Verisk Analytics, Broadridge Financial Solutions, MetLife and Arthur J. Gallagher.

Berkshire Hathaway is also capitalizing on the rotation out of tech. Its Class B shares are up 8% this month, though it's still lagging behind the S&P 500 this year.

Berkshire owns a wide swath of operating companies, including insurance giant Geico and Burlington Northern Santa Fe railroad. It also has a $364 billion stock portfolio including companies like Apple, Coca-Cola, Alphabet and Bank of America. That diversification may help Berkshire continue to outperform if the tech sector drags down the S&P 500.

Trivector Research sees potential in "non-tech compounders." Healthcare giant Eli Lilly is one idea. The stock is up 22% on the strength of Lilly's weight-loss drugs. The company has more in the pipeline, including a next-generation obesity drug that Lilly plans to file for FDA approval early in 2027.

Viking Holdings, a cruise operator, is also proving durable. The company said on its August earnings call that 40% of its river capacity and 60% of its ocean capacity was already booked for 2027. "Based on recent events, we've seen our guests have proved to be resilient and are continuing to book 2027 and future seasons," the company told investors.

Viking stock is up 15% this year but it may still have upside. The average Wall Street target is $109, above recent prices around $82. Barclays recently upgraded the cruise operator to overweight with a $102 target, citing the company's "compelling risk/reward."

For release at 2:30 p.m. EDT Share

The Federal Reserve Board on Thursday requested public comment on two proposals related to establishing a regulatory framework for Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act.

The first proposal would require that Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers fully back their stablecoins with certain permissible reserve assets, such as short-term Treasury bills and certain other high-quality, liquid assets. The proposal would also establish standardized capital requirements to address certain credit and operational risks of payment stablecoin activities, as well as risk management standards, in accordance with the law. Separately, the proposal would introduce rules for Board-supervised firms that safekeep the assets backing payment stablecoins. It would also clarify the permissibility of stablecoin and related activities for Board-supervised banks.

The second proposal would establish a tailored application process for Board-supervised banks applying to issue payment stablecoins. These applicants would be required to submit a business plan and financial information, among other documents. The proposal would also create a process governing appeals, hearings, and final determinations for applications.

The comment period will close 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

#2981. Federal Reserve Board finalizes changes to enhance the transparency and public accountability of its stress test and reduce volatility in its stress test-related capital requirements

An official website of the United States Government

Official websites use .govA .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States.

Secure .gov websites use HTTPSA lock (LockLocked padlock icon) or https:// means you've safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites.

The Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States, provides the nation with a safe, flexible, and stable monetary and financial system.

Review of Monetary Policy Strategy, Tools, and Communications

Mergers, Acquisitions, and Other Applications

Financial Stability Coordination & Actions

Financial Market Utilities & Infrastructures

For release at 9:00 a.m. EDT Share

The Federal Reserve Board on Wednesday finalized changes to enhance the transparency and public accountability of its stress test and reduce volatility in its stress test-related capital requirements. The two final rules are largely similar to the proposed rules from 2025. The Board also requested comment on a proposal to better capture differences in banks' business models to generate fee income.

The Board conducts stress tests to ensure that large banks are sufficiently capitalized and able to lend to households and businesses even in a severe recession. In December 2024, the Board announced it would modify the test to improve its resilience.

"The stress test is an essential component of our regulatory capital framework," said Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman. "Today's changes preserve its resilience by ensuring that it is transparent, granular, and risk-sensitive. The public will now have greater assurance that the risks banks take will be reflected appropriately in their stress test losses and their capital requirements."

The first final rule requires the Board to invite public input annually on the stress test scenarios and any material model changes. It also updates the framework that guides the design of the hypothetical scenarios and adopts the models that will be used for the 2027 stress test. In addition, the final rule makes several adjustments to the stress test calendar. The final rule also updates the global market shock component, which is a set of shocks to specific market components applied to banks with large trading books. These banks will now be tested against two global market shock components each year, and the Board will use the shock that produces the largest losses for each firm to calculate the firm's stress test results.

The second final rule requires the Board, when calculating stress capital buffer requirements, to average the results from the two most recent annual supervisory stress tests for firms subject to the stress test in both years. The Board will begin averaging stress capital buffer requirements in 2028 to ensure that only models incorporating public input are used in the calculation.

The proposal would request public comment on a revision to the Board's noninterest income model that would improve the stress test's ability to capture business model diversity across firms. If adopted, these adjustments would replace the current noninterest income model that projects each bank's fee income under stress. Comments are due 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

Together, the changes are likely to reduce year-over-year volatility in capital requirements by approximately 50 percent and are not expected to materially affect aggregate capital requirements.

#2980. Columbia coach Megan Griffith returns from suspension for big game vs. Michigan

Without head coach Megan Griffith on the sidelines for its first three games of the season, the Columbia women's basketball team didn't just survive — it thrived.

The Lions went 3-0 against Davidson, Rhode Island and Belmont, a trio of squads that ranked in the top 110 of NET last year, a metric the NCAA uses to sort teams. Columbia won those games by an average margin of 13.3 points with associate coach Tyler Cordell making the in-game decisions and adjustments.

"Yeah, she should just take my job," Griffith said with a laugh during a Zoom call with reporters. "What I loved about it was how she just jumped right into it. I think Ty really understood the game planning aspect from my standpoint and how I think about it, and she put her spin on it. Which for her, that is so easy because she built the program with me."

Griffith is now back on the sidelines for Columbia following a three-game suspension, returning to the lead chair on the bench for perhaps the toughest stretch of the Lions' schedule. On Thursday, Nov. 12, they'll host No. 2 Michigan at Levien Gymnasium in New York City, travel to No. 18 Maryland on Sunday, Nov. 15, then host No. 5 Duke on Saturday, Nov. 21.

Columbia announced it was suspending Griffith — an alum of the Ivy League institution who is in her 10th season leading the Lions — in October following a review of the program by an outside firm after the university received a complaint about her behavior during practices from past seasons.

In a statement, Columbia said the review did not require notice to the NCAA of any rules violations and did not involve any allegations of violations of the university's anti-discrimination policies, Title IX or related policies. According to the statement, "Griffith expressed regret for the times in which her interactions with the team did not align with the university's expectations."

USA TODAY Sports was provided with a statement from current Columbia players, too. They said they "fully stand with and support" Griffith and that the complaint was "not indicative of our experience as part of this program."

During a call with reporters on Tuesday, Nov. 10, Griffith didn't discuss the reasoning behind her suspension, but talked about the positives that she took away from it.

"What a unique experience this has been. The biggest benefit was, I think, bringing my staff into how I game plan and think about the game, bringing our players more deeply into it, and then I got to watch a lot and coach the details of the game in a very different way," Griffith said. "I got to observe from a very different vantage point of a game. And obviously, that's not what I wanted. You want to be with your team, right?

"But it was a great opportunity to learn in a different way, and I think our team and my staff did a phenomenal job of stepping up and battling together."

Griffith, 41, played at Columbia from 2003-2007 and was a two-time All-Ivy League selection. After playing professionally in Europe, she joined the coaching ranks by becoming an assistant for Courtney Banghart at Princeton during a stretch where the Tigers made three NCAA Tournaments.

In 2016, Griffith took the reins at her alma mater and has turned Columbia into a consistent mid-major power. In the last five seasons, the Lions were 125-35 with three regular season Ivy League titles, two at-large NCAA Tournament appearances, a runner-up finish in the WNIT in 2023 and a WBIT championship last season. Columbia also won an NCAA Tournament game in 2025, defeating Washington in the First Four.

The March Madness bids and victory — and the WBIT title — were the first in Columbia's history. The program that Griffith has turned the Lions into is one that Power 4 teams and national title contenders are willing to play in the non-conference slate now, because they know Columbia will provide a competitive game and a sufficient measuring stick.

And for Columbia, pulling off an upset in one of these games can be the bullet point on the resume it needs to secure a berth in March Madness.

"It's a gauntlet. I love a challenge," Griffith said. "We have to prove a resume for March. Not that March hinges on (these games), but it gives you another chance, right? So, very intentionally, we always look for a couple of these Quad 1 games.

"Teams like Michigan, teams like Duke, they're not afraid to play anywhere. Those are teams trying to prepare themselves for hostile environments and playing against strong teams. I think that's just a good sign of a program that's really trying to test themselves for March and make a deep run."

Led by reigning Ivy League Player of the Year Riley Weiss, Columbia also brought back key contributors in Mia Broom, Fliss Henderson and 6-foot-3 German forward Hilke Feldrappe. Through the transfer portal, former Big Ten Rookie of the Year Mary Ashley Stevenson has also joined Columbia this season after spending one season apiece at Purdue and Stanford.

"They can turn it on when they want. I think we need to realize they can turn it on more. I think we're sometimes assessing the game and I'm like, 'Impose yourself. Be tone-setters,'" Griffith said. "I just want to see what we're made of a little bit more, right? Let's really test ourselves. We're throwing ourselves fully into the fire here."

To have a chance against a pair of teams in Michigan and Duke that made the Elite Eight last season and a consistent winner in Brenda Frese's Maryland, Columbia will need to push itself to play at its very best.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Columbia coach Megan Griffith returns from suspension for big game vs. Michigan

#2979. Prediction market traders say an Anthropic IPO is near-certain this year after company filed with SEC

Anthropic on Monday unveiled its Form S-1 filing, taking the company one step closer to completing its long-awaited move to the public markets, which is now seen as almost guaranteed to come this year.

Speculators on prediction market platform Kalshi place 95% odds that the artificial intelligence giant officially announces an initial public offering by the end of 2026.

Kalshi defines officially announcing an IPO as either the Securities and Exchange Commission declaring an S-1 effective, a priced IPO or an exchange assigning a ticker to a stock.

The Anthropic S-1 envisions a Nasdaq Stock Market ticker symbol of "ANT."

Anthropic is aiming to start trading the week of Nov. 16, according to a report in the Wall Street Journal. Traders on Kalshi place just a 14% chance that the company begins trading before then.

On the Polymarket platform, traders give a 69% chance that Anthropic will list on a public exchange and open for trading by Nov. 20.

#2972. Terms of trade for Andre Cisco changed; here's what Lions sent Jets

In their original announcement of the trade, the Detroit Lions said they had sent a sixth-round draft pick in 2028 to the New York Jets to acquire safety Andre Cisco.

Those terms have since been updated, according to the NFL's transaction wire Tuesday, Nov. 10. The Lions instead sent the Jets their sixth-round draft pick in 2029.

"All other conditions of the trade remain unchanged," the transaction wire read.

More: Lions quiet at trade deadline after earlier move for Andre Cisco

Detroit's move for Cisco, 26, was its only in-season trade in 2026. Lions coach Dan Campbell said Monday, "We've liked Cisco from afar. ... He's athletic, he's versatile, he knows our system, he knows the verbiage, so we feel like this is a guy that can help us here a little bit. We're excited."

Cisco has been playing under Jets head coach Aaron Glenn since 2025, allowing him to be familiar with Detroit's defense. Glenn was the defensive coordinator with the Lions from 2021-24, and his influence remains through current defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, who Glenn mentored.

Heading into the Boston Celtics matchup against the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday, November 10, all eyes will be on the potential matchup between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. After all, the two All-Stars spent nine years establishing themselves as one of the best duos in the NBA, winning a championship in 2024, only for Brown to be traded earlier this summer.

Brown wasn't the only player to change teams during that trade, though. Paul George was shipped to Boston to make the salaries work, and is already looking like an ideal fit next to Tatum and within Joe Mazzulla's system. In fact, both George and Brown have enjoyed strong starts to their life with their respective new teams, and on Tuesday, both will likely be motivated to prove the opposing team wrong for parting ways with them.

Once you factor in the deep rivalry between Philadelphia and Boston, and the presence of long-time Celtics enemy LeBron James, you have some can't-miss television that will appeal to die-hards and casual fans alike.

In a recent video uploaded to YouTube by 98.5 The Sports Hub, Chris Gasper joined Mike Felger and Tony Massarotti to discuss the upcoming Celtics and Sixers game, looking at multiple angles that will draw attention, both leading into the game and throughout the night itself. #2957. Former New York Yankees 32-Year-Old Abruptly Released By New Team

NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JUNE 19: Anthony Misiewicz #58 of the New York Yankees in action against the Baltimore Orioles at Yankee Stadium on June 19, 2024 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) Getty

NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JUNE 19: Anthony Misiewicz #58 of the New York Yankees reacts after an out against the Baltimore Orioles during the ninth inning at Yankee Stadium on June 19, 2024 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) Getty

The New York Yankees had another strong regular season in 2026, as they had a 93-68 record.

However, New York once again had a very frustrating postseason. This is because they were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. The Yankees are facing a big offseason because of it.

Now, with the offseason just beginning, a former Yankees pitcher has hit the free agent market.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – JUNE 19: Anthony Misiewicz #58 of the New York Yankees in action against the Baltimore Orioles at Yankee Stadium on June 19, 2024 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images)

Former Yankees pitcher Anthony Misiewicz has been released by the Cincinnati Reds.

"LHP Anthony Misiewicz has elected free agency," MLB.com reported.

Misiewicz becoming a free agent comes after he spent this season in the Reds' minor league system. In 48 games with Triple-A Louisville, the former New York pitcher posted a 3-3 record, a 3.23 ERA, and 40 strikeouts.

Misiewicz did not make an MLB appearance for the Reds during the 2026 season.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – JUNE 19: Anthony Misiewicz #58 of the New York Yankees reacts after an out against the Baltimore Orioles during the ninth inning at Yankee Stadium on June 19, 2024 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images)

The Yankees claimed Misiewicz off waivers from the Detroit Tigers during the 2023 season. From there, the 32-year-old spent two seasons with New York.

In four games with New York from 2023 to 2024, Misiewicz posted a 1-0 record, a 2.45 ERA, and three strikeouts.

Misiewicz spent most of this time with the Yankees organization down in Triple-A, though. He had a 3-1 record and a 3.91 ERA in 19 games for Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre in 2023. He then followed that up by posting a 3-2 record and a 3.90 ERA in 47 games with the Triple-A club in 2024.

Misiewicz's time with New York officially ended following the 2024 season when he elected free agency.

#2956. As AI becomes more fractured, one name stands out: AMD

As Anthropic rushes to takes its shares public, the AI trade is showing cracks, and they are not confined to fringe players.

We recently wrote about CoreWeave, which fell 15.5% on Oct. 14 as yields on its 2032 notes touched 15%, and its default-swap spreads nearly doubled in October. IREN is down more than 20% this year. Last Thursday, the contagion reached chipmakers, which makes sense since much of CRWV and IREN's spending is going there. AMD dropped 8.1% as Meta's financing plans and a supply warning from Lam Research exacerbated data-center fears about the pace of AI spending.

Because when you screen for factors that demonstrably generate outperformance over time, the list narrows quickly. My screen: price above the 200-day moving average; revenue growing at least as fast as the S&P 500 (5%+ per annum); EPS growing at least as fast (7%+); rating upgrades; a PEG below 3; and ROE and ROIC of at least 12%. Of the names reporting in the next two weeks, AMD is effectively the only one that makes the list. Yes, you can (and arguably should, as our staples article described) position your portfolio with slightly less tech exposure than the broad indices provide, but we can't ignore the market's biggest and most transformative sector entirely.

Especially because the growth in this case doesn't just meet my criteria; it blows past them. Consensus for Q3 calls for EPS of $1.94 on revenue of $13.06 billion, versus $1.20 and $9.25 billion a year ago. That's YoY growth of nearly 62% and 41%, respectively. The recent drawdown came from a sector selloff, not anything AMD reported, but it shows that if some names in the space get hit, even the larger players are likely to feel it. On Oct. 6, Lisa Su said AMD would substantially increase supply in 2027 because AI orders keep outrunning capacity.

So how do you balance factors we know work for a fast-growing company against a backdrop of cracks in the AI trade? Options.

Owning the stock outright means absorbing a roughly 9% to 11% implied earnings-related move (day of). Earnings are about a week out, and over the past four quarters the smallest move over a similar window was more than 9%, and the largest move, after the company reported its Q1 26 results, was 38%! Of course, that kind of volatility means options aren't cheap, and that rich premium is also a reason not to simply buy calls.

A call spread risk reversal does both jobs: it reduces risk if the cracks widen, and the short options offset the elevated volatility we would otherwise pay for. The bottom chart shows that, by sacrificing about $1,700 of upside for $5,000 in outperformance during a severe downside move, and given how jittery this trade has been lately, this is a way to stay in it with considerably less risk. $5,000 less, specifically. Of course, selling that out will tie up some cash, but less so than simply buying the stock. And selling both the out and the call reduces long call purchase by 66%
